Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 1–4:

Surat al-A'raf

Surat al-A'raf
Makkiyya (Meccan) entirely, except five verses, the first of which is "Ask them about the town that was by the sea" (7:163) [128/a]

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad.﴾

﴿A Book﴾ meaning: this is a Book, ﴿revealed to you﴾, and it is the Qur'an, ﴿so let there be no constriction in your breast because of it﴾. Mujahid said: "(Constriction means) doubt." So the address is to the Messenger ﷺ, and what is meant is the Ummah (community). Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Haraj (constriction) means narrowness; the meaning is: let your breast not be constricted by conveying and discharging what you were sent with." ﴿That you may warn thereby﴾, meaning: a Book revealed to you so that you may warn by it, ﴿and as a reminder for the believers﴾, meaning: an admonition for them. It is in the nominative case, being a continuation of (the word) "Book".

﴿Follow﴾, meaning: and say to them, "Follow ﴿what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾, meaning: do not take others than Him as protectors whom you obey in disobedience to Allah the Exalted, ﴿little do you remember﴾, meaning: you take heed." Ibn 'Amir recited "yatadhakkarun" with a ya' and a ta'.

﴿And how many a town have We destroyed﴾ with punishment. ﴿How many﴾ (kam) is for abundance, and "rubba" is for paucity. ﴿Our punishment came upon it﴾, meaning Our chastisement, ﴿by night﴾, ﴿or while they were taking a midday rest﴾. It is from al-qaylulah (the midday rest). Its implied sense: Our punishment came upon them by night while they were asleep, or by day while they were resting at midday, i.e. sleeping at noon. Al-qaylulah is resting at midday, even if it does not include sleep. The meaning of the verse: Our punishment came upon them while they did not expect it, either by night or by day. Al-Zajjaj said: "'Aw' (or) indicates the alternation of the punishment, once at night and once by day." It was also said: the meaning is that among the people of those towns were some whom We destroyed by night, and some whom We destroyed by day.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of "We destroyed it, and Our punishment came upon it"? How can the coming of punishment be after destruction? It is answered: the meaning of "We destroyed" is: We decreed its destruction, and then Our punishment came upon it. It was also said: "Our punishment came upon it" explains "We destroyed it", like the saying of one who says, "You gave me and so you did well to me," which has no difference from saying, "You did well to me and so you gave me," so one of them is a substitute for the other.

﴿فَمَا كَانَ دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ That is, their statement, their supplication, and their humble pleading. The word *da'wa* can mean a claim (*iddi'a'*) and can also mean supplication (*du'a'*). The final outcome of their affair was the acknowledgment of their wrongdoing at a time when acknowledgment would not benefit them.

﴿فَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الَّذِينَ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ meaning: the nations, about their response to the messengers. This is a question of reproach, not a question of seeking information. That is, We will ask them about what they did regarding what the messengers conveyed to them. ﴿وَلَنَسْأَلَنَّ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ about the conveying of the message.

﴿فَلَنَقُصَّنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِعِلْمٍ﴾ meaning: We will inform them with knowledge. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: the book of their deeds will speak against them, as in His saying: ﴿هَذَا كِتَابُنَا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ (al-Jathiyah, 29). ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا غَائِبِينَ﴾ from the messengers regarding what they conveyed, and from the nations regarding how they responded.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَالْوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ﴾ meaning: the Day of questioning. Mujahid said: its meaning is that the judgment on that Day is justice. Most scholars said: it refers to the weighing of deeds by the balance (*mizan*, scale). Allah Most High sets up a balance for Himself, which has a tongue and two pans, each pan as large as the distance between the East and the West.

They differed about how the weighing takes place. Some said: the pages of deeds are weighed. It has been narrated to us that a man will have ninety-nine registers unfolded before him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then a small card will be brought out for him, on which is written the testimony, "There is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger." The registers will be placed in one pan and the card in the other pan. The registers will rise up and the card will outweigh them.¹

It was also said: the persons themselves are weighed. It has been narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A large, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh as much as the wing of a mosquito in the sight of Allah."²

It was also said: the deeds are weighed. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Good deeds will be brought in a good form and bad deeds in an ugly form, and they will be placed in the balance. The wisdom behind weighing deeds is that Allah tests His servants with faith in this world, and establishes the proof against them in the Hereafter.

﴿فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ Mujahid said: its meaning is his good deeds. ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ meaning: "those are the successful."

Allah Most High sets up a balance for Himself, which has a tongue and two pans, each pan as large as the distance between the East and the West.

They differed about how the weighing takes place. Some said: the pages of deeds are weighed. It has been narrated to us that a man will have ninety-nine registers unfolded before him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then a small card will be brought out for him, on which is written the testimony, "There is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger." The registers will be placed in one pan and the card in the other pan. The registers will rise up and the card will outweigh them.¹

It was also said: the persons themselves are weighed. It has been narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A large, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh as much as the wing of a mosquito in the sight of Allah."²

It was also said: the deeds are weighed. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Good deeds will be brought in a good form and bad deeds in an ugly form, and they will be placed in the balance. The wisdom behind weighing deeds is that Allah tests His servants with faith in this world, and establishes the proof against them in the Hereafter.

﴿فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ Mujahid said: its meaning is his good deeds. ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ meaning: "those are the successful."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 9–12:**

﴿Whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls because they wronged Our signs.﴾ (They) denied (them).

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), when death came to him, said in his will to Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): "The scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are heavy only because of their following the truth in the world and its weight upon them. It is right that a scale in which the truth is placed tomorrow should be heavy. The scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection are light only because of their following falsehood in the world and its lightness upon them. It is right that a scale in which falsehood is placed tomorrow should be light."

If it is said: He said "whose scales" (mawazinuhu) in the plural, while the mizan (scale) is singular? It is said: its wording may be plural while its meaning is singular, as in His saying "O messengers" (al-Mu'minun 51). It was also said: every servant has a mizan. It was also said: the origin is one great mizan, and each servant has within it a mizan attached to him. It was also said that it is plural because the mizan comprises the two pans, the witnesses, and the tongue of the balance, and the weighing is not complete except by their combination.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And We have certainly established you on the earth﴾, meaning: We established you. The meaning of "establishment" (tamkin) is granting possession and capability. ﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, meaning: means by which you live during the days of your lives, from trades, earnings, food and drink. Ma'aayish (means of livelihood) is the plural of ma'ishah (livelihood). ﴿Little is it that you are grateful﴾ for what We have done for you.

His Mighty and Majestic saying: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We created you" means your origins and fathers, "then We fashioned you" means in the wombs of your mothers. Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "We created you" refers to Adam, and "We fashioned you" refers to his offspring. Mujahid said regarding "We created you": Adam; then "We fashioned you" in the loins of Adam, in the plural wording, because he is the father of mankind, so the creation of him is the creation of all who come forth from his loins. It was also said: "We created you" in the loins of Adam, then "We fashioned you" on the Day of the Covenant when He brought you forth like specks (al-dharr). 'Ikrimah said: "We created you" in the loins of men, then "We fashioned you" in the wombs of women. Yaman said: He created the human in the womb, then fashioned him, and split his hearing, his sight and his fingers. It was also said: all of it refers to Adam, whom He created and fashioned, and "thumma" (then) here means "wa" (and).

﴿Then We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam.﴾ If it is said: The command to the angels to prostrate was before the creation of the children of Adam, so what is the meaning of His saying "then We said" when "thumma" indicates sequence and delay? It is said: according to the view of one who directs the creation and fashioning to Adam alone, this statement is consistent. As for the view of one who directs it to the offspring, there are several answers regarding it:

One of them: "thumma" means "wa", i.e., "and We said to the angels", so it does not indicate sequence and succession.

It was also said: it means "thumma" (then) I inform you that We said to the angels: prostrate.

It was also said: there is inversion in it, its sense being: "And We had certainly created you," meaning Adam, "then We said to the angels: prostrate," "then We fashioned you."

His Exalted saying: ﴿So they prostrated﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated﴾ to Adam.

﴿He said﴾: Allah, Exalted, said: O Iblis, ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ meaning: What prevented you from prostrating? The "la" (not) here is extra, as in His saying: ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a city which We have destroyed that they will not return﴾ (al-Anbiya' 95) [128/b].

﴿He said﴾, Iblis replying: ﴿I am better than him﴾, because ﴿You created me from fire and created him from clay﴾, and fire is better than and more luminous than clay.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The first to apply qiyas (analogical reasoning) was Iblis, and he erred in the analogy. Whoever measures the religion by something of his own opinion, Allah will join him with Iblis."

Ibn Sirin said: "The sun was only worshipped through qiyas."

Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "The wicked one thought that fire was better than clay, and did not know that excellence belongs to the one to whom Allah grants excellence. Allah has preferred clay over fire in several respects, among them: the essence of clay is steadiness, dignity, forbearance and patience, and it was what drove Adam, after the felicity that preceded for him, to repentance, humility and supplication, so it bequeathed to him election, repentance and guidance. The essence of fire is lightness, hastiness, sharpness and elevation, and it was what drove Iblis, after the wretchedness that preceded for him, to arrogance and persistence, so it bequeathed to him the curse and wretchedness. Moreover, clay is the means of gathering things together, while fire is the means of their dispersal; and clay is the means of life, for the life of trees and plants is by it, while fire is the means of destruction."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 13–17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it."﴾ That is, from Paradise. It was also said: from the heaven to the earth. He had dominion over the earth, and He removed him from it to the islands of the sea, and his throne was in the Green Sea. So he does not enter the earth except in fear, in the manner of a thief, like an old man in worn-out clothes, startled at every step until he leaves it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant﴾ by disobeying the command, ﴿therein﴾ that is, in Paradise. So no arrogant one who disobeys the command of Allah should dwell in Paradise or in the heaven. ﴿So get out; indeed you are of the debased.﴾ That is, of the humiliated. Al-saghar (debasement) means abasement and disgrace.

﴿He said﴾ Iblis, at that moment, ﴿"Reprieve me"﴾ delay me and grant me respite, so do not cause me to die, ﴿"until the Day they are resurrected"﴾ from their graves, which is the final blast at the establishment of the Hour. The wicked one intended that he would not taste death.

﴿He said﴾ Allah, may He be exalted, ﴿"Indeed, you are of those reprieved"﴾ those given respite. He clarified the duration of the reprieve and the respite in another place, saying: ﴿"Until the Day of the appointed time"﴾ (Al-Hijr, 38). This is the first blast, when all creation dies.

His saying: ﴿"Because You have sent me astray"﴾ The scholars differed regarding "ma" (mā). It was said that it is interrogative, meaning: "By what did You send me astray?" Then he began, saying: ﴿"I will surely sit in wait for them"﴾. It was also said that "ma" is conditional, meaning: "Because You have sent me astray, I will surely lie in wait for them." It was also said that it is the verbal "ma" (mā maṣdariyya) in the place of an oath, its estimate being: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them," like His saying: ﴿"by what my Lord forgave me"﴾ (Yasin, 27), meaning: by the forgiveness of my Lord.

The meaning is: by Your power over me and the execution of Your authority over me. Ibn al-Anbari said: that is, by what You cast into my heart of error, which was the cause of my descent from the heaven. "Aghwaytani" means: You led me astray from guidance. It was also said: You destroyed me. It was also said: You frustrated me. ﴿"I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path"﴾ that is, I will surely sit for the children of Adam on Your upright path, which is Islam.

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "from before them" means from the direction of the Hereafter, so I will cast doubt in them about it. ﴿And from behind them﴾ I will make them desire their worldly life. ﴿And from their right﴾ I will confuse for them the matter of their religion.

﴿And from their left﴾ I will make sins appealing to them. Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿from before them﴾ from the direction of their worldly life, meaning I will adorn it in their hearts. ﴿And from behind them﴾ from the direction of the Hereafter, so I will say: there is no resurrection, no rising, no Paradise, no Fire. ﴿And from their right﴾ from the direction of their good deeds. ﴿And from their left﴾ from the direction of their evil deeds.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 18–21:**

﴿He said﴾: God Most High said to Iblis, ﴿Get out of it, disgraced and expelled.﴾ That is, blamed. The words *al-dhaym* (الذَّيْمُ) and *al-dha'm* (الذَّأْمُ) mean the most severe blame. It is said: *dha'amahu yadh'amuhu dha'man*, so he is *madhu'um* (مَذْءُومٌ), and *dhamahu yadhimuhu dhamman*, so he is *madhim* (مَذِيمٌ), like *sara yasiru sayran*. *Al-madhhur* (الْمَدْحُورُ) means the one who is removed and driven away. It is said: *dahara yadhharuhu dahran* when he removed him and drove him away. Ibn 'Abbas said: *madhu'man* means despised. Qatadah said: *madhu'man madhhuran* means cursed and banished. Al-Kalbi said: *madhu'man, madhhuran* means expelled from the Garden and from every good.

﴿Whoever follows you among them﴾, from the children of Adam, ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾. The *lam* here is *lam al-qasam* (لَامُ الْقَسَمِ), the particle of oath, ﴿with you all together﴾. That is: with you and your offspring and the disbelievers of the children of Adam, all together.

﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾. That is, to them. *Al-waswasah* (الْوَسْوَسَةُ) is speech that Satan casts into the heart of a human being. ﴿To reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾. That is, to expose to them what was covered and hidden from them of their nakedness. It was said: the *lam* here is *lam al-'aqibah* (لَامُ الْعَاقِبَةِ), the particle of consequence. Iblis did not whisper for this purpose, but its outcome for them was that, namely the exposure of their nakedness. This is like the saying of God Most High: "Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief" (al-Qasas, 8). Then He explained the whispering, saying: ﴿And he said﴾, meaning Iblis to Adam and Hawwa', ﴿Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels﴾. That is: lest you be, out of dislike that you should become two angels among the angels, knowing good and evil. ﴿Or lest you become of the immortals﴾, those who remain and do not die. As He said in another place: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" (Ta-Ha, 120).

﴿And he swore to them both: Indeed I am to you both of the sincere advisers﴾. That is, he swore and took an oath to them. Qatadah said: He swore to them by God until he deceived them, and the believer may be deceived by God. So he said: "I was created before you both, and I know more than you both, so follow me and I will guide you." Iblis was the first to swear falsely by God. When he swore, Adam thought that no one would swear falsely by God, so he was deceived by him.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verse 22:**

﴿So he led them on with deception.﴾ That is, he deceived them. It is said: "So-and-so kept leading someone on with deception (*yudalli li-fulan bi-ghurur*)," meaning he kept deceiving him and speaking to him with false embellishment of words.

It is also said: he brought them down (*hatthahuma*) from the station of obedience to the state of disobedience. *Tadalli* (descent) occurs only from a height to a lower place. *Tadliyah* is the lowering of a bucket into a well. It is said: "He lowered himself (*tadalla bi-nafsihi*) and lowered another (*dallā ghayrahu*)." Al-Azhari said: its origin is the thirsty man lowering a bucket into the well so that he may be watered with water, but he does not find the water, so he becomes one who is let down (*mudallan*) by deception. *Al-ghurur* is showing sincere counsel while concealing deceit.

﴿When they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: "When they ate from it." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "Before they had swallowed it, the punishment seized them." The punishment was that *badat* (became apparent) to them, *sau'atuhuma* (their private parts), meaning their awrah (parts that must be covered). Their clothing fell away from them, so that each of them saw the other's awrah that had been concealed, though they had not been able to see it before. Wahb said: "Their clothing was of light." Qatadah said: "It was a nail-like covering (*zufr*) that Allah had clothed them with. When they fell into sin, their private parts became apparent to them, and they felt shame." ﴿And they began﴾ (*wa tafiqa*): they set about and started ﴿to patch﴾ (*yakhsifani*): they mended, stuck together and joined ﴿over themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾, which were fig leaves, until it became like a garment.

Al-Zajjaj said: they would place one leaf over another leaf so as to cover their private parts. It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Adam was a tall man, as if he were a towering palm tree (*nakhlah sahuq*) [[That is, the tall palm tree that is excessively high, whose fruit is out of reach of the one who picks it.]], abundant in head hair. When he fell into the error, his private part became apparent to him, which he had not been seeing. So he set off fleeing through the Garden, and a tree of the trees of the Garden confronted him and held him back by his hair. He said to it, 'Release me!' It said, 'I will not release you.' So his Lord called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, my Lord, but I was ashamed before You.'" [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and as a mawquf (ending with a Companion): 12/352 and 354. Ibn Kathir said (2/207): "Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh have narrated it through several routes from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a marfu', but the mawquf is sounder in its chain." The soundness of the chain up to Ubayy (may Allah be pleased with him) does not mean the soundness of the report itself, since these unseen details have no established proof of their authenticity, and they are often taken from the People of the Book. And Allah knows best.]]

﴿And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and tell you that Satan is a clear enemy to you?"﴾ That is, eating from it. Meaning: clearly hostile.

Muhammad ibn Qays said: "His Lord called out to him: 'O Adam, did you eat from it when I had forbidden you?' He said: 'My Lord, Hawwa' fed me from it.' He said to Hawwa': 'Why did you feed him?' She said: 'The serpent commanded me.' He said to the serpent: 'Why did you command her?' It said: 'Iblis commanded me.' Then Allah, exalted is He, said: 'As for you, O Hawwa', you shall bleed as you made the tree bleed, and you will bleed every month. As for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs, and you will walk on your belly and your face, and whoever meets you will crush your head. As for you, O Iblis, you are cursed and rejected.'" [[The weakness of these narrations has been pointed out previously, and that they are derived from the Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narratives). The report of Muhammad ibn Qays was narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 1/530-531, 12/354, and in his History: 1/109.]]

﴿He said: "Therein you will live﴾, meaning you will live on the earth, ﴿and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth﴾, meaning: from the earth you will be brought out of your graves for the Resurrection.

Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i (al-Kisāʾī) recited ﴿tukhrajūna﴾ with a fatha on the tā' here and in al-Zukhruf. Yaʿqub agreed with them here, and Hamzah and al-Kisa'i added "wa-kadhalika tukhrajūna" (﴿and likewise you will be brought forth﴾) at the beginning of al-Rum. The rest recited it with a damma on the tā' and a fatha on the rā' in these places.

﴿O Children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you﴾, meaning: We created for you ﴿clothing﴾. It was said: He said "sent down" because clothing comes only from the produce of the earth, and produce grows from what descends from the sky. So the meaning of His words ﴿sent down﴾ is: We sent down its causes. It was also said: all the blessings of the earth are attributed to the blessings of the sky, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We sent down iron﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 25), while iron is extracted from the earth.

The occasion of the revelation of this verse (Asbab al-Nuzul, "occasions of revelation") was that in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam) they used to circumambulate the House naked, saying: "We will not circumambulate in garments in which we have disobeyed God." Men would circumambulate by day and women by night, naked.

Qatadah said: A woman would circumambulate, placing her hand over her private part, and say:
"Today it appears, all or part of it,
and what appears of it, I do not make lawful."

So God, glorified is He, commanded covering, and said: ﴿We have certainly sent down to you clothing that covers your private parts﴾ [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 259–260; Ibn Kathir: 2/209, 211.]], meaning it conceals your nakedness. Its singular is sawʾah, and it was so named because its exposure distresses its owner. So do not circumambulate naked. ﴿And as adornment (rīsh)﴾, meaning wealth, according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It is said: "tarayyasha al-rajul" when a man becomes wealthy. It was also said: al-rīsh means beauty, that is, the garments with which they adorn themselves. It was also said: it is clothing itself.

﴿And the clothing of God-consciousness, that is best﴾. The people of Madinah, Ibn ʿAmir and al-Kisa'i recited "wa-libāsa" with a fatha on the sīn, in coordination with His words ﴿libāsan﴾ (clothing). The others recited it with a damma, as the subject (al-ibtidāʾ, the nominative beginning of the sentence), with ﴿khayr﴾ (best) as its predicate, and they treated ﴿dhalika﴾ (that) as an additional element (ṣilah, a connecting particle) in the sentence. For this reason Ibn Masʿud and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recited ﴿wa-libāsu al-taqwā dhālika khayr﴾.

They differed concerning ﴿the clothing of God-consciousness﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the clothing of God-consciousness is faith (al-īmān). Al-Hasan said: it is modesty (al-ḥayāʾ), because it prompts one to God-consciousness.

ʿAṭiyyah related from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is righteous action. And from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, that he said: it is a good bearing (al-samt al-ḥasan).

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: the clothing of God-consciousness is fear of God. Al-Kalbi said: it is chastity (al-ʿafāf). The meaning is: the clothing of God-consciousness is better for its wearer when he adopts it, more than the clothing created for him for adornment.

Ibn al-Anbari said: the clothing of God-consciousness is the first clothing, and He repeated it only to inform that covering the private parts is better than being naked during circumambulation.

Zayd ibn ʿAli said: the clothing of God-consciousness is the equipment with which one protects oneself in war, such as the coat of mail, the helmet, the arm guards and the leg guards.

It was also said: the clothing of God-consciousness is wool and coarse garments worn by people of scrupulousness (ahl al-waraʿ).

﴿That is among the signs of God, that perhaps they will be reminded﴾.

ʿAṭiyyah related from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is righteous action. And from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, that he said: it is a good bearing (al-samt al-ḥasan).

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: the clothing of God-consciousness is fear of God. Al-Kalbi said: it is chastity (al-ʿafāf). The meaning is: the clothing of God-consciousness is better for its wearer when he adopts it, more than the clothing created for him for adornment.

Ibn al-Anbari said: the clothing of God-consciousness is the first clothing, and He repeated it only to inform that covering the private parts is better than being naked during circumambulation.

Zayd ibn ʿAli said: the clothing of God-consciousness is the equipment with which one protects oneself in war, such as the coat of mail, the helmet, the arm guards and the leg guards.

It was also said: the clothing of God-consciousness is wool and coarse garments worn by people of scrupulousness (ahl al-waraʿ).

﴿That is among the signs of God, that perhaps they will be reminded﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 27–29:

﴿O Children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you﴾, meaning: let not Satan lead you astray, ﴿as he removed your parents﴾, meaning: just as he tempted your parents Adam and Hawwa' (Eve) and caused them to be removed, ﴿from the Garden, stripping off from them their clothing to show them their private parts﴾, so that each of them would see the private parts of the other. ﴿Indeed, he sees you﴾, meaning: Satan sees you, O children of Adam, ﴿he and his soldiers (qabiluhu)﴾, meaning his troops. Ibn 'Abbas said: "his offspring (waladuhu)." Qatadah said: "his qabil are the jinn and the devils." ﴿from where you do not see them﴾. Malik ibn Dinar said: "Indeed, an enemy who sees you while you do not see him is extremely hostile and burdensome, except for the one whom Allah protects." ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies﴾, meaning companions and helpers, ﴿for those who do not believe﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "Their authority over them is that they increase them in their misguidance, as He says: ﴿Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?﴾" (Maryam, 83).

﴿And when they commit an indecency (fahisha)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: it is their circumambulating the House naked. 'Ata' said: "Shirk (polytheism) and fahisha is a term for every ugly act that reaches the extreme of ugliness."

﴿They say: We found our fathers upon it﴾. There is an implied element in this, meaning: "And when they commit an indecency and are forbidden from it, they say: We found our fathers upon it." It was said: "From where did your fathers take it?" They said: ﴿And Allah commanded us to it.﴾ Say: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?﴾

﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice (qist)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah)." Al-Dahhak said: "monotheism (tawhid)." Mujahid and al-Suddi said: "justice (al-'adl)."

﴿And set your faces (wujuhakum) toward every masjid﴾. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: meaning, direct your faces toward the Ka'bah during prayer, wherever you are. Al-Dahhak said: "When the prayer comes while you are at a masjid, pray in it, and let none of you say: 'I pray in my masjid.'" It was also said: the meaning is: make your prostration purely for Allah. ﴿And call upon Him﴾, meaning worship Him, ﴿being sincere to Him in religion﴾, meaning in obedience and worship, ﴿as He originated you, you will return.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah the Exalted originated the creation of the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers," as He says: ﴿He is the One who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ (al-Taghabun, 2). Then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He created them, believers and disbelievers. Mujahid said: "They will be resurrected upon what they died upon."

[129/a]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "They will return to His work concerning them." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "As He decreed for you, so you will be."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "Whoever Allah originates the creation of upon wretchedness will go to it, even if he does the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis used to do the deeds of the people of happiness and then went to wretchedness. And whoever Allah originates the creation of upon happiness will go to it, even if he does the deeds of the people of wretchedness, just as the magicians used to do the deeds of the people of wretchedness and then went to happiness."

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us: Abu Ghassan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa'd say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, a servant may act, in the eyes of people, with the deeds of the people of Paradise while he is actually of the people of the Fire; and indeed, a servant may act, in the eyes of people, with the deeds of the people of the Fire while he is actually of the people of Paradise. Indeed, deeds are only by their final outcomes."

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: "As He originated you and created you in this world when you were nothing, so you will return alive on the Day of Resurrection," as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ (al-Anbiya', 104). Qatadah said: "He originated them from dust and to dust they will return." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ (Ta-Ha, 55).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 30–32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A group He guided﴾, meaning God guided them, ﴿and a group deserved, upon them, error﴾, meaning: by His prior will. ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of God, and they think that they are guided﴾. In this is evidence that the disbeliever who thinks he is upon the truth in his religion, and the one who denies and the one who is stubbornly opposed, are equal.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾. The people of tafsir said: The Banu Amir used to circumambulate the House naked, so God, Exalted and Majestic, revealed: "O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer", meaning clothing. Mujahid said: that which covers your nakedness, even if it is a cloak.

Al-Kalbi said: The adornment is that which covers the nakedness at every place of prayer, for circumambulation or prayer.

﴿And eat and drink﴾. Al-Kalbi said: The Banu Amir, during the days of their pilgrimage, would not eat any food except sustenance, and would not eat fat, thereby glorifying their pilgrimage. The Muslims said: "We have more right to do that, O Messenger of God." So God, Exalted and Majestic, revealed: "And eat", meaning meat and fat, "and drink", meaning milk. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. (260).]] ﴿And do not be excessive﴾ by forbidding what God has permitted for you of meat and fat, ﴿indeed, He does not love the excessive﴾, those who do that. Ibn Abbas said: Eat whatever you wish and wear whatever you wish, as long as two things do not miss you: extravagance and arrogance. Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: God has gathered all of medicine in half a verse when He said: "Eat and drink, and do not be excessive."

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He brought forth for His servants﴾, meaning the wearing of clothing during circumambulation, ﴿and the good things of provision﴾, meaning meat and fat during the days of the pilgrimage.

And from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah: "and the good things of provision" refers to what the people of jahiliyyah forbade of the baha'ir and the sawa'ib.

﴿Say: They are, for those who believed, in the life of this world, purely [theirs] on the Day of Resurrection﴾. In this there is an ellipsis; its estimated reading is: they are for those who believed and for the polytheists in the life of this world, for the people of shirk share with the believers in the good things of this world, while in the Hereafter they are purely for the believers, with no share for the polytheists in them.

It was also said: they are purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection, free from disturbance and grief for the believers, for in this world they have them together with disturbance and grief.

Nafi' read ﴿khalisatun﴾ in the nominative, meaning: Say: they are for those who believed, shared in this world, and in the Hereafter they are purely, on the Day of Resurrection, for the believers. The others read it in the accusative as a circumstantial (qat') form. ﴿Thus We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 33–35:

﴿Say: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾. He means: circumambulating the House naked. "What is apparent" is the circumambulation of men by day, and "what is concealed" is the circumambulation of women by night. It was also said: it refers to fornication, secretly and openly.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: I said, "Did you hear this from Abdullah?" He said: "Yes." Then he raised it (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is more jealous than Allah, which is why He has forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And no one loves praise more than Allah, which is why He praised Himself." [Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-An'am, chapter "And do not approach indecencies": 8/296, and in Tawhid and in Nikah; and Muslim in Tawbah, chapter on Allah's jealousy and the prohibition of indecencies, no. (2760): 4/2113-2114.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And sin﴾, he means: wrongdoing and disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: it is the sin for which there is no prescribed punishment (hadd). Al-Hasan said: "sin" is wine. The poet said:

"I drank sin until my reason was lost...
Thus sin takes away the intellects."

﴿And transgression﴾: injustice and arrogance, ﴿without right﴾, ﴿and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾, meaning no proof or evidence, ﴿and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾, regarding the prohibition of tilth and livestock, according to the view of Muqatil. Others said: it is general, covering speaking about the religion without certainty.

﴿And for every nation is a term﴾: a period of time, and provision of food and drink. Ibn Abbas, Ata' and al-Hasan said: it means the appointed time for the descent of punishment upon them. ﴿So when their term comes﴾ and their provision ends, ﴿they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾, i.e., they cannot go ahead of it. This was when they asked for the punishment, so Allah revealed this verse.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O Children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you﴾, i.e., "if they come to you." It was said: He intended all the messengers.

Muqatil said: by His words "O Children of Adam" He meant the polytheists of the Arabs, and by "messengers" He meant Muhammad ﷺ alone. ﴿Reciting My verses to you﴾. "What is apparent" is the circumambulation of men by day, and "what is concealed" is the circumambulation of women by night. It was also said: it refers to fornication, secretly and openly.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: I said, "Did you hear this from Abdullah?" He said: "Yes." Then he raised it (to the Prophet), saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one is more jealous than Allah, which is why He has forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed. [Reported by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-An'am, chapter "And do not approach indecencies": 8/296, and in Tawhid and in Nikah; and Muslim in Tawbah, chapter on Allah's jealousy and the prohibition of indecencies, no. (2760): 4/2113-2114.]

Thus sin takes away the intellects."

They differed about this. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: it is what has been decreed for them of punishment and determined against them, such as blackened faces and blue eyes. Allah the Exalted said, ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah with their faces blackened﴾ (Az-Zumar, 60).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 38–40:

﴿He will say: "Enter among nations"﴾ meaning: Allah will say to them on the Day of Resurrection, "Enter among nations", that is, along with groups, ﴿who have passed away﴾, that is, departed, ﴿before you, of jinn and humankind, into the Fire﴾, meaning the disbelievers of the previous nations. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾, meaning its sister in religion, not in lineage. Thus the Jews curse the Jews, the Christians curse the Christians, and every group curses its sister, and the followers curse the leaders. He did not say "its brother" because He means the nation and the community. ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾, that is, they catch up with one another, follow one another and gather together in the Fire. ﴿The last of them will say about the first of them﴾. Muqatil said: meaning the last of them to enter the Fire, who are the followers, ﴿about the first of them﴾, that is, the first of them to enter, who are the leaders, because the leaders enter the Fire first. Ibn Abbas said: it means the last of each nation about its first. As-Suddi said: the people of the last era about the first of them who established that religion for them. ﴿Our Lord, these﴾ who ﴿misled us﴾ from guidance, meaning the leaders, ﴿so give them a double punishment from the Fire﴾, that is, double the punishment upon them. ﴿He will say﴾, Allah the Exalted, ﴿"For each is double"﴾, meaning for the leaders and the followers there is a double punishment, ﴿but you do not know﴾ what each group among you has of punishment.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read: "wa-lakin la ta'lamun" (but you do not know). Abu Bakr read "la ya'lamun" with the ya', that is: the followers do not know what the leaders have, nor do the leaders know what the followers have.

﴿The first of them will say to the last of them﴾, meaning the leaders to the followers, ﴿"You had no advantage over us"﴾, because you disbelieved just as we disbelieved; so we and you are equal in disbelief and equal in punishment, ﴿so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. It is read with the ta', Abu Amr read it lightened; with the ya', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i lightened it; and the rest read it with the ta' doubled. ﴿The gates of heaven﴾: for their supplications, nor for their deeds. Ibn Abbas said: for their spirits, because they are evil and are not raised up, rather they are cast down to Sijjin. The gates of heaven are only opened for the spirits of the believers, their supplications and their deeds. ﴿Nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾, that is, until the camel enters the hole of the needle; al-Khiyat and al-Makhit are the needle. What is meant is that they will never enter Paradise, because when a thing is attached to something impossible, this indicates the emphasis of the prohibition, as one says: "I will not do such-and-such until the raven turns white or the pitch turns white," meaning "I will never do it."

﴿Thus We recompense the criminals.﴾

In Ibn Abi Shaybah, through Rabahi from Ali, it is *muttasil* (with a connected chain)."]

Wrongs that they committed against one another in the world will be settled among them, until, when they have been purified and cleansed, they will be permitted to enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will know his abode in Paradise better than he knew his abode in the world." [Related by al-Bukhari in *al-Riqaq*, chapter "Retribution on the Day of Resurrection" (11/395), and in *al-Mazalim*; and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (15/196).]

Al-Suddi said concerning this verse: When the people of Paradise are led to Paradise, they find at its gate a tree, at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They drink from one of them, and whatever resentment was in their breasts is removed; this is the pure drink (*shara>b tahur*). They wash in the other, and the radiance of bliss flows over them; their hair will never become disheveled nor their clothes worn after that, forever. ["Ilā hadha" means: to this, that is, the path to Paradise.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: its meaning is: He guided us to a deed whose reward is this. ﴿And we would not have been guided﴾ — Ibn Amir recited "*ma kunna*" without the conjunctive waw — ﴿had Allah not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.﴾ This is the statement of the people of Paradise when they see with their own eyes what the messengers had promised them. ﴿And they will be called: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾ It is said: this call occurs when they see Paradise from a distance, and they are called: "This is Paradise." 

It is also said: this call occurs within Paradise itself.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Khatib informed us, from Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Khallal, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: A caller will call out: "Indeed, you will be healthy and never fall ill; you will live and never die; you will be young and never grow old; and you will enjoy bliss and never suffer distress." That is His saying: "And they will be called: 'This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.'" This is a *sahih* hadith related by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain, as a *marfu'* report (attributed to the Prophet). [Related by Muslim in *al-Jannah*, chapter "On the Permanence of the Bliss of the People of Paradise," no. 2837 (4/2182).]

It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is not one of you except that he has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the disbeliever, he will inherit the believer's dwelling in the Fire, and the believer will inherit the disbeliever's dwelling in Paradise." [Related by Ibn Abi Hatim. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/135).]

Wrongs that they committed against one another in the world will be settled among them, until, when they have been purified and cleansed, they will be permitted to enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will know his abode in Paradise better than he knew his abode in the world." [Related by al-Bukhari in *al-Riqaq*, chapter "Retribution on the Day of Resurrection" (11/395), and in *al-Mazalim*; and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (15/196).]

They drink from one of them, and whatever resentment was in their breasts is removed; this is the pure drink (*shara>b tahur*). They wash in the other, and the radiance of bliss flows over them; their hair will never become disheveled nor their clothes worn after that, forever. ["Ilā hadha" means: to this, that is, the path to Paradise.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: its meaning is: He guided us to a deed whose reward is this. ﴿And we would not have been guided﴾ — Ibn Amir recited "*ma kunna*" without the conjunctive waw — ﴿had Allah not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.﴾ This is the statement of the people of Paradise when they see with their own eyes what the messengers had promised them. ﴿And they will be called: "This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do."﴾ It is said: this call occurs when they see Paradise from a distance, and they are called: "This is Paradise." 

It is also said: this call occurs within Paradise itself.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Khatib informed us, from Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Harith, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Khallal, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: A caller will call out: "Indeed, you will be healthy and never fall ill; you will live and never die; you will be young and never grow old; and you will enjoy bliss and never suffer distress." That is His saying: "And they will be called: 'This is Paradise, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.'" This is a *sahih* hadith related by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with this chain, as a *marfu'* report (attributed to the Prophet). [Related by Muslim in *al-Jannah*, chapter "On the Permanence of the Bliss of the People of Paradise," no. 2837 (4/2182).]

As for the disbeliever, he will inherit the believer's dwelling in the Fire, and the believer will inherit the disbeliever's dwelling in Paradise." [Related by Ibn Abi Hatim. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/135).]

﴿For them there will be a bed of Hellfire beneath them, and above them coverings.﴾ That is, a bed (*mihad*) means a couch. ﴿Coverings (ghawashin)﴾ means blankets (*luhuf*). It is the plural of *ghashiyah*, meaning that which covers and envelops them. It refers to the Fire surrounding them from every side, as Allah says: "For them will be canopies of fire above them and canopies beneath them" (Az-Zumar, 16). ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity.﴾ That is, its ability, and that with which it is not distressed or constricted. ﴿They are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever.﴾

﴿And We will remove﴾ and extract ﴿whatever resentment (ghill) is in their breasts﴾, that is, deceit and enmity that existed between them in the world. Thus We make them brothers, ﴿upon thrones facing one another.﴾ None of them will envy another for anything that Allah has granted to some of them.

﴿Rivers flow beneath them.﴾ Al-Hasan narrated from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "By Allah, this verse was revealed about us, the People of Badr: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, as brothers upon thrones facing one another.﴾" [Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shaf* (p. 64): "Ibn Sa'd narrated it through Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father, and al-Tabari through Ma'mar from Qatadah from Ali; both are *munqati'* (with a broken chain). In Ibn Abi Shaybah, through Rabahi from Ali, it is *muttasil* (with a connected chain)."]

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 44–46:

God Most High says: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true."﴾ That is, the reward, ﴿in truth﴾, meaning in sincerity. ﴿"Have you found what your Lord promised you?"﴾ That is, the punishment, ﴿"in truth?" They will say, "Yes."﴾ Al-Kisa'i read the vowel of the ʿayn (in ﴿naʿam﴾) with a kasra wherever it occurs, while the others read it with a fatha; both are dialectal variants (lughatan). ﴿Then a caller will call out between them﴾, that is, a caller will proclaim, making both groups hear: ﴿"The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ The people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿAsim read "anna" with a light (unstressed) nun and "laʿnatu" in the nominative (raf'). The others read it with a stressed nun, and "laʿnata Allah" in the accusative (nasb). "The wrongdoers" means the disbelievers.

﴿Who turn (people) away from the way of God﴾, that is, they divert people, ﴿from the way of God﴾, the obedience of God, ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, that is, they seek it to be deviant and inclined, meaning they seek the way of God while deviating from the right course.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They pray to other than God, and they glorify what God has not glorified. The word ʿiwaj (crookedness), with a kasra on the ʿayn, is used of religion, affairs, and the earth, and of everything that is not upright; with a fatha it is used of everything that is upright, such as a wall, a spear, and similar things.

﴿And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.﴾

﴿And between them is a barrier﴾, meaning between the Garden and the Fire. It has also been said: between the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire there is a barrier, and it is the wall which God Most High mentioned in His saying: "So a wall will be set up between them with a gate" (al-Hadid 13).

God Most High says: ﴿And on the heights (al-A'raf) are men﴾. Al-A'raf is that wall which is between the Garden and the Fire. It is the plural of ʿurf, which is a name for an elevated place, and from it comes ʿurf al-dik (the comb of the rooster), because of its elevation above the rest of its body. Al-Suddi said: That wall was called al-A'raf because its occupants recognize (yaʿrifun) people.

They differed concerning the men whom God informed were on the A'raf. Hudhayfa and Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal. Their bad deeds fell short of bringing them into the Garden, and their good deeds did not carry them beyond the Fire. So they stopped there until God decides concerning them what He wills. Then He admits them into the Garden by the bounty of His mercy, and they are the last of the people to enter the Garden.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Tawba informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us: Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub al-Kisa'i informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us: Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khallal related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr said, narrating from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: People will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one, enters the Garden, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one, enters the Fire. Then he recited the saying of God Most High: "Then those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful; and those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost their souls" (al-A'raf 8–9). Then he said: Indeed the scale tips with the weight of a mustard seed, or it inclines. He said: And whoever's good deeds and bad deeds are equal, is among the companions of the A'raf, and they are made to stop upon the Sirat (bridge). Then they recognize the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. When they look toward the people of the Garden, they call out, "Peace be upon you," and when they turn their sight toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people." As for the people of good deeds, they are given a light by which they walk before them and on their right, and every servant is given a light on that day. When they reach the Sirat, God removes the light of every hypocrite man and woman. When the people of the Garden see what the hypocrites have encountered, they say, "Our Lord, complete for us our light."

As for the companions of the A'raf, the light is not removed from before them, but their bad deeds prevent them from proceeding. So hope remains in their hearts, since the light has not been removed from before them. At that point God says: "They have not entered it, while they hope (to enter)." The hope was the light that was before them (in their hearts). Then they will be admitted into the Garden, and they will be the last of the people of the Garden to enter.

Shurahbil ibn Saʿd said: The companions of the A'raf are a people who went out to fight in the way of God without the permission of their parents. It was also transmitted by Muqatil in his tafsir, traced back (marfuʿan, i.e., attributed to the Prophet ﷺ): They are men who fought in the way of God while disobedient to their parents, and they were killed. They were freed from the Fire by their being killed in the way of God, and they were held back from the Garden by their parents' disobedience. So they are the last to enter the Garden.

It is related from Mujahid that they are people with whom one of the two parents was pleased and not the other. They will be held back on the A'raf until God judges between the creation, and then they will enter the Garden.

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: They are those who died in the fatra (the interval between prophets) and did not change their religion.

It has also been said: They are the children of polytheists. Al-Hasan said: They are people of excellence among the believers who rose up upon the A'raf and look down over the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire together, observing the states of both groups.

God Most High says: ﴿They will recognize each by their mark﴾, that is, they recognize the people of the Garden by the whiteness of their faces and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces.

﴿And they will call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you."﴾ That is, when they see the people of the Garden, they say, "Peace be upon you." ﴿They have not entered it﴾, meaning the companions of the A'raf have not entered the Garden, ﴿but they hope (to enter)﴾ into it. Abu al-ʿAliya said: God placed that hope in them only as an honor to them. Al-Hasan said: The One who placed hope in their hearts will bring them to what they hope for.

It has also been said: They are the children of polytheists. Al-Hasan said: They are people of excellence among the believers who rose up upon the A'raf and look down over the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire together, observing the states of both groups.

God Most High says: ﴿They will recognize each by their mark﴾, that is, they recognize the people of the Garden by the whiteness of their faces and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces.

﴿And they will call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you."﴾ That is, when they see the people of the Garden, they say, "Peace be upon you." ﴿They have not entered it﴾, meaning the companions of the A'raf have not entered the Garden, ﴿but they hope (to enter)﴾ into it. Abu al-ʿAliya said: God placed that hope in them only as an honor to them. Al-Hasan said: The One who placed hope in their hearts will bring them to what they hope for.

When their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say: "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people." ﴿وَإِذَا صُرِفَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ تِلْقَاءَ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ﴾ They seek refuge in Allah (taʿawwadhū billāh), ﴿قَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ meaning: the disbelievers in the Fire.

﴿وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالًا﴾ "The companions of al-aʿrāf (the Heights) call out to men who were great ones among the people of the Fire in the world, ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ قَالُوا مَا أَغْنَى عَنْكُمْ جَمْعُكُمْ﴾ recognizing them by their marks. Then they look toward Paradise and see in it the poor and the weak whom they used to mock, such as Salman, Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal and their likes. **Qur'an 7:50–53**

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of the Garden: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided for you."﴾ That is, pour (ṣabbū) upon us, from the water, or from what Allah has provided you. That is, be generous to us with what Allah has provided you of the food of the Garden.

ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: When the people of the heights (aṣḥāb al-aʿrāf) entered the Garden, the people of the Fire longed for relief and said: "O Lord, we have relatives among the people of the Garden. Permit us to see them and speak with them, so that they may look upon their relatives in the Garden and the bliss they are in, and recognize them." But the people of the Garden did not recognize them because of the blackness of their faces. So the companions of the Fire called out to the companions of the Garden by their names, and informed them of their relatives, saying: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided you." ﴿They replied: "Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers."﴾ That is, the water and the food.

﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾: this refers to what Satan had adorned for them of forbidding the baḥīra (a she-camel whose ear was slit and set free) and its kind, and of the whistling (mukāʾ) and clapping (taṣdiyah) around the House, and all the other blameworthy practices which they used to perform in the Jāhiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam). It is also said that "their religion" means "their festival." ﴿And the life of this world deceived them. So today We will forget them﴾, that is, We will leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾, that is, as they abandoned working for the meeting of this their Day, ﴿and they used to deny Our signs.﴾

﴿And indeed We brought them a Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿which We have detailed﴾, that is, made clear, ﴿with knowledge﴾ from Us of what sets them right, ﴿a guidance and a mercy﴾, that is, We made the Qur'an a guide and a source of mercy, ﴿for a people who believe.﴾ 130/b

﴿Do they await﴾, that is, do they wait for ﴿except its ta'wīl (its final outcome or fulfilment)?﴾ Mujāhid said: its recompense. al-Suddī said: its consequence. The meaning is: do they await anything except what their affair will come to, namely the punishment, and their destination, which is the Fire?

﴿On the day its ta'wīl comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth."﴾ That is, its recompense and what their affair will come to. They acknowledged it when acknowledgement no longer benefits them. ﴿So do we have any intercessors now, who might intercede for us? Or could we be sent back﴾ to the world, ﴿so that we might do other than what we used to do?﴾ ﴿They have lost their souls﴾, that is, they destroyed them through the punishment, ﴿and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them.﴾ [wa-baṭala] [[Omitted in manuscript "b".]]

**[Commentary on Qur'an 7:54]**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. He meant: in the measure of six days, because a day is from the rising of the sun until its setting. There was then no day, no sun, and no sky. It is said: six days like the days of the Hereafter, and each day like a thousand years. It is also said: like the days of this world. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Allah, mighty and majestic, was able to create the heavens and the earth in a glance and an instant, but He created them in six days [as a lesson]¹ to His creation in deliberation and patience in affairs. A hadith has come: "Deliberation is from Allah and haste is from Satan."² 

﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴾. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: "istaqarra" (He settled). Abu 'Ubayda said: "ṣa'ada" (He ascended). The Mu'tazila interpreted "istiwa'" (establishing) as "istila'" (dominion). As for the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna), they say: the establishment above the Throne is an attribute of Allah, Exalted is He, without how (bi-la kayf). It is obligatory for a person to believe in it, and he leaves the knowledge of it to Allah, mighty and majestic. A man asked Malik ibn Anas about His saying: (The Most Merciful established Himself upon the Throne) [Ta-Ha: 5], "How did He establish Himself?" He lowered his head for a long time, and sweat came over him. Then he said: "The establishment is not unknown, the how is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, asking about it is an innovation, and I do not think you are but a misguided man." Then he ordered that he be taken out.

It is narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and others of the scholars of the Sunna, concerning these verses which came regarding the ambiguous attributes (al-sifat al-mutashabiha): they let them pass as they came, without how.

"Al-'Arsh" in language means the couch (al-sarir). It is said: it is what is elevated and shades, and from it comes "'arsh al-kurum" (the trellis of the vines). It is also said: al-'Arsh means kingship (al-mulk).

﴿He covers the night over the day﴾. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub recited "yughashshi" with the intensive form here and in Surat al-Ra'd, while the rest recited it with the light form (yughshi). The meaning is: the night comes upon the day and covers it. There is an ellipsis, meaning: and the day covers the night; He did not mention it because the context indicates it. In another verse He mentioned it, saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. ﴿Seeking it rapidly﴾, meaning: swiftly. That is because each of them follows the other and succeeds it, as if one is pursuing the other.

﴿And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited all of them in the nominative (marfu'), as a subject and predicate, while the rest recited them in the accusative (mansub). Likewise in Surat al-Nahl, as a conjunction upon His saying "created the heavens and the earth." That is: He created these things subjected, meaning: made subservient ﴿by His command﴾. ﴿Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command﴾. His is the creation because He created them, and His is the command: He commands in His creation whatever He wills. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: Allah distinguished between the creation and the command, so whoever joins between them has disbelieved.

﴿Blessed is Allah﴾, meaning: Allah is exalted and magnified. It is said: He is elevated. The word "mubarak" means the elevated. It is also said: "tabaraka" is of the form "tafa'ala" from "barakah," which is growth and increase; that is, blessing is acquired and attained by remembering Him. 

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He brings every blessing." Al-Hasan said: blessing comes from Him. It is also said: "tabaraka" means "taqaddasa" (He is sanctified), and "al-quds" is purity. It is said: "Tabaraka Allah" means: by His name blessing is sought in everything. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 55–56:

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾. "Humbly" (tadarru') means with submission and lowliness; "secretly" (khufyah) means privately.

Al-Hasan said: "The difference between a secret supplication and a public supplication is seventy-fold. The Muslims would strive in supplication while no voice of theirs was heard; it was nothing but a whisper between them and their Lord. This is because Allah, glory be to Him, says: 'Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly.' And Allah mentioned a righteous servant and approved of his action, saying: 'When he called upon his Lord with a secret call' [Maryam: 3]."

﴿Indeed, He does not like the transgressors﴾. It was said: the transgressors in supplication. Abu Mijlaz said: they are those who ask for the ranks of the Prophets, peace be upon them.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Fashani informed us, al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Lu'lu'i informed us, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salamah, informed us, Sa'id al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu Na'amah, that Abdullah ibn Mughaffal heard his son say: "O Allah, I ask You for the white palace on the right of Paradise when I enter it." He said: "My son, ask Allah for Paradise and seek refuge from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There will come among this Ummah people who will transgress in purification and supplication.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Taharah, chapter on extravagance in water: 1/87; and Ibn Majah in Du'a, chapter on the disapproval of transgression in supplication, no. (3864), with the wording: "There will come people who transgress in supplication...": 2/1271. Al-Hakim authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed: 1/504. Ibn Hibban, no. (171), pp. (70-71) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/172, 183 from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and 4/86, 87, 5/55 from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir: 2/222-223 and said: "It is a good chain, with no problem."]]

It was also said: he meant transgression by loudness and shouting [and screaming]. [Omitted from manuscript "B".] Ibn Juraij said: among transgression is raising the voice, calling out and shouting in supplication.

We have also related from Abu Musa, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) campaigned against Khaybar, the people overlooked a valley and raised their voices with takbir. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; you are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and near." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on the battle of Khaybar: 7/470, and in al-Da'awat, al-Tawhid and al-Jihad. Muslim narrated it in al-Dhikr, al-Du'a, al-Tawbah and al-Istighfar, chapter on lowering the voice in remembrance, no. (2704): 4/2076; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/66.]] Atiyyah said: they are those who invoke curses upon the believers in what is not permissible, saying: "O Allah, disgrace them; O Allah, curse them."

﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾. That is: do not cause corruption in it through sins and through calling to other than the obedience of Allah, after Allah has reformed it by sending the Messengers and clarifying the Law, and by calling to the obedience of Allah. This is the meaning of the statements of al-Hasan, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi.

Atiyyah said: "Do not disobey on the earth, lest Allah withhold the rain and destroy the crops because of your sins." Accordingly, the meaning of His words "after its reformation" is: after Allah has reformed it with rain and fertility.

﴿And call upon Him in fear and hope﴾. That is: in fear of Him and of His punishment, and in hope for what He has of forgiveness and reward. Ibn Juraij said: the fear of justice and the hope of grace.

﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾. He did not say "qaribah" (near, feminine). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Mercy" here means reward, so the adjective agreed with the meaning rather than the wording, as in His saying: "And when the division takes place, if relatives, orphans and the needy are present, provide for them from it" [al-Nisa': 8], where He did not say "from them", because He meant inheritance and wealth.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Qarib" and "ba'id" are used alike in the language for the masculine and feminine, and the singular and plural. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said: "Qarib" in the language may mean nearness of kinship and nearness of distance. The Arabs say: "This is a woman who is qaribah to you" when it means kinship, and "qarib minka" when it means distance.

The Almighty said: ﴿It is He who sends the winds as glad tidings﴾. ʿĀṣim recited "bushran" (بُشْرًا) with a *bāʾ*, with a *ḍamma* on it and a sukūn on the *shīn*, here and in al-Furqan and surah al-Naml. The meaning is that they bring glad tidings of rain, as evidenced by the Almighty's words: "the winds as bearers of glad tidings" (al-Rum 46). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī recited "nashran" (نَشَرًا) with an *nūn*, and with a *fatḥa* on it, and it refers to the pleasant, gentle wind. The Almighty said: [The words in these brackets are omitted from "b".] "And those that scatter in scattering" (al-Mursalat 3). Ibn ʿĀmir recited with a *ḍamma* on the *nūn* and a sukūn on the *shīn*. The others recited with a *ḍamma* on both the *nūn* and the *shīn*, as the plural of *nushūr*, like *ṣabūr* and *ṣabr*, and *rasūl* and *rusul*, meaning scattered; these are the winds that blow from every direction. ﴿Before His mercy﴾, that is, before the rain.

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Muḥammad al-Khaṭīb informed us: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad al-Khallāl informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbās al-Aṣamm informed us: al-Rabīʿ informed us: al-Shāfiʿī informed us: a trustworthy narrator (al-thiqah) related from al-Zuhrī, from Thābit ibn Qays, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A wind struck the people on the road to Makkah while ʿUmar was on pilgrimage, and it grew strong. ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to those around him: "What has reached you concerning the wind?" They did not give him any answer. Then news reached me of what ʿUmar had asked about concerning the wind, so I urged my mount until I caught up with ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), and I was at the back of the people. I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have been informed that you asked about the wind, and I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The wind is from the Spirit of Allah; it comes with mercy and with punishment, so do not revile it, but ask Allah for its good and seek refuge in Him from its evil.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 264; Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on what to say when the wind rages, 8/4, and the wording is his; Ibn Majah in al-Adab, chapter on the prohibition of reviling the wind, 2/1228; al-Shafiʿi in al-Musnad, 1/175-176; al-Nasaʾi in ʿAmal al-Yawm wal-Laylah, p. 520; al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar, 1/399; al-Bayhaqi in al-Daʿawat al-Kabir (see Mishkat al-Masabih, 1/480); Ibn Ḥibbān authenticated it, p. 488 of al-Mawarid; al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak, 4/285; Imam Aḥmad in al-Musnad, 2/268; the author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 4/391, and its isnad is ṣaḥīḥ (sound).] ʿAbd al-Razzāq related it from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, with its isnad. [See al-Musannaf of Imam ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 11/89.]

﴿Until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾, the winds have carried heavy clouds laden with rain, ﴿We drive them﴾; the pronoun refers back to the clouds, ﴿to a dead land﴾, that is, to a dead land in need of water. It was also said: the meaning is to bring life to a dead land with no vegetation in it. ﴿Then We send down therewith﴾, that is, with the clouds. It was also said: into that dead land ﴿water﴾, meaning rain, ﴿and We bring forth with it fruits of every kind. Thus We bring forth the dead﴾. He used the revival of the earth after its death as evidence for the revival of the dead. ﴿That you may remember﴾. Abu Hurayrah and Ibn ʿAbbās said: when all people die at the first blast, Allah will send upon them a rain like the semen of men, from water beneath the Throne called the water of life, and they will sprout in their graves like the growth of crops. When their bodies are complete, He will breathe the spirit into them, then cast sleep upon them, so they sleep in their graves. Then they will be raised at the second blast, and they will find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes. At that they will say: ﴿"Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?"﴾ (Ya Sin 52).

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And the good land—its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾. This is a parable which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, struck for the believer and the disbeliever. Abu Jaʿfar recited "nakidan" (نَكِدًا) with a *fatḥa* on the *kāf*, and the others recited it with a *kasra*, meaning with little difficulty, with toil and hardship.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlaʾ informed us: Hammad ibn Usamah informed us, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain that fell upon a land. Part of it was good ground that absorbed the water and produced grass and abundant herbage. Part of it was hard ground that held the water, so Allah benefited people by it: they drank, gave drink, and cultivated. And another part of it was barren plain that holds no water and produces no herbage. That is the likeness of one who gains understanding in the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah has sent me with, so he knows and teaches; and the likeness of one who does not lift his head to it and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I have been sent." The Qur'anic phrase is: ﴿We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾. He is Nuh ibn Lamak ibn Mutushalakh ibn Akhnukh, and he is Idris. He was the first prophet sent after Idris. He was a carpenter (najjar), and God sent him to his people when he was fifty years old. Ibn 'Abbas said he was forty. It was also said that he was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old. [[In "B": "one hundred and fifty years old."]] Muqatil said he was one hundred. Ibn 'Abbas said: he was named Nuh because of how much he wailed (naha) over himself.

They differed about the reason for his wailing. Some said it was because of his supplication against his people for their destruction. It was also said that it was because of his dispute with his Lord concerning his son Kan'an. It was also said that he passed by a mangy dog and said: "Begone, you ugly thing!" Then God, exalted is He, revealed to him: "Did you find fault with Me, or with the dog?"

﴿He said to his people: "O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him."﴾ Abu Ja'far and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ghayrihi﴾ (with a kasra on the ra' wherever it occurs), as an attribute of "god" (ilah). Hamzah agreed with them on the verse in Surat Fatir: "Is there any creator other than God?" [Fatir: 3]. The others read it with a damma on the ra' as a fronting (taqdim), its meaning being: "you have no god other than Him."

﴿Indeed I fear for you﴾, if you do not believe, ﴿the punishment of a great day.﴾

﴿The chiefs of his people said: "Indeed we see you in clear error,"﴾ meaning mistake and departure from the truth, ﴿clear﴾, meaning evident.

﴿He said: "O my people, there is no error in me,"﴾ and he did not say "laysat" (feminine), because the meaning of "dalalah" (error) is "dalal"; or it is on the fronting of the verb. ﴿"But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.﴾
