When the people woke, they wrapped themselves in shrouds, applied perfume, and threw themselves to the ground, turning their eyes to the sky once and to the earth once, not knowing from where the punishment would come to them. When the forenoon of Sunday grew intense, a shout came to them from the sky, containing the sound of every thunderbolt and the voice of everything on earth that has a voice. It tore their hearts within their breasts, and none of them, small or great, remained except that he perished, just as God Most High said: ﴿So they were found lying prostrate in their homes﴾. Except for one paralysed girl called Dhari'ah daughter of Salif, who was an unbeliever and extremely hostile to Salih. God released her legs after she had witnessed the punishment, and she came out faster than anything has ever been seen to move, until she reached Qazah, which is the valley of the villages. She informed them of what she had witnessed of the punishment and what had befallen Thamud. Then she asked for water and was given to drink, and when she drank, she died.

Al-Suddi mentioned another account regarding the hamstringing of the she-camel. He said: God Most High revealed to Salih, peace be upon him, that his people would hamstring his she-camel. He told them this, and they said: "We would never do that." Salih said: "A boy will be born in this month of yours who will hamstring her, and your destruction will be at his hands." They said: "No child will be born to us in this month except that we will kill him." He said: "Nine of them had children born in that month, and they slaughtered their sons. Then a child was born to the tenth, but he refused to slaughter his son, though he had not had a child before that, and his son was blue-eyed and red-complexioned, and grew up quickly. Whenever he passed by the nine and they saw him, they said: 'If our sons were alive, they would have been like this.' So the nine were angry with Salih because he was the cause of the killing of their children. They swore by God: 'We will ambush him and his family.' They said: 'We will go out so that people see that we have gone out on a journey, then we will come to the cave and remain in it, until when night falls and Salih goes out to his mosque, we will come to him and kill him. Then we will return to the cave and stay in it, then we will return to our dwellings and say: We did not witness the destruction of his people, and we are truthful, and they will believe us, thinking that we had set out on a journey.'" Salih did not sleep with them in the village, and he would spend the night in a mosque called the Mosque of Salih. When he woke in the morning, he would come to them and admonish and remind them, and when evening came, he would go out to the mosque and spend the night there. So they set out and entered the cave, and the cave collapsed upon them and killed them. Then some men who had found out about this went out and found them crushed. They returned shouting in the village: "O servants of God, Salih was not satisfied with ordering them to kill their children, so he killed them himself!" The people of the village then united in hamstringing the she-camel.

Ibn Ishaq said: The nine's plot to ambush Salih came after their hamstringing of the she-camel, as we have mentioned.

Al-Suddi and others said: When the son of the tenth was born, namely Qidar, he grew in one day as much as others grew in a week, and in a month as much as others grew in a year. When he became an adult, he sat with some people who were drinking alcohol, and they wanted water to mix with their drink. That day was the she-camel's turn to drink, and they found that the water had been drunk by the she-camel. This upset them greatly, and they said: "What are we to do with milk? If we took this water that the she-camel drinks and gave it to our livestock and our crops, it would be better for us." Ibn al-'Ashir said: "Shall I hamstring her for you?" They said: "Yes," so they hamstrung her.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Yahya ibn Hassan ibn Hayyan Abu Zakariyya, from Sulayman, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar: that when the Messenger of God ﷺ alighted at al-Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he ordered them not to drink from a well there nor to draw water from it. They said: "We have kneaded dough with it and drawn water." So he ordered them to throw away that dough and pour out that water. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter on the words of God Most High: "And to Thamud, their brother Salih": 6/378, and by Muslim in al-Zuhd, chapter "Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves," no. (2981): 4/2286, with a similar wording.]

Nafi' said from Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered them to pour out what they had drawn from its wells, to feed the camels the dough, and ordered them to draw water from the well which the she-camel used to come to. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter on the words of God Most High: "And to Thamud, their brother Salih": 6/378.]

Abu al-Zubayr related from Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ passed by al-Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he said to his companions: "None of you should enter the village, nor drink from its water, nor enter upon these punished people, unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you." Then he said: "As for what follows, do not ask your Messenger for signs. These are the people of Salih, who asked their Messenger, so God sent the she-camel. She used to come from this mountain pass and depart from this mountain pass, and drink their water on the day of her coming. He showed them the place where the young camel ascended from the rock, but they defied the command of their Lord and hamstrung her. So God Most High destroyed everyone under the canopy of the sky among them, in the east and west of the earth, except one man called Abu Righal, who was the father of Thaqif. He was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. But when he came out, what had befallen his people befell him, and he was buried, and a golden branch was buried with him. He showed them the grave of Abu Righal, so the people descended and rushed with their swords, dug around it and extracted that branch." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/230 (Halabi edition), and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad in abridged form: 3/296; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/340-341, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Haythami attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bazzar and Ahmad, and said: the narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to Ibn Hibban. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/37-38, al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 65, al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/492.]

The believing group from the people of Salih numbered four thousand. Salih led them out to Hadramawt, and when they entered it, Salih died, so it was named Hadramawt (meaning: Salih has died). Then the four thousand built a city called Hasura'. Some people of knowledge said: He died in Mecca at the age of fifty-eight, and he remained among his people for twenty years.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 76–79 (part 1 of 2):

﴿The arrogant among his people said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you believe."﴾ That is, they denied it.

﴿Then they hamstrung the she-camel﴾. Al-Azhari (al-Azhari) said: *al-'aqr* is cutting the hamstring (*'urqub*) of a camel. Then slaughtering (*al-nahr*) was called *'aqr*, because the one who slaughters a camel hamstrings it first and then slaughters it. ﴿And they transgressed against the command of their Lord﴾. *Al-'utuw* is excess in falsehood. It is said: "'Ata, ya'tu, 'utuwwan," meaning they became arrogant. The meaning is: they disobeyed God, abandoned His command concerning the she-camel, and denied their prophet.

﴿And they said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers."﴾ That is, the punishment.

﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, which is the shaking and quaking of the earth. They were destroyed by the Cry (*al-sayha*) and the quake (*al-raj'fa*). ﴿So they became motionless in their homes﴾. It is said: he meant the dwellings (*al-diyar*). It is also said: he meant in their land and their town, and that is why he used the singular *al-dar*. ﴿Prostrate﴾, meaning lifeless and dead. It is said: they fell on their faces, dead, every one of them.

﴿So he turned away from them﴾, that is, Salih turned away from them, ﴿and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisers."﴾ If it is asked: how did he address them with his words, "I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you," after they had been destroyed by the quake?

It is said: just as the Prophet ﷺ addressed the disbelievers among the dead of Badr when he cast them into the well. He began calling them by their names and their fathers' names: "Does it please you that you had obeyed God and His Messenger? Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?" Then 'Umar said: "O Messenger of God, how can you speak to bodies that have no spirits?" The Prophet ﷺ said: ["By He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad"] [[Addition from "B" and from Sahih al-Bukhari.]] "You are no better at hearing what I say than they are, but they cannot answer." [[A portion of a hadith from Anas ibn Malik, narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Campaigns (al-Maghazi), chapter "The killing of Abu Jahl": 7/300–301. He also narrated in the same place from Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet ﷺ stood at the well of Badr and said: "Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" Then he said: "Indeed, they now hear what I say." This was mentioned to 'A'isha, who said: The Prophet ﷺ only said: "They now know that what I used to tell them is the truth." Then she recited: "Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear" until she finished the verse. This was among what the Mother of the Believers 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, corrected in Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, claiming that he erred in saying "they hear," when the correct wording is "they know." Al-Bayhaqi said: knowledge does not preclude hearing. The answer concerning the verse is that He does not make them hear while they are dead; rather, God revived them so that they heard, as Qatada said. Neither 'Umar nor his son, may God be pleased with them both, were alone in relating this; Abu Talha agreed with them. Al-Tabarani has a similar report from Ibn Mas'ud with a sound chain, and one from 'Abd Allah ibn Sidan similar to it, in which: "They said, 'O Messenger of God, do they hear?' He said: 'They hear as you hear, but they do not answer.'" In the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: "But today they do not answer." It is strange that in Ibn Ishaq's Maghazi there is a report through Yunus ibn Bukayr with a good chain from 'A'isha similar to the hadith of Abu Talha, in which: "You are no better at hearing what I say than they are." Ahmad also narrated it with a good chain. If it is preserved, then it seems she retracted her denial because of what was established for her through the reports of these Companions, since she had not witnessed the event. For detailed study, see: Fath al-Bari 7/303–304; al-Ijaba li-Iradi ma Istadrakathu 'A'isha 'ala al-Sahaba by al-Zarkashi, pp. 99–100; al-Raw al-Anf by al-Suhayli 2/74.]] .

It is also said: he addressed them so that it would be a lesson for those who came after them.

It is also said: the verse contains an inversion of order, its meaning being: "So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord,' and then the earthquake seized them."

The story of Thamud, as related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Wahb, and others, is that when 'Ad was destroyed and their affair ended, Thamud lived on after them. They were made successors in the land, settled in it, multiplied, and lived long, until one of them would build a house of clay, and it would collapse while he was still alive. When they saw this, they carved houses out of the mountains. They were comfortable in their livelihood, but they acted corruptly and spread corruption in the land, and they worshipped other than God. So God sent to them Salih, and they were an Arab people. Salih was among the most central of them in lineage, the best of them in noble descent and position. God sent him to them while he was a young man. He called them to God until his hair turned grey and he grew old, and only a few weak people followed him. When Salih persisted with them in calling and delivering the message, and gave them many warnings and threats, they asked him to show them a sign that would confirm what he said. He said to them: "What sign do you want?" They said: "Come out with us tomorrow to our festival." They had a festival on a known day of the year when they went out with their idols. "You call on your God and we will call on our gods. If yours is answered, we will follow you, and if ours is answered, you will follow us." Salih said to them: "Yes." So they went out with their idols to their festival, and Salih went out with them. They called on their idols and asked them that no prayer of Salih be answered. Then Jundu' ibn 'Amr ibn Hawwas, who was then the chief of Thamud, said: "O Salih, bring forth for us from this rock, a solitary rock in a corner of al-Hijr called al-Katiba, a she-camel that is pregnant, hollow-bellied, hairy, and in her tenth month." (*Al-mukhtarijah* is what resembles the Bactrian camel.) "If you do this, we will believe you and have faith in you." So Salih took from them their solemn covenant that if he did it, they would believe him and have faith in him. They said: "Yes." So Salih prayed two units of prayer and called upon his Lord, and the rock began to heave like a woman in labour giving birth. Then the rock moved and split open, and out came a pregnant she-camel, hollow-bellied and hairy, just as they had described, and no one knew what was between her sides of bone except God, while they watched. Then she gave birth to a young one like her in size. Jundu' ibn 'Amr and a group of his people believed in him. The nobles of Thamud wished to believe and affirm him, but Dhu'ab ibn 'Amr ibn Labid, al-Hubab (the keeper of their idols), and Rabab ibn Sam'ar, who was their soothsayer, forbade them. They were among the nobles of Thamud.

When the she-camel came out, Salih said to them: "This is the she-camel of God. She has a turn to drink, and you have a turn on a known day." So the she-camel stayed, along with her drinking share, in the land of Thamud, grazing on the trees and drinking water. She used to come to the water on alternate days. On her day, she would put her head into a well in al-Hijr called the Well of the She-Camel, and she would not raise her head until she had drunk every drop of water in it, leaving none. Then she would raise her head and stretch herself out wide so that they could milk her, and they would drink what they wanted of her milk and store it, until they had filled all their containers. Then she would leave by a path other than the one by which she had come, for she could not depart from where she had come because it was too narrow for her. On the next day it was their day, and they would drink what water they wanted and store what they wished for the she-camel's day. Thus they lived in ease and comfort. When the heat was at the top of the valley, the she-camel would summer there, and their livestock, sheep, cattle, and camels, would flee from her, descending to the bottom of the valley in its heat and dryness. In winter she would winter in the bottom of the valley, and their livestock would flee to the top of the valley in the cold and barrenness. That harmed their livestock, as a trial and a test. This weighed heavily on them, so they transgressed against the command of their Lord, and this drove them to hamstring the she-camel. They agreed together to hamstring her.

There were two women of Thamud. One of them was called 'Unayza, daughter of Ghanm ibn Mijlaz, known by the kunya Umm Ghanm; she was the wife of Dhu'ab ibn 'Amr. She was an old, aged woman, who had beautiful daughters and wealth in camels, cattle, and sheep. The other woman was called Sudu, daughter of al-Mahya, who was beautiful, wealthy, and had many livestock. Both of them were among the people most hostile to Salih. Both loved the hamstringing of the she-camel, because she had harmed their livestock. So they schemed to hamstring the she-camel. Sudu summoned a man of Thamud called al-Hubab to hamstring the she-camel, and offered herself to him if he did it, but he refused her. So she summoned a cousin of hers called Mus'da' ibn Muhraj ibn al-Mahya, and promised herself to him on condition that he hamstring the she-camel. He was one of the most handsome and wealthiest of people, and he agreed to that. 'Unayza, daughter of Ghanm, summoned Qidar ibn Salif. He was a short, red-faced, blue-eyed man. They claimed he was the child of an adulteress, though he was not Salif's son, but he was born on Salif's bed. She said: "I will give you whichever of my daughters you wish, on condition that you hamstring the she-camel." Qidar was powerful and unassailable among his people.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Wuhayb informed us: Hisham informed us, from his father, that 'Abd Allah ibn Zam'a informed him that he heard the Prophet ﷺ giving a sermon, and he mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: (﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ [al-Shams: 12]). A mighty, violent, unassailable man among his people was sent forth for her, like Abu Zam'a. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary on the surah "By the sun and its brightness": 8/705, and in the Book of Marriage; by Muslim in the Book of Paradise and Its Bliss and Its People, chapter "The Fire Which the Tyrants Enter," no. (2855): 4/2191; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/182.]] .

Returning to the story: they said: Qidar ibn Salif and Mus'da' ibn Muhraj set out and incited the wicked people of Thamud, and seven men followed them, so they were nine men. Qidar, Sada'a, and their companions went out and watched for the she-camel as she came away from the water. Qidar lay in ambush for her at the base of a rock on her path, and Mus'da' lay in ambush on another path. The she-camel passed by Mus'da', who shot her with an arrow that lodged in the muscle of her leg. 'Unayza, daughter of Ghanm, went out and told her daughter, who was among the most beautiful people, to unveil herself to Qidar. She did, and then she urged him on. He attacked the she-camel with a sword and cut her hamstring, so she fell and cried out a single cry, warning her young one. Then he stabbed her in the neck and slaughtered her. The people of the town came out, divided her meat, and cooked it. When her young one saw this, he ran until he reached a lofty mountain called Sinw, though it is also said its name was Qarra. Salih was told: "Go after the she-camel, for she has been hamstrung." He came, and they went out to meet him, apologizing to him: "O Prophet of God, it was only so-and-so who hamstrung her, and we are not to blame." Salih said: "See whether you can find her young one. If you find him, perhaps the punishment will be lifted from you." So they went out searching for him. When they saw him on the mountain, they went to seize him, but God revealed to the mountain, and it rose high into the sky until the birds could not reach it.

Salih came, and when the young camel saw him, it wept until its tears flowed, then it cried out three times, and the rock split open and it entered it. Salih said: "For every cry there is a term of one day. Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."

Ibn Ishaq said: Four men from the nine who hamstrung the she-camel followed the young camel. Among them were Mus'addi' ibn Muharrij and his brother Dhab ibn Muharrij. Mus'addi' shot it with an arrow that pierced its heart. Then he dragged it by its leg and brought it down. They threw its meat in with the meat of its mother.

Salih said to them: "You have violated the sanctity of God, so rejoice in the punishment of God and His vengeance." They mocked him and said: "When will that be, O Salih? And what is the sign of it?" They used to name the days among themselves: Ahad was the first day, Ithnayn was "the easier," Thulatha' was Dabar, Arba'a was Jubar, Khamis was Mu'nis, Jum'a was al-'Arubah, and Sabt was Shiyar. They had hamstrung the she-camel on Wednesday. So when they said this, Salih said to them: "You will wake on the morning of Mu'nis with your faces yellowed, then you will wake on the day of al-'Arubah with your faces reddened, then you will wake on the day of Shiyar with your faces blackened, and then the punishment will overtake you on the day of Awwal."

When Salih said this to them, the nine who had hamstrung the she-camel said: "Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful, we will hasten him ahead of us, and if he is lying, we will have joined him to his camel." So they came to him at night to ambush him in his household. But the angels struck them with stones, and when they were late in returning to their companions, they came to Salih's dwelling and found them crushed by stones. They said to Salih: "You killed them." Then they resolved to attack him, but his clan stood between him and them and put on their weapons, and they said to them: "By God, you shall never kill him, for he has promised you that the punishment will descend upon you after three days. If he is truthful, you will only increase your Lord's anger against you, and if he is lying, you will have what you are seeking behind you." So they withdrew from them that night. In the morning, on Thursday, their faces were yellow as though smeared with saffron, the young and the old, the males and the females. So they were certain of the punishment and knew that Salih had spoken the truth. They sought him in order to kill him, but Salih went out fleeing from them until he came to a clan of Thamud called Banu Ghanm. He stayed with their chief, a man called Nufayl, who was known as Abu Hudb, and he was a polytheist. He concealed him, and they could not reach him. So they went to the companions of Salih and tortured them in order to make them guide them to him. A man among the companions of Salih called Mub'i' ibn Haram said: "O Prophet of God, they are torturing us so that we will guide them to you. Shall we guide them?" He said: "Yes." So he guided them to him. They went to Abu Hudb and spoke to him about it, and he said: "Yes, Salih is with me, and you have no way over him." So they turned away from him and left him alone, and what God had sent down upon them of His punishment distracted them from him. Some of them informed others of what they saw in their faces. When evening came, they all cried out: "Surely one day of the term has passed." When they woke on the second day, their faces were reddened as though dyed with blood, so they shouted, wailed and wept, and they knew that it was the punishment. When evening came, they all cried out: "Surely two days of the term have passed, and the punishment has come upon you." When they woke on the third day, their faces were blackened as though smeared with pitch, so they all cried out: "Surely the punishment has come upon you."

When it was the night of Sunday, Salih departed from among them, together with those who had embraced Islam with him, to al-Sham, and he settled at Ramla in Palestine. When the people woke, they wrapped themselves in shrouds, applied perfume, and threw themselves to the ground, turning their eyes to the sky once and to the earth once, not knowing from where the punishment would come to them. When the forenoon of Sunday grew intense, a shout came to them from the sky, containing the sound of every thunderbolt and the voice of everything on earth that has a voice. It tore their hearts within their breasts, and none of them, small or great, remained except that he perished, just as God Most High said: ﴿So they were found lying prostrate in their homes﴾. Except for one paralysed girl called Dhari'ah daughter of Salif, who was an unbeliever and extremely hostile to Salih. God released her legs after she had witnessed the punishment, and she came out faster than anything has ever been seen to move, until she reached Qazah, which is the valley of the villages. She informed them of what she had witnessed of the punishment and what had befallen Thamud. Then she asked for water and was given to drink, and when she drank, she died.

Al-Suddi mentioned another account regarding the hamstringing of the she-camel. He said: God Most High revealed to Salih, peace be upon him, that his people would hamstring his she-camel. He told them this, and they said: "We would never do that." Salih said: "A boy will be born in this month of yours who will hamstring her, and your destruction will be at his hands." They said: "No child will be born to us in this month except that we will kill him." He said: "Nine of them had children born in that month, and they slaughtered their sons. Then a child was born to the tenth, but he refused to slaughter his son, though he had not had a child before that, and his son was blue-eyed and red-complexioned, and grew up quickly. Whenever he passed by the nine and they saw him, they said: 'If our sons were alive, they would have been like this.' So the nine were angry with Salih because he was the cause of the killing of their children. They swore by God: 'We will ambush him and his family.' They said: 'We will go out so that people see that we have gone out on a journey, then we will come to the cave and remain in it, until when night falls and Salih goes out to his mosque, we will come to him and kill him. Then we will return to the cave and stay in it, then we will return to our dwellings and say: We did not witness the destruction of his people, and we are truthful, and they will believe us, thinking that we had set out on a journey.'" Salih did not sleep with them in the village, and he would spend the night in a mosque called the Mosque of Salih. When he woke in the morning, he would come to them and admonish and remind them, and when evening came, he would go out to the mosque and spend the night there. So they set out and entered the cave, and the cave collapsed upon them and killed them. Then some men who had found out about this went out and found them crushed. They returned shouting in the village: "O servants of God, Salih was not satisfied with ordering them to kill their children, so he killed them himself!" The people of the village then united in hamstringing the she-camel.

Ibn Ishaq said: The nine's plot to ambush Salih came after their hamstringing of the she-camel, as we have mentioned.

Al-Suddi and others said: When the son of the tenth was born, namely Qidar, he grew in one day as much as others grew in a week, and in a month as much as others grew in a year. When he became an adult, he sat with some people who were drinking alcohol, and they wanted water to mix with their drink. That day was the she-camel's turn to drink, and they found that the water had been drunk by the she-camel. This upset them greatly, and they said: "What are we to do with milk? If we took this water that the she-camel drinks and gave it to our livestock and our crops, it would be better for us." Ibn al-'Ashir said: "Shall I hamstring her for you?" They said: "Yes," so they hamstrung her.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Yahya ibn Hassan ibn Hayyan Abu Zakariyya, from Sulayman, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar: that when the Messenger of God ﷺ alighted at al-Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he ordered them not to drink from a well there nor to draw water from it. They said: "We have kneaded dough with it and drawn water." So he ordered them to throw away that dough and pour out that water. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter on the words of God Most High: "And to Thamud, their brother Salih": 6/378, and by Muslim in al-Zuhd, chapter "Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves," no. (2981): 4/2286, with a similar wording.]

Nafi' said from Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered them to pour out what they had drawn from its wells, to feed the camels the dough, and ordered them to draw water from the well which the she-camel used to come to. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter on the words of God Most High: "And to Thamud, their brother Salih": 6/378.]

Abu al-Zubayr related from Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ passed by al-Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he said to his companions: "None of you should enter the village, nor drink from its water, nor enter upon these punished people, unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you." Then he said: "As for what follows, do not ask your Messenger for signs. These are the people of Salih, who asked their Messenger, so God sent the she-camel. She used to come from this mountain pass and depart from this mountain pass, and drink their water on the day of her coming. He showed them the place where the young camel ascended from the rock, but they defied the command of their Lord and hamstrung her. So God Most High destroyed everyone under the canopy of the sky among them, in the east and west of the earth, except one man called Abu Righal, who was the father of Thaqif. He was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. But when he came out, what had befallen his people befell him, and he was buried, and a golden branch was buried with him. He showed them the grave of Abu Righal, so the people descended and rushed with their swords, dug around it and extracted that branch." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/230 (Halabi edition), and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad in abridged form: 3/296; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/340-341, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Haythami attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Bazzar and Ahmad, and said: the narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to Ibn Hibban. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/37-38, al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 65, al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/492.]

The believing group from the people of Salih numbered four thousand. Salih led them out to Hadramawt, and when they entered it, Salih died, so it was named Hadramawt (meaning: Salih has died). Then the four thousand built a city called Hasura'. Some people of knowledge said: He died in Mecca at the age of fifty-eight, and he remained among his people for twenty years.

And as for Lut (We sent Lut). It was also said that the meaning is: "Remember Lut." He was Lut ibn Haran ibn Tarikh, the nephew of Ibrahim. ﴿When he said to his people﴾, who were the people of Sodom. The reason was that Lut had set out from the land of Babil [traveled] [[omitted from "B".]] with his uncle Ibrahim, peace be upon him, believing in him and migrating with him to al-Sham. Ibrahim settled in Filastin (Palestine), and Lut settled in al-Urdunn (Jordan). Allah, mighty and majestic, sent him to the people of Sodom, and he said to them: ﴿Do you commit the indecency that no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾, meaning the coming to males. Amr ibn Dinar said: "Whenever a male is seen with a male in the world, he is from the people of Lut."

﴿Indeed you﴾: the people of Medina and Hafs read it (innakum) with a kasra on the alif (inna), as a statement (khabar). The others read it as a resumption (istinaf), so that the sentence begins anew. ﴿Lata'tun al-rijal﴾ (you come to the men) in their backsides, ﴿desire instead of women﴾. This explains that indecency, meaning that the backsides of men are more desirable to you than the private parts of women. ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed the bounds﴾, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They had fruits and villages the like of which was not in the land, so people targeted them and harmed them. Iblis appeared to them in the form of an old man and said: "If you do such and such to them, you will be saved." They refused. When people persisted against them, they targeted them and found them as young boys in the morning, so they seized them and forced them to submit themselves, and they became corrupt, and this practice became firmly established among them. Al-Hasan said: They used to marry only strangers.

Al-Kalbi said: The first to do the deed of the people of Lut was Iblis, because their lands became fertile, so the people of other regions came to them seeking it. That is, Iblis appeared to them in the form of a young man, then he invited them to his backside, and he was taken from behind. Then Allah, exalted, commanded the sky to rain stones upon them and commanded the earth to swallow them.

And as for Lut (We sent Lut). It was also said that the meaning is: "Remember Lut." He was Lut ibn Haran ibn Tarikh, the nephew of Ibrahim. ﴿When he said to his people﴾, who were the people of Sodom. The reason was that Lut had set out from the land of Babil [traveled] [[omitted from "B".]] with his uncle Ibrahim, peace be upon him, believing in him and migrating with him to al-Sham. Ibrahim settled in Filastin (Palestine), and Lut settled in al-Urdunn (Jordan). Allah, mighty and majestic, sent him to the people of Sodom, and he said to them: ﴿Do you commit the indecency that no one in the worlds has committed before you?﴾, meaning the coming to males. Amr ibn Dinar said: "Whenever a male is seen with a male in the world, he is from the people of Lut."

﴿Indeed you﴾: the people of Medina and Hafs read it (innakum) with a kasra on the alif (inna), as a statement (khabar). The others read it as a resumption (istinaf), so that the sentence begins anew. ﴿Lata'tun al-rijal﴾ (you come to the men) in their backsides, ﴿desire instead of women﴾. This explains that indecency, meaning that the backsides of men are more desirable to you than the private parts of women. ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed the bounds﴾, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They had fruits and villages the like of which was not in the land, so people targeted them and harmed them. Iblis appeared to them in the form of an old man and said: "If you do such and such to them, you will be saved." They refused. When people persisted against them, they targeted them and found them as young boys in the morning, so they seized them and forced them to submit themselves, and they became corrupt, and this practice became firmly established among them. Al-Hasan said: They used to marry only strangers.

Al-Kalbi said: The first to do the deed of the people of Lut was Iblis, because their lands became fertile, so the people of other regions came to them seeking it. That is, Iblis appeared to them in the form of a young man, then he invited them to his backside, and he was taken from behind. Then Allah, exalted, commanded the sky to rain stones upon them and commanded the earth to swallow them.

﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said﴾. Some of them said to others: ﴿Expel them from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾. That is, Lut and those who followed his religion. Purity here means they keep themselves away from the backsides of men.

﴿So We saved him﴾, that is, Lut, ﴿and his family﴾, the believers among them. It was also said that his family here means his two daughters. ﴿Except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾, that is, among those left to the punishment. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 86:

﴿And do not sit on every path﴾, i.e., on every road, ﴿threatening﴾, i.e., intimidating, ﴿and barring from the way of Allah﴾

the religion of Allah, ﴿those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked﴾, i.e., deviant. It was also said: you seek crookedness in the religion and deviation from the right course. This was because they used to sit on the road and say to anyone who wished to believe in Shu'ayb: "Indeed, Shu'ayb is a liar, so let him not seduce you from your religion." They would also threaten the believers with killing and frighten them. Al-Suddi said: they were tax collectors (ʿashshārūn).

﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you﴾, so their number increased, ﴿and observe how was the end of the corrupters﴾, i.e., the final outcome of the people of Lut.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 87–89:

﴿And if a group of you believe in that with which I have been sent, and a group does not believe,﴾ meaning: if you differ concerning my message, and you become two factions, some denying and some confirming, ﴿then be patient until Allah judges between us,﴾ by punishing the deniers and saving the believers, ﴿and He is the best of judges.﴾

﴿The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said,﴾ meaning the leaders who magnified themselves above faith in him, ﴿"We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return to our millah (religious community)."﴾ That is, you will return to our religion, which we follow. ﴿He said,﴾ Shu'ayb said, ﴿"Even though we are averse?"﴾ meaning: even if we are averse, that is, even if we dislike it, will you force us into it?

﴿We would have fabricated a lie against Allah if we returned to your millah after Allah had saved us from it, and it is not for us to return to it,﴾ after Allah had rescued us from it, ﴿unless Allah, our Lord, wills.﴾ He says: unless it has already preceded for us in Allah's knowledge and will that we return to it, and then the decree of Allah concerning us proceeds and His judgment is executed upon us.

It is said: What is the meaning of their saying, "or you will return to our millah," and "it is not for us to return to it," when Shu'ayb had never been upon their millah, so that their saying "you will return to our millah" would be correct? It is answered: its meaning is "or you will enter our millah," and so he said, "it is not for us to enter it."

It is also said: its meaning is, if we become in your millah. And the meaning of "ada" (returned) is "sara" (became).

It is also said: by it he meant the people of Shu'ayb, because they had been disbelievers and then believed, so Shu'ayb answered on their behalf.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge,﴾ His knowledge encompasses everything, ﴿in Allah we have put our trust,﴾ regarding what you threaten us with. Then Shu'ayb, after he had despaired of their success, returned and said: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people,﴾ that is: judge between us, ﴿in truth,﴾ and al-Fattah (the Opener) means al-Qadi (the Judge). ﴿And You are the best of those who open,﴾ that is, the best of judges.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 96–100:**

﴿If the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth.﴾ That is, the rain from the sky and the plants from the earth. The root meaning of *barakah* (blessing) is persistence in something, that is, We would have continued to send them rain and plants and lifted from them drought and barrenness. ﴿But they denied, so We seized them for what they had been earning﴾ from evil deeds.

﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure﴾ those who disbelieved and denied, that is, the people of Mecca and its surroundings, ﴿that Our punishment will not come upon them by night﴾ that is, Our chastisement, ﴿while they are sleeping?﴾

﴿Or do they feel secure﴾: Ahl al-Hijaz and Ahl al-Sham read *"aw amina"* with a sukun on the waw (*aw*), while the rest read it with a fatha on it (*awa*). ﴿That the people of the towns will not have Our punishment come upon them in the forenoon﴾ that is, in daytime. *Duha* is the early part of the day, the time when the sun spreads out. ﴿while they are playing?﴾ heedless and amused.

﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of God? None feels secure from the plan of God except the losing people.﴾ The *makr* (plan) of God is His gradual drawing of them on (*istidraj*) by the favours He bestows upon them in their worldly life. Atiyyah said: it means His seizing and His punishment.

﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the land after its people﴾ who were in it before them, ﴿that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins﴾ as We punished those before them, ﴿and We seal up their hearts so they do not hear?﴾ Qatadah and Ya'qub read *"nahdi"* with the nun, as a form of majesty (*ta'zim*), while the rest read it with the ya', in the singular (*tafrid*), meaning: has it not been made clear to them (*awa lam nubayyin*). ﴿We seal﴾ means We lock, ﴿upon their hearts, so they do not hear﴾ faith, and do not accept admonition. Al-Zajjaj said: the statement ﴿and We seal﴾ is disconnected (*munqati'*) from what precedes it, because ﴿We afflicted﴾ is in the past tense (*madi*), while *"natba'u"* (We seal) is in the future tense (*mustaqbal*).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 101–102:

﴿Those are the cities﴾, i.e., these are the cities whose affairs and the affairs of their people I have mentioned to you, meaning: the cities of the people of Noah, ʿAad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and Shuʿayb. ﴿We relate to you some of their news﴾, i.e., their reports, because of the lessons (iʿtibar) they contain. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with signs, miracles, and wonders. ﴿But they were not ones to believe in what they had denied before﴾, i.e., they were not going to believe, after seeing the miracles and wonders, in what they had denied before seeing those wonders. Its parallel is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: (A people before you asked such questions, then they became disbelievers because of them) [al-Ma'idah: 102].

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi said: meaning, these disbelievers whom We destroyed would not have believed, upon the sending of the messengers, in what they had denied before, on the day the covenant was taken from them when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam; so they acknowledged with their tongues while concealing denial. Mujahid said: its meaning is that they would not have believed, even if We had brought them back to life after their destruction, in what they had denied before their destruction, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden) [al-An'am: 28].

Yaman ibn Rabab said: this is in the sense that every prophet warned his people of the punishment and they denied him; it means: they would not have believed in what their predecessors of the bygone nations had denied, but rather they denied what their predecessors had denied. Its parallel is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: (Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "A sorcerer or a madman") [al-Dhariyat: 52].

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., just as Allah sealed the hearts of the bygone nations whom He destroyed, so Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers among your people whom He has decreed will not believe.

﴿And We did not find in most of them any covenant﴾, i.e., fulfilment of the covenant which He made with them on the day of the covenant, when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam. ﴿And indeed, We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., We found most of them to be none but defiantly disobedient, breakers of the covenant.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 103–107:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa with Our signs﴾, that is: after Nuh, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb, ﴿Musa with Our signs﴾, meaning with Our proofs, ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged them﴾, meaning they denied them. The word zulm (wrongdoing) means placing a thing in other than its proper place, so their wronging consisted in placing disbelief in the place of faith. ﴿Then see how was the end of the corrupters﴾, meaning: and how We dealt with them.

﴿And Musa said﴾, when he entered upon Pharaoh: ﴿O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾ to you. Pharaoh said: "You are lying." Musa said:

﴿It is fitting for me that I should not say about Allah except the truth﴾. That is: I am worthy (khaliq, "deserving") that I should not say about Allah except the truth. Here "ʿalā" (on/upon) carries the meaning of "bi" (with), as one says: "ramaytu bi-l-qaws" and "ramaytu ʿalā l-qaws" (I shot with the bow), and "ji'tu ʿalā ḥālin ḥasanatin" and "bi-ḥālin ḥasanatin" (I came in a good state). This is supported by the reading of Ubayy and al-A'mash: "ḥaqīqun bi-an lā aqūla ʿalā llāhi illā l-ḥaqq." Abu ʿUbayda said: its meaning is "ḥarīṣun ʿalā an lā aqūla ʿalā llāhi illā l-ḥaqq" (eager that I should not say about Allah except the truth). Nafi' read (ʿalayya) with a shadda on the yāʾ, meaning: it is a binding truth upon me that I should not say about Allah except the truth.

﴿I have certainly come to you with a clear proof from your Lord﴾, meaning the staff, ﴿so send with me the Children of Israel﴾, that is: release them and let them go back to the Holy Land. Pharaoh had made them serve in hard labour, such as brick-making, carrying earth, and the like.

Pharaoh said, replying to Musa: ﴿He said: If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are of the truthful﴾.

﴿So Musa cast down his staff﴾ from his hand, ﴿and behold, it was a serpent, manifest﴾. The thu'ban (serpent) is the great male of the snakes. If it is said: Did He not say elsewhere: ﴿as if it were a jann﴾ [an-Naml: 10], and the jann is a small snake? It is said: it was like the jann in its movement and agility, but in its body it was a great serpent.

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi said: when he cast down the staff, it became a great serpent, yellow and maned, its mouth wide open, the distance between its two jaws being eighty cubits, and it rose from the ground to the height of a mile. It stood up before him on its tail, placing its lower jaw on the ground and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, and it turned towards Pharaoh to seize him. It is related that it took hold of Pharaoh's canopy between its fangs, so Pharaoh leapt from his throne fleeing, and he defecated.

It is said: the bowel complaint seized him that day four hundred times, and it charged at the people, so they fled and cried out, and twenty-five thousand of them died, some of them trampling others. Pharaoh entered the house and cried: "O Musa, I beseech you by the One who sent you, take it back, and I will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 113–117:**

﴿And the sorcerers came to Pharaoh﴾, and they gathered together. ﴿They said﴾ to Pharaoh, ﴿"Indeed, there will surely be a reward for us"﴾, that is, a payment (ju'l) and wealth, ﴿"if we are the victors"﴾. The people of the Hijaz (Ahl al-Hijaz) and Hafs read "inna lana" (إِنَّ لَنَا) as a declarative statement, while the rest read it as an interrogative (bi-l-istifham). They did not differ regarding ash-Shu'ara' (verse 41) that it is interrogative.

﴿Pharaoh said﴾, ﴿"Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near"﴾ in high rank with me, in addition to the reward. Al-Kalbi said: that means you will be the first to enter and the last to leave.

﴿They said﴾, meaning the sorcerers, ﴿"O Musa, either you throw﴾ your staff, ﴿or we will be the throwers"﴾ of our staffs and ropes.

﴿He said﴾, Musa, ﴿"Rather, you throw"﴾. ﴿So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people﴾, that is, they diverted their eyes from perceiving the reality of what they had done, through deception (tamwih) and imagination (takhyil), and this is what sorcery is. ﴿And they terrified them﴾, that is, they frightened and alarmed them. ﴿And they produced a great sorcery﴾. That is because they threw large ropes and long pieces of wood, and suddenly they were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, climbing over one another. It is related in the story that the earth, a mile by a mile, became serpents and vipers in the eyes of the people.

﴿And We revealed to Musa, "Throw your staff"﴾. So he threw it, and it became a great serpent, until it blocked the horizon. Ibn Zayd said: their gathering was at Alexandria. It is said: the tail of the serpent reached behind the lake, then it opened its mouth eighty cubits wide. ﴿Then it began to swallow﴾. Hafs read "talqafu" (تَلْقَفُ) with a sukun on the lam, lightened, wherever it occurs, while the others read it with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the qaf, meaning "it swallows". ﴿What they fabricate﴾, that is, what they lie about of imaginings. It was also said: they were forging falsehoods upon the people. So it seized their ropes and their staffs one by one until it had swallowed them all, and it turned toward the people who were present, so the crowd fell upon one another, and there died in the crush twenty-five thousand of them. Then Musa took it, and it became a staff as it had been.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 118–124:

﴿فَوَقَعَ الْحَقُّ﴾ Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: "The truth became manifest." ﴿وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ "And what they had been doing was nullified," i.e., the magic. The reason was that the magicians said: "If what Musa is doing were magic, our ropes and our staffs would have remained. When they were gone, they knew that this was from the command of Allah."

﴿فَغُلِبُوا هُنَالِكَ وَانْقَلَبُوا صَاغِرِينَ﴾ "They were overcome there and turned back humiliated," i.e., disgraced and subdued.

﴿وَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾ "And the magicians were cast down prostrating," to Allah the Exalted. Muqatil said: "Allah cast them down." It was also said: "Allah inspired them to prostrate, and so they prostrated." Al-Akhfash said: "Because of how quickly they prostrated, it was as if they had been thrown down."

﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ "They said: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds." Pharaoh said: "Do you mean me?" They said: ﴿رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ "The Lord of Musa and Harun."

﴿رَبِّ مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ﴾ Muqatil said: Musa said to the chief of the magicians: "Will you believe in me if I defeat you?" He said: "I will bring a magic that no magic can overcome, and if you defeat me, I will certainly believe in you," while Pharaoh was watching.

﴿قَالَ﴾ Pharaoh said to them, when they believed: ﴿آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ "Have you believed in him?" Hafs recited "āmantum" as a statement (khabar) here, and in Ta-Ha and ash-Shu'ara'; the others recited it as a question (istifham): "a'amantum bih?" ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾ "Before I gave you permission?" i.e., "Did you believe Musa without my command to you?" ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَمَكْرٌ مَكَرْتُمُوهُ﴾ "Indeed, this is a plot you have plotted," i.e., a scheme you and Musa devised ﴿فِي الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ "in the city," i.e., in Egypt, before your departure to this place, ﴿لِتُخْرِجُوا مِنْهَا أَهْلَهَا﴾ "to expel its people from it," so that you might take control of Egypt. ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "But you will soon know" what I will do to you.

﴿لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ "I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides," which means cutting off one extremity from each side. Al-Kalbi said: "I will cut off your right hands and your left feet." ﴿ثُمَّ لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ "Then I will crucify you all" on the bank of [the river] [[In "B": (sea)]] of Egypt.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 125–127:**

﴿They said﴾, meaning the sorcerers to Pharaoh, ﴿Indeed, we are to our Lord returning﴾, meaning returning in the Hereafter.

﴿And you do not resent us﴾, meaning: you do not hate us. Al-Dahhak and others said: "You do not find fault with us." 'Ata' said: "We have no sin against you for which you would punish us, ﴿except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us﴾." Then they turned to God, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿"Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, meaning pour out, ﴿and cause us to die as Muslims"﴾. Al-Kalbi mentioned that Pharaoh cut off their hands and feet and crucified them. Others mentioned that he was not able to reach them, based on the words of God the Exalted: (They will not reach you both by Our signs; you and those who follow you will be the victors) [al-Qasas: 35].

﴿And the eminent ones of the people of Pharaoh said﴾ to him, ﴿"Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land?"﴾ By "causing corruption in the land" they meant calling the people to oppose Pharaoh in his worship. ﴿And leave you﴾, meaning: and so that they leave you, ﴿and your gods﴾, so that he would not worship you and you would not be worshipped. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had a cow that he worshipped, and whenever he saw a beautiful cow he would order them to worship it. That is why al-Samiri brought out a calf for them. Al-Hasan said: he had hung a cross around his neck and worshipped it. Al-Suddi said: Pharaoh had taken idols for his people and ordered them to worship them, and he said to his people, "These are your gods, and I am their lord and your lord." That is His saying (I am your most high lord) [al-Nazi'at: 24]. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak recited: "وَيَذَرَكَ وَإِلَاهَتِكَ" with a kasra on the alif, meaning: your worship, so that he would not worship you, because Pharaoh was worshipped and did not worship. It was also said that by "al-ilah" (the gods) he meant the sun, and they used to worship it. The poet said:

"We went back from al-La'ba at midday to a palace, and hurried the sun-goddess lest she return."

﴿He said﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿"We will kill their sons﴾. The people of the Hijaz recited "سَنَقْتُلُ" with light emphasis, from the verb "qatala" (to kill), while the others recited it with the doubled "qatt" from "taqtil" (repeated killing) for intensification: "سَنُقَتِّلُ". ﴿And keep their women alive﴾, meaning we will leave them alive, ﴿and indeed we are above them, dominant﴾, meaning victorious.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh used to kill the sons of the Children of Israel in the year in which it was said that a boy would be born who would take away your kingdom. He continued killing them until Moses came to them with the message, and what came of his affair came. Pharaoh said: "Repeat the killing of them." So they repeated the killing of them, and the Children of Israel complained about that.

It was also said that by "al-ilah" (the gods) he meant the sun, and they used to worship it. The poet said:

"We went back from al-La'ba at midday to a palace, and hurried the sun-goddess lest she return."

﴿He said﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿"We will kill their sons﴾. The people of the Hijaz recited "سَنَقْتُلُ" with light emphasis, from the verb "qatala" (to kill), while the others recited it with the doubled "qatt" from "taqtil" (repeated killing) for intensification: "سَنُقَتِّلُ". ﴿And keep their women alive﴾, meaning we will leave them alive, ﴿and indeed we are above them, dominant﴾, meaning victorious.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh used to kill the sons of the Children of Israel in the year in which it was said that a boy would be born who would take away your kingdom. He continued killing them until Moses came to them with the message, and what came of his affair came. Pharaoh said: "Repeat the killing of them." So they repeated the killing of them, and the Children of Israel complained about that.

﴿Musa said to his people, "Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the good outcome is for the God-conscious (al-muttaqun)."﴾ He means the land of Egypt. ﴿He gives it as inheritance﴾ means He gives it to ﴿whomever He wills of His servants﴾. ﴿The good outcome is for the God-conscious﴾ means victory and triumph. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 131–133:

﴿When good came to them﴾, meaning: fertility, abundance and well-being, ﴿they said, "This is ours"﴾, that is: we are its people and deserve it by the custom that has prevailed for us in the abundance of our provisions. They did not regard it as a favour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that they would give thanks for it. ﴿But if an evil befell them﴾, drought and calamity, and they saw what they disliked, ﴿they ascribed it as an omen﴾, that is, they considered it a bad omen, ﴿to Moses and those with him﴾. They said: "Nothing has befallen us in calamity until we saw them. This is from the ill omen of Moses and his people."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: The rule of Pharaoh lasted four hundred years, and he lived six hundred and twenty years without seeing anything disagreeable. Had he suffered for one day from hunger, or a fever for one night, or a pain for one hour during that period, he would never have claimed lordship. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Behold, their omen is with Allah﴾, that is: their portion of fertility and drought, good and evil, is entirely from Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Their omen is what Allah has decreed for them and determined for them." In another report from him: "Their misfortune is with Allah and from Allah's side," that is: misfortune came to them only because of their disbelief in Allah. It has also been said: its meaning is the great misfortune that awaits them with Allah, namely the punishment of the Fire. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that what befell them was from Allah.

﴿They said﴾, meaning: the Copts, to Moses, ﴿Whatever sign you bring us﴾ (mahma: a word used for condition and consequence; mata ma), ﴿with which to bewitch us﴾, to turn us from the religion we are upon, ﴿we will not believe you﴾, that is, we will not accept you as truthful.

﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and Muhammad ibn Ishaq (their statements have intermingled) said: When the magicians believed and Pharaoh returned defeated, he and his people refused anything but to remain in disbelief and persist in evil. So Allah sent them sign after sign, and seized them with years of famine and a decrease in fruits. When He had dealt with them through the four signs, the staff, the hand, the years of famine and the decrease of fruits, and they refused to believe, Moses prayed against them, saying: "O Lord, Your servant Pharaoh has exalted himself in the land, transgressed and rebelled, and his people have broken Your covenant. Lord, seize them with a punishment that You make a vengeance for them, an admonition for my people, and a sign and lesson for those after them." So Allah sent upon them the flood, which is the water: Allah sent water upon them, while the houses of the Children of Israel and the houses of the Copts were intermingled. The houses of the Copts filled with water until they stood in it up to their collarbones, and whoever sat down among them drowned, while not a drop of water entered the houses of the Children of Israel. The water stood on their land, so they could not plough or do any work. This lasted for them seven days, from Saturday to Saturday.

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: the flood is death. Wahb said: the flood is the plague, in the language of Yemen. Abu Qilabah said: the flood is smallpox, and they were the first people to be punished with it, and it remained on earth.

Muqatil said: the flood is the water that rose above their crops.

Ibn Dhabyan related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The flood is a command from Allah that encompassed them," then he recited: (Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping) [al-Qalam: 19].

The grammarians of Kufa said: al-tufan is a verbal noun that is not pluralised, like al-rujhan and al-nuqsan. The grammarians of Basra said: it is a plural, its singular being tufanah. So they said to Moses: "Pray to your Lord to remove the rain from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the flood from them. Allah then caused to grow for them, in that year, things they had never noticed before: grass, crops and fruit, and their lands became fertile. They said: "This water was only a blessing upon us and abundance." They did not believe, and they remained a month in well-being. Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, which devoured most of their crops, fruits and the leaves of trees, until they were eating the doors, roof beams of the houses, wood, clothes, belongings and the iron door nails, until their homes collapsed. The locusts were afflicted with hunger, so they never got full. None of this befell the Children of Israel. They wailed and cried out, saying: "O Moses, pray to your Lord for us. If you remove the plague from us, we will truly believe in you," and they gave him Allah's covenant and His pledge. Moses, upon him be peace, prayed, and Allah removed the locusts from them after they had remained for seven days, from Saturday to Saturday.

In a report: "Upon the breast of every locust is written: the Greatest Army of Allah." [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/522-523, which contains a number of reports with this meaning, some of which are weak and objectionable.]]

It is said that Moses went out to an open space and pointed with his staff towards the east and the west, and the locusts returned from where they had come. Some of their crops and produce had remained, so they said: "What remains for us is sufficient, and we will not abandon our religion." They did not fulfil what they had pledged and returned to their evil deeds. They remained a month in well-being, then Allah sent upon them the lice.

[They differed concerning the lice.] Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: al-qummal is the weevil that emerges from wheat. Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: al-qummal is the dabā and the flying locusts that have wings, and the dabā are the small ones that have no wings. [Ikrimah said: they are the young of the locusts.] Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is al-hamnan, a kind of tick. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is the lice. And Abu al-Hasan recited it as (al-qaml) with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the mim.

They said: Allah commanded Moses to walk to a reddish sand-hill in a village of Egypt called 'Ayn al-Shams. Moses walked to that sand-hill, which was sandy, and struck it with his staff, and the lice poured out upon them. They pursued whatever remained of their crops, trees and livestock and ate it, and they licked up all the earth. It would enter between a man's garment and his skin and bite him, and a man would eat food and it would be full of lice.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: al-qummal is the weevil that emerges from grains. A man would take out ten sacks to the mill and would not get back three qafiz from them. They were not afflicted with a calamity more severe for them than the lice. It took their hair, their skin, the eyelashes of their eyes and their eyebrows, and it clung to their skins like smallpox upon them, and it prevented them from sleep and rest. They cried out and shouted to Moses: "We repent, so pray to your Lord to remove the calamity from us." Moses, upon him be peace, prayed to Allah, and Allah removed the lice from them after they had remained upon them for seven days, from Saturday to Saturday. Then they broke their word and returned to their most wicked deeds. They said: "We have never been more certain that he is a sorcerer than today, when he makes the sand into creatures." Moses prayed after they had remained a month in well-being, and Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled their houses, their courtyards, their food and their vessels. No one would uncover a vessel or food without finding frogs in it. A man would sit among the frogs up to his chin, and when he wanted to speak a frog would leap into his mouth. They would leap into their cooking pots and spoil their food and extinguish their fires. A man would lie down and frogs would climb on him in heaps, until he could not turn to his other side. He would open his mouth to take a bite and a frog would reach his mouth before his food did. If he kneaded dough, it would be crushed in it, and if he opened a cooking pot it would be full of frogs. They suffered great harm from them.

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: the frogs were land creatures. When Allah sent them upon the family of Pharaoh, they heard and obeyed, so they began to throw themselves into the cooking pots while they were boiling, and into the ovens while they were blazing. Allah rewarded them for their good obedience with cool water. When they saw this, they wept and complained of it to Moses, saying: "This time we repent and will not return." He took their pledges and covenants. Then he prayed to his Lord and He removed the frogs from them after they had remained seven Saturdays, from Saturday to Saturday. They remained a month in well-being, then they broke the covenant and returned to their disbelief. So Moses prayed against them, and Allah sent upon them blood. The Nile flowed with blood over them, their water became blood, and whenever they drew water from the wells and rivers they found only thick, red blood. They complained to Pharaoh, saying: "We have no drink." He said: "He has bewitched you." They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find nothing in our vessels but thick blood?" Pharaoh used to put a Copt and an Israelite together at one vessel, and what was on the side of the Israelite would be water and the Copt's side would be blood. [They would both go to the jar in which there was water, and the Israelite would get water while the Copt got blood.] So much so that a woman of the family of Pharaoh would come to a woman of the Children of Israel when thirst had afflicted them and say: "Give me to drink from your water," and she would pour for her from her waterskin, and it would turn into blood in the vessel. She would say: "Put it in your mouth and then spit it into mine," and she would take water into her mouth, but when she spat it into the other's mouth it became blood. Pharaoh himself was seized by thirst so severely that he was compelled to chew moist trees, and when he chewed them their water became salty, bitter water in his mouth. They remained in this condition for seven days, drinking nothing but blood.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: the blood with which they were afflicted was nosebleeding. They came to Moses and said: "O Moses, pray to your Lord to remove this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs﴾, following one another. Their detail is that each punishment lasted a week, and between every two punishments there was a month. ﴿But they were arrogant and were a guilty people.﴾
