Zayd ibn Aslam said: the blood with which they were afflicted was nosebleeding. They came to Moses and said: "O Moses, pray to your Lord to remove this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs﴾, following one another. Their detail is that each punishment lasted a week, and between every two punishments there was a month. ﴿But they were arrogant and were a guilty people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 131–133:

﴿When good came to them﴾, meaning: fertility, abundance and well-being, ﴿they said, "This is ours"﴾, that is: we are its people and deserve it by the custom that has prevailed for us in the abundance of our provisions. They did not regard it as a favour from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that they would give thanks for it. ﴿But if an evil befell them﴾, drought and calamity, and they saw what they disliked, ﴿they ascribed it as an omen﴾, that is, they considered it a bad omen, ﴿to Moses and those with him﴾. They said: "Nothing has befallen us in calamity until we saw them. This is from the ill omen of Moses and his people."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: The rule of Pharaoh lasted four hundred years, and he lived six hundred and twenty years without seeing anything disagreeable. Had he suffered for one day from hunger, or a fever for one night, or a pain for one hour during that period, he would never have claimed lordship. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Behold, their omen is with Allah﴾, that is: their portion of fertility and drought, good and evil, is entirely from Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Their omen is what Allah has decreed for them and determined for them." In another report from him: "Their misfortune is with Allah and from Allah's side," that is: misfortune came to them only because of their disbelief in Allah. It has also been said: its meaning is the great misfortune that awaits them with Allah, namely the punishment of the Fire. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that what befell them was from Allah.

﴿They said﴾, meaning: the Copts, to Moses, ﴿Whatever sign you bring us﴾ (mahma: a word used for condition and consequence; mata ma), ﴿with which to bewitch us﴾, to turn us from the religion we are upon, ﴿we will not believe you﴾, that is, we will not accept you as truthful.

﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and Muhammad ibn Ishaq (their statements have intermingled) said: When the magicians believed and Pharaoh returned defeated, he and his people refused anything but to remain in disbelief and persist in evil. So Allah sent them sign after sign, and seized them with years of famine and a decrease in fruits. When He had dealt with them through the four signs, the staff, the hand, the years of famine and the decrease of fruits, and they refused to believe, Moses prayed against them, saying: "O Lord, Your servant Pharaoh has exalted himself in the land, transgressed and rebelled, and his people have broken Your covenant. Lord, seize them with a punishment that You make a vengeance for them, an admonition for my people, and a sign and lesson for those after them." So Allah sent upon them the flood, which is the water: Allah sent water upon them, while the houses of the Children of Israel and the houses of the Copts were intermingled. The houses of the Copts filled with water until they stood in it up to their collarbones, and whoever sat down among them drowned, while not a drop of water entered the houses of the Children of Israel. The water stood on their land, so they could not plough or do any work. This lasted for them seven days, from Saturday to Saturday.

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: the flood is death. Wahb said: the flood is the plague, in the language of Yemen. Abu Qilabah said: the flood is smallpox, and they were the first people to be punished with it, and it remained on earth.

Muqatil said: the flood is the water that rose above their crops.

Ibn Dhabyan related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The flood is a command from Allah that encompassed them," then he recited: (Then there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were sleeping) [al-Qalam: 19].

The grammarians of Kufa said: al-tufan is a verbal noun that is not pluralised, like al-rujhan and al-nuqsan. The grammarians of Basra said: it is a plural, its singular being tufanah. So they said to Moses: "Pray to your Lord to remove the rain from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the flood from them. Allah then caused to grow for them, in that year, things they had never noticed before: grass, crops and fruit, and their lands became fertile. They said: "This water was only a blessing upon us and abundance." They did not believe, and they remained a month in well-being. Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, which devoured most of their crops, fruits and the leaves of trees, until they were eating the doors, roof beams of the houses, wood, clothes, belongings and the iron door nails, until their homes collapsed. The locusts were afflicted with hunger, so they never got full. None of this befell the Children of Israel. They wailed and cried out, saying: "O Moses, pray to your Lord for us. If you remove the plague from us, we will truly believe in you," and they gave him Allah's covenant and His pledge. Moses, upon him be peace, prayed, and Allah removed the locusts from them after they had remained for seven days, from Saturday to Saturday.

In a report: "Upon the breast of every locust is written: the Greatest Army of Allah." [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/522-523, which contains a number of reports with this meaning, some of which are weak and objectionable.]]

It is said that Moses went out to an open space and pointed with his staff towards the east and the west, and the locusts returned from where they had come. Some of their crops and produce had remained, so they said: "What remains for us is sufficient, and we will not abandon our religion." They did not fulfil what they had pledged and returned to their evil deeds. They remained a month in well-being, then Allah sent upon them the lice.

[They differed concerning the lice.] Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: al-qummal is the weevil that emerges from wheat. Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: al-qummal is the dabā and the flying locusts that have wings, and the dabā are the small ones that have no wings. [Ikrimah said: they are the young of the locusts.] Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is al-hamnan, a kind of tick. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: it is the lice. And Abu al-Hasan recited it as (al-qaml) with a fatha on the qaf and a sukun on the mim.

They said: Allah commanded Moses to walk to a reddish sand-hill in a village of Egypt called 'Ayn al-Shams. Moses walked to that sand-hill, which was sandy, and struck it with his staff, and the lice poured out upon them. They pursued whatever remained of their crops, trees and livestock and ate it, and they licked up all the earth. It would enter between a man's garment and his skin and bite him, and a man would eat food and it would be full of lice.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: al-qummal is the weevil that emerges from grains. A man would take out ten sacks to the mill and would not get back three qafiz from them. They were not afflicted with a calamity more severe for them than the lice. It took their hair, their skin, the eyelashes of their eyes and their eyebrows, and it clung to their skins like smallpox upon them, and it prevented them from sleep and rest. They cried out and shouted to Moses: "We repent, so pray to your Lord to remove the calamity from us." Moses, upon him be peace, prayed to Allah, and Allah removed the lice from them after they had remained upon them for seven days, from Saturday to Saturday. Then they broke their word and returned to their most wicked deeds. They said: "We have never been more certain that he is a sorcerer than today, when he makes the sand into creatures." Moses prayed after they had remained a month in well-being, and Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled their houses, their courtyards, their food and their vessels. No one would uncover a vessel or food without finding frogs in it. A man would sit among the frogs up to his chin, and when he wanted to speak a frog would leap into his mouth. They would leap into their cooking pots and spoil their food and extinguish their fires. A man would lie down and frogs would climb on him in heaps, until he could not turn to his other side. He would open his mouth to take a bite and a frog would reach his mouth before his food did. If he kneaded dough, it would be crushed in it, and if he opened a cooking pot it would be full of frogs. They suffered great harm from them.

Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: the frogs were land creatures. When Allah sent them upon the family of Pharaoh, they heard and obeyed, so they began to throw themselves into the cooking pots while they were boiling, and into the ovens while they were blazing. Allah rewarded them for their good obedience with cool water. When they saw this, they wept and complained of it to Moses, saying: "This time we repent and will not return." He took their pledges and covenants. Then he prayed to his Lord and He removed the frogs from them after they had remained seven Saturdays, from Saturday to Saturday. They remained a month in well-being, then they broke the covenant and returned to their disbelief. So Moses prayed against them, and Allah sent upon them blood. The Nile flowed with blood over them, their water became blood, and whenever they drew water from the wells and rivers they found only thick, red blood. They complained to Pharaoh, saying: "We have no drink." He said: "He has bewitched you." They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find nothing in our vessels but thick blood?" Pharaoh used to put a Copt and an Israelite together at one vessel, and what was on the side of the Israelite would be water and the Copt's side would be blood. [They would both go to the jar in which there was water, and the Israelite would get water while the Copt got blood.] So much so that a woman of the family of Pharaoh would come to a woman of the Children of Israel when thirst had afflicted them and say: "Give me to drink from your water," and she would pour for her from her waterskin, and it would turn into blood in the vessel. She would say: "Put it in your mouth and then spit it into mine," and she would take water into her mouth, but when she spat it into the other's mouth it became blood. Pharaoh himself was seized by thirst so severely that he was compelled to chew moist trees, and when he chewed them their water became salty, bitter water in his mouth. They remained in this condition for seven days, drinking nothing but blood.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: the blood with which they were afflicted was nosebleeding. They came to Moses and said: "O Moses, pray to your Lord to remove this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, as distinct signs﴾, following one another. Their detail is that each punishment lasted a week, and between every two punishments there was a month. ﴿But they were arrogant and were a guilty people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 134–136:

﴿When the plague (ar-rijz) befell them﴾, i.e., the punishment descended upon them, which is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: the flood and other things. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ar-rijz is the plague ( at-ta'un), and it was the sixth punishment after the [five] signs [[Omitted from "A".]], until seventy thousand of them died in one day, so that by evening they had no one left to bury them. ﴿They said﴾ to Musa, ﴿"O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you"﴾, i.e., by what He has enjoined upon you.

Ata' said: "by what He has informed you." It was also said: "by what He has covenanted with you of answering your supplication" ﴿"If you remove the punishment (ar-rijz) from us"﴾, which is the plague, ﴿"we will surely believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you."﴾

Abu al-Hasan as-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi narrated to us: Abu Mus'ab narrated to us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Abu an-Nadr, mawla of Umar ibn Ubayd Allah, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, that he heard him asking Usama ibn Zayd: "Did you hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the plague?" Usama ibn Zayd said: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said] [[Omitted from "B".]]: "The plague is a punishment (rijz) sent upon the Children of Israel, or upon those who were before you. So when you hear of it in a land, do not go to it; and when it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya' (6/513), and Muslim in as-Salam, chapter on plague, omens, soothsaying and the like, no. (2218) 4/1737, and the author in Sharh as-Sunnah: 5/254.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So when We removed the punishment from them, until a term which they were to reach﴾, meaning: until drowning in the sea, ﴿behold, they broke their word﴾, i.e., they violated the covenant.

﴿So We took vengeance upon them and drowned them in the sea﴾, meaning: the sea (al-yamm), ﴿because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾, i.e., heedless of the retribution before it befell them. It was also said: the meaning is "turning away from Our signs."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 137–140:

﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit﴾ (they were) subdued and humiliated, through the slaughter of their sons and the use of their women for service, and the enslavement, and they were the Children of Israel [[Omitted from "ب".]] ﴿the eastern and western parts of the land﴾, meaning Egypt and al-Sham (Syria), ﴿which We had blessed﴾ with water, trees, fruits, fertility and abundance. ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾, meaning: the word of Allah was fulfilled, which was His promise to them of victory and establishment in the land. This is His saying, exalted is He: (And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land) [al-Qasas: 5]. ﴿Because they had been patient﴾ in their religion and under the torment of Pharaoh. ﴿And We destroyed﴾, meaning We annihilated, ﴿what Pharaoh and his people had been making﴾ in the land of Egypt of buildings, ﴿and what they had been erecting﴾. Mujahid said: they used to build of houses and palaces. Al-Hasan said: they used to erect (trellises) of trees, fruits and grapes. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read ﴿ya'rushun﴾ with a damma on the ra' here and in al-Nahl, and the others read it with a kasra.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. Al-Kalbi said: Musa brought them across the sea on the day of 'Ashura', after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, so he fasted it in gratitude to Allah, mighty and majestic. ﴿Then they came﴾, meaning they passed, ﴿upon a people who were devoted﴾, meaning who remained (in devotion). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ya'kifun" with a kasra on the kaf, and the others read it with a damma, and both are dialects. ﴿To idols﴾, meaning idols, ﴿belonging to them﴾, which they worshipped besides Allah.

Ibn Jurayj said: they were images of cows, and that was the beginning of the matter of the calf. Qatadah said: those people were from Lakhm, and they were encamped at al-Raqqah. When the Children of Israel saw that, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god﴾, meaning an image that we may worship, ﴿just as they have gods﴾. That was not a doubt on the part of the Children of Israel concerning the oneness of Allah; rather its meaning was: make for us something that we may magnify, and draw near to Allah, mighty and majestic, through magnifying it. They thought that this would not harm their religion, and that was because of the severity of their ignorance.

﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿Indeed you are a people who are ignorant﴾ of the greatness of Allah.

﴿Indeed, these – what they are in is doomed﴾, destroyed, ﴿and worthless is what they have been doing﴾. And al-Tabbir is destruction.

﴿He said﴾, meaning Musa: ﴿Should I seek for you other than Allah as a god, while He has preferred you over the worlds?﴾, meaning: should I seek and request for you, ﴿over the worlds﴾, meaning over the worlds of your time.

Abu Sa'id 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us, that my grandfather Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us, that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us, that Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dayri informed us, that 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, that Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ toward Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, make for us a Dhat Anwat as the disbelievers have a Dhat Anwat." The disbelievers used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and sit around it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allahu akbar! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Musa: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods.' Indeed you will follow the ways of those before you." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on trials, the section "You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you": 6/407–408, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. And Ibn Ishaq in al-Sirah: 4/84–85; al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, no. (1346); Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah: 1/37; Ibn Hibban, no. (1835) from Mawarid al-Zam'an; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/218. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 137–140:

﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit﴾ (they were) subdued and humiliated, through the slaughter of their sons and the use of their women for service, and the enslavement, and they were the Children of Israel [[Omitted from "ب".]] ﴿the eastern and western parts of the land﴾, meaning Egypt and al-Sham (Syria), ﴿which We had blessed﴾ with water, trees, fruits, fertility and abundance. ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾, meaning: the word of Allah was fulfilled, which was His promise to them of victory and establishment in the land. This is His saying, exalted is He: (And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land) [al-Qasas: 5]. ﴿Because they had been patient﴾ in their religion and under the torment of Pharaoh. ﴿And We destroyed﴾, meaning We annihilated, ﴿what Pharaoh and his people had been making﴾ in the land of Egypt of buildings, ﴿and what they had been erecting﴾. Mujahid said: they used to build of houses and palaces. Al-Hasan said: they used to erect (trellises) of trees, fruits and grapes. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read ﴿ya'rushun﴾ with a damma on the ra' here and in al-Nahl, and the others read it with a kasra.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. Al-Kalbi said: Musa brought them across the sea on the day of 'Ashura', after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, so he fasted it in gratitude to Allah, mighty and majestic. ﴿Then they came﴾, meaning they passed, ﴿upon a people who were devoted﴾, meaning who remained (in devotion). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ya'kifun" with a kasra on the kaf, and the others read it with a damma, and both are dialects. ﴿To idols﴾, meaning idols, ﴿belonging to them﴾, which they worshipped besides Allah.

Ibn Jurayj said: they were images of cows, and that was the beginning of the matter of the calf. Qatadah said: those people were from Lakhm, and they were encamped at al-Raqqah. When the Children of Israel saw that, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god﴾, meaning an image that we may worship, ﴿just as they have gods﴾. That was not a doubt on the part of the Children of Israel concerning the oneness of Allah; rather its meaning was: make for us something that we may magnify, and draw near to Allah, mighty and majestic, through magnifying it. They thought that this would not harm their religion, and that was because of the severity of their ignorance.

﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿Indeed you are a people who are ignorant﴾ of the greatness of Allah.

﴿Indeed, these – what they are in is doomed﴾, destroyed, ﴿and worthless is what they have been doing﴾. And al-Tabbir is destruction.

﴿He said﴾, meaning Musa: ﴿Should I seek for you other than Allah as a god, while He has preferred you over the worlds?﴾, meaning: should I seek and request for you, ﴿over the worlds﴾, meaning over the worlds of your time.

Abu Sa'id 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us, that my grandfather Abu Sahl 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us, that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us, that Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dayri informed us, that 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, that Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ toward Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, make for us a Dhat Anwat as the disbelievers have a Dhat Anwat." The disbelievers used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and sit around it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allahu akbar! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Musa: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods.' Indeed you will follow the ways of those before you." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on trials, the section "You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you": 6/407–408, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. And Ibn Ishaq in al-Sirah: 4/84–85; al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, no. (1346); Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah: 1/37; Ibn Hibban, no. (1835) from Mawarid al-Zam'an; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/218. See: al-Nahj al-Sadid fi Takhrij Ahadith Taysir al-'Aziz al-Hamid, pp. 64–65.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 141–142:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you﴾. Ibn 'Amir read "anjākum" (anjākum, "He delivered you"), and it is likewise written so in the Mushafs of the people of Syria. ﴿from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women﴾. Nafi' read "yaqtulūna" (yaqtulūna, "they slaughter") with a light (khafīfah) pronunciation, from al-qatl (killing). The others read it with shaddah (the doubled consonant), indicating intensification, from al-taqtīl (repeated slaughter). ﴿And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾.

﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights﴾, of Dhu al-Qa'dah, ﴿and We completed them with ten﴾ from Dhu al-Hijjah, ﴿so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said﴾ at his departure toward the mountain for the intimate converse (munājāh), ﴿to his brother Aaron: Be my successor﴾, be my deputy, ﴿among my people, and set things right﴾, meaning: set them right by leading them to obedience to Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means kindness toward them and goodness to them. ﴿And do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾, meaning: do not obey whoever disobeys Allah, and do not agree with him in his affair. The reason was that Moses, peace be upon him, had promised the Children of Israel, while they were in Egypt, that when Allah destroyed their enemy, He would bring them a Book containing a clarification of what they should do and what they should leave. When Allah did that for them, Moses asked his Lord for the Book, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to fast thirty days. When the thirty were complete, he noticed the change in his mouth's odor, so he cleaned his teeth with a stick of carob (kharrūb) wood.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: he ate from the bark of a tree, and the angels said to him: "We used to smell the scent of musk from your mouth, and you spoiled it with the siwak." So Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to fast ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, and said: "Do you not know that the odor of the mouth of one who fasts is more fragrant to Me than the scent of musk?" So their trial was in the ten that He added.

So their trial was in the ten that He added.

[136/b] The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time﴾, meaning at the time We had set for him to speak with Him. The people of tafsir (exegetical scholarship) said: When Musa, peace be upon him, came to Mount Sinai for the appointment with his Lord, he purified himself and purified his garments. In the narrative: Allah, Exalted and Majestic, sent down a darkness extending seven farsakh, drove Satan away from him, drove away the creeping creatures of the earth, removed the two angels from him, unveiled the heaven for him, and he saw the angels standing in the air and saw the Throne exposed. Allah spoke to him and conversed with him until He made him hear. Jibril, peace be upon him, was with him, but he did not hear what his Lord said to him. Then He drew him close until he heard the scratching of the Pen. Musa, peace be upon him, found the speech of his Lord sweet and longed to see Him. ﴿He said: My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: There is an ellipsis here; its implied meaning is: Show me Yourself, that I may look at You. Ibn 'Abbas said: Grant me the ability to look at You.

If it is asked: How did he ask for the vision when he knew that Allah, Exalted, cannot be seen in this world? Al-Hasan said: Longing overwhelmed him, so he asked for the vision. It is also said: He asked for the vision, supposing that it was permissible for Him to be seen in this world. ﴿He said﴾ Allah, Exalted, ﴿You will not see Me﴾. No human being can bear to look at Me in this world; whoever looks at Me in this world dies. Then Musa said: My God, I have heard Your speech, and I long to look upon You. Yet to look upon You and then die is dearer to me than to live without seeing You. Allah, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿But look at the mountain﴾, which was the greatest mountain in Madyan, called Zubayr.

Al-Suddi said: When Allah spoke to Musa, the wicked Iblis burrowed into the earth until he emerged between the feet of Musa, and he whispered to him: Could it be that a Satan is speaking to you? At that point Musa asked for the vision, and Allah, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾.

Those who deny the vision (of Allah in the Hereafter) have clung to the apparent meaning of this verse, saying: Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, and "lan" (never) denotes permanence. But there is no proof for them in it. The meaning of the verse is: You will not see Me in this world, or at present, because he was asking for the vision at that moment. And "lan" (ﻟَﻦْ) does not denote permanence, as in His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they will never wish for it, ever﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:95), reporting about the Jews. Then He informed about them that in the Hereafter they will wish for death, saying: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:77), and: ﴿Would that it had been the end﴾ (Al-Haqqah 69:27). The evidence for this is that He did not attribute to him ignorance regarding asking for the vision, nor did He say: "I am not seen," so that they would have a proof. Rather, He made the vision contingent upon the mountain remaining in its place, and the mountain remaining in its place upon being manifested is not impossible if Allah grants it that strength. What is contingent upon something that is not impossible is not impossible itself.

Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me﴾. Wahb and Ibn Ishaq said: When Musa asked his Lord for the vision, Allah sent down fog, thunderbolts, darkness, thunder and lightning, and they encompassed the mountain on which Musa was, for four farsakh on every side. Allah commanded the angels of the heaven to form ranks before Musa. So the angels of the lowest heaven passed by him like swarms of cattle, their mouths glorifying and sanctifying (Allah) with great voices like the sound of a fierce thunder. Then Allah commanded the angels of the second heaven to descend upon Musa and form ranks before him. They descended upon him like lions, with a roar of glorification and sanctification. The weak servant, Ibn Imran, was terrified by what he saw and heard, and every hair on his head and body stood on end. Then he said: I have repented of my request. Will anything deliver me from the place I am in? The best of the angels and their chief said to him: O Musa, be patient for what you asked; a little of what you have seen is a great deal.

Then Allah commanded the angels of the third heaven to descend upon Musa and form ranks before him. They descended like vultures, with a loud crashing and intense trembling, their mouths glorifying and sanctifying like the clamor of a great army, their colors like the flames of fire. Musa was terrified, his breathing grew heavy, and he despaired of life. The best of the angels said to him: Stay in your place, O son of Imran, until you see what you cannot bear. Then Allah, Exalted, commanded the angels of the fourth heaven to descend and form ranks before Musa ibn Imran. They descended upon him, unlike any of those who had passed him before. Their colors were like the flames of fire, and the rest of their bodies were like white snow. Their voices were lofty in sanctification and glorification, and no voice of those who had passed him before came close to theirs. His knees knocked together, his heart trembled, and his weeping intensified. The best of the angels and their chief said to him: O son of Imran, be patient with what you asked, for a little of what you have seen is a great deal.

Then Allah, Exalted, commanded the angels of the fifth heaven to descend and form ranks before Musa. They descended upon him having seven colors. Musa could not keep his gaze following them; he had never seen their like, nor heard the like of their voices. His inner being filled with fear, his grief intensified, and his weeping increased. The best of the angels and their chief said to him: O son of Imran, stay in your place until you see some of what you cannot bear.

Then Allah commanded the angels of the sixth heaven: Descend upon My servant who asked to see Me. They descended upon him, each angel holding in his hand something like a tall palm tree, a fire brighter than the sun. Their garments were like the flames of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, those angels who had been before them among the angels of the heavens responded to them, all of them saying with the intensity of their voices: Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of Might, Eternal, who never dies. On the head of each of those angels were four faces. When Musa saw them, he raised his voice in glorification along with them, as they glorified, weeping and saying: My Lord, remember me and do not forget Your servant. I do not know whether I will escape from what I am in or not. If I go out, I will be burned, and if I remain, I will die. The chief of the angels, the greatest among them, said to him: O son of Imran, your fear is about to intensify and your heart is about to be torn out. So be patient for what you asked.

Then Allah, Exalted, commanded that His Throne be carried by the angels of the seventh heaven. When the light of the Throne appeared, the mountain split apart from the greatness of the Lord, Majestic in His majesty. The angels of the heavens raised their voices all together, saying: Glory be to the Holy One, Lord of Might, Eternal, who never dies, with intense voices. The mountain shook, every tree in it was crushed, and the weak servant Musa fell down on his face, unconscious, with no spirit left in him. Then Allah, in His mercy, sent the Spirit, and it covered him. He turned over upon him the rock on which Musa had been, and made it like a dome so that Musa would not be burned. The Spirit raised him up like a lump of clay. Musa stood up glorifying Allah, Exalted, and saying: I have believed in You, my Lord, and I have affirmed that no one sees You and remains alive. Whoever looks at Your angels, his heart is torn out. How great You are, and how great are Your angels! You are the Lord of lords, the God of gods, and the King of kings. Nothing equals You, and nothing can stand before You. My Lord, I repent to You, and praise be to You; You have no partner. How great You are, and how sublime You are, Lord of the worlds.

That is the meaning of His saying, Exalted: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:143). Ibn 'Abbas said: The light of his Lord appeared to the mountain, the mountain of Zubayr. Al-Dahhak said: Allah manifested from the light of the veils the size of a bull's nostril. Abdullah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Only a manifestation of Allah's greatness equal to the eye of a needle reached the mountain, until it became dust. Al-Suddi said: It manifested only the size of the little finger. What supports this is what Thabit narrated from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse and said: "Like this," and he placed the thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, and the mountain crumbled. [Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, Surah al-A'raf, 8/451-452, who said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith; he also related it through 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Warraq and said: This is a hasan hadith. Al-Hakim also related it in al-Mustadrak, 2/320-321.]

It is related from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that Allah manifested a light the size of a dirham from seventy thousand veils, and it made the mountain crumble, i.e., level with the earth. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited (دَكَّاءَ) with a long vowel, without tanwin, here and in Surah al-Kahf, and Asim agreed with them in al-Kahf. The others recited (دَكًّا) with a short vowel and tanwin. For the one who reads it short, its meaning is: He made it pounded to dust, since al-Dakk and al-Daqq are the same. It is also said: Its meaning is that Allah crushed it into powder, as He said: ﴿No! When the earth is crushed, crushed to powder﴾ (Al-Fajr 89:21). For the one who reads it with the long vowel, the meaning is: He made it level, a flat ground (ardan dakkaa').

It is also said: Its meaning is that He made it like a dakkaa', which is a she-camel without a hump. Ibn 'Abbas said: He made it dust. Sufyan said: The mountain sank into the earth until it fell into the sea, and it is still moving in it. Ata' al-Awfi said: It became a vast heap of sand. Al-Kalbi said: He made it dakkaa', meaning He broke it into small mountains.

It occurs in some tafsir works: Because of His greatness, it became six mountains, three of which fell in Madinah: Uhud, Warqan, and Radwa, and three fell in Makkah: Thawr, Thabir, and Hira. [This lengthy report from Ibn Ishaq and Wahb is among the Israiliyyat (narratives of Jewish origin) in the tafsir of the verses, and it contains much incoherent material with clear signs of fabrication. Here we place the words of Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahbah commenting on this report after citing al-Baghawi's version. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "These narrations and their like, we have no doubt, are from the Israiliyyat of the Children of Israel and their lies against Allah, against the Prophets, and against the angels, so do not give them any attention. The tafsir of the verse has no need of these narrations. The verse is clear and evident, and there is nothing in it indicating the impossibility of seeing Allah in the Hereafter, as the noble Qur'an and the authentic, mutawatir Sunnah establish. At most, it indicates the impossibility of visual seeing in this world, because the perishable eye cannot perceive the enduring Essence." See: Al-Isra'iliyyat wa'l-Mawdu'at by Abu Shahbah, pp. 277-281.]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said: Stricken, swooning. Qatadah said: Dead. Al-Kalbi said: Musa fell unconscious on Thursday, the Day of 'Arafah, and was given the Torah on Friday, the Day of Sacrifice.

Al-Waqidi said: When Musa fell unconscious, the angels of the heavens said: What has the son of Imran to do with asking for the vision? In some books [This too is among the fabricated Israiliyyat, and it agrees with the nature of the Children of Israel and their attitude toward the Prophets, their prolonging their tongues with evil against them and belittling them as much as they could. See: Tafsir al-Alusi, 9/46.] it is related that the angels of the heavens came to Musa while he was unconscious, and they began kicking him with their feet, saying: O son of the menstruating women, did you hope to see the Lord of Might?

﴿Then when he regained consciousness﴾: when Musa came out of his swoon and his reason returned, he realized that he had asked for something that was not fitting for him. ﴿He said: Glory be to You! I repent to You﴾ from asking for the vision. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾ that You cannot be seen in this world. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: I am the first among the Children of Israel to believe in You.

He said, "O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech; so take what I have given you and be among the thankful." ﴿O Musa, I have chosen you above the people﴾: I selected you above the people. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "إِنِّيَ" (*inniya*, "indeed I") with a fatha on the yā' (the final letter), and likewise "أَخِيَ اشْدُدْ" (*akhiya ushdud*, "my brother, strengthen") in Taha 31. "بِرِسَالَاتِي" (*bi-risalati*, "by My messages"): the people of the Hijaz read "بِرِسَالَتِي" (*bi-risalati*, "by My message") in the singular, as a collective noun of unity (tawhid), while the others read it in the plural. "فَخُذْ مَا آتَيْتُكَ" (*fa-khudh ma ataytuka*, "so take what I have given you"): what I gave you. "وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ" (*wa kun mina al-shakirin*, "and be among the thankful"): to God for His blessings.

If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying, "I have chosen you above the people by My messages," when others were also given messages? It is answered: since the message was not general for all people, His saying "I have chosen you above the people" is correct, even though others shared it with him. This is like a man saying, "I have singled you out with my counsel," even though he consulted others too; when the consultation was not general, the statement is correct.

According to part of the narration, after his Lord spoke to him, Musa (peace be upon him) could not be looked at by anyone because of the light that covered his face, and he kept a veil over his face until he died. His wife said to him, "I have been a *ayyim* (a woman without a husband, *ayyim* from *ayama*, "to be without a mate") from you since your Lord spoke to you." So he uncovered his face for her, and a ray like the rays of the sun struck her. She put her hand over her face and went out prostrating to God, and said, "Pray to God that He make me your wife in Paradise." He said, "That is yours, if you do not marry after me, for a woman belongs to her last husband."

Abu Sa'id al-Sharihi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Muzakki informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj narrated to us: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Rashid ibn As'ad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Mughafiri narrated to us, from his father, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, that Musa looked into the Torah and said, "I find a nation, the best of nations, brought forth for mankind, who enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, believe in God, in the first Book and in the last Book, and fight the people of misguidance until they fight the one-eyed Dajjal. My Lord, make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Muhammad, O Musa." He said, "My Lord, I find a nation who praise (God) much, the guardians of the sun, who take decisions, and when they intend a matter they say, 'We will do it, if God wills.' So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Muhammad." He said, "My Lord, I find a nation who eat their expiations and their charities; the earlier ones used to burn their charities with fire. They are those who respond and those to whom response is given, the intercessors and those for whom intercession is made. So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Muhammad." He said, "My Lord, I find a nation that, when one of them ascends a height, says *takbir* (Allahu akbar), and when he descends into a valley, praises God. The earth is a purifier for them and a place of prayer wherever they are. They purify themselves from major impurity, and their purification with earth is like their purification with water where they cannot find water. They are radiant, with marks of ablution. So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Muhammad." He said, "My Lord, I find a nation that, when one of them intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is written for him equal to it; and if he does it, ten times its equivalent is written for him, up to seven hundred times. And when one of them intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is written against him; and if he does it, only one equal evil is written against him. So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Ahmad." He said, "My Lord, I find a nation that is merciful and weak, who inherit the Book from those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; among them is one who wrongs himself, among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds. I find none of them except as one shown mercy. So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Muhammad." He said, "O my Lord, I find a nation whose *masahif* (the copies of their scriptures, [in variant "ب": their Gospels]) are in their chests, who wear the colours of the garments of the people of Paradise, who form rows in their prayer like the rows of the angels, whose voices in their mosques are like the humming of bees, and none of whom will ever enter the Fire, except one who sees the reckoning as one sees a stone from behind a barrier. So make them my nation." He said, "They are the nation of Ahmad." When Musa marvelled at the good that God gave Muhammad (ﷺ) and his nation, he said, "Would that I were one of the companions of Muhammad and his nation!" God revealed to him three verses to satisfy him with them: "O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech," up to His saying, "I will show you the abode of the defiant. And among the people of Musa is a nation who guide by the truth and by it act justly." So Musa was fully content.

[Footnote: Al-Suyuti attributed it to Abu Nu'aym in *al-Dala'il*, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Mughafiri, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, as a *mawquf* report (a statement ending with Ka'b himself). See *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 3/557-558. Similar wording was also transmitted by al-Tabari, from Qatada, as the occasion of revelation for His saying, "And he threw down the Tablets" (7:150). Al-Baghawi did not mention that in his narration. Ibn 'Atiyya al-Andalusi said in his *Tafsir* (6/87): "This is a poor opinion that should not be ascribed to Musa (peace be upon him)." Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatada a strange statement in this regard, whose chain does not validly go back to Qatada's report. Ibn 'Atiyya and many scholars have rejected it, and it deserves rejection. Qatada probably received it from some of the People of the Book, among whom are liars, fabricators, impostors and heretics." See *Tafsir Ibn Kathir*: 2/249. Al-Qurtubi said: "There is no regard for what is reported from Qatada, even if it is authentic. It is not valid that the throwing down of the Tablets was because of what he saw of the excellence of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that this was not for his own nation. This is a poor opinion that should not be attributed to Musa (peace be upon him)." See *Tafsir al-Qurtubi*: 7/288.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 145:**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We wrote for him﴾, meaning for Musa (Moses), ﴿on the Tablets﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means the Tablets of the Tawrah (Torah). A hadith states: "They were of the lote-tree of Paradise, and the length of the Tablet was twelve cubits" [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/548.]]. There also came, in the narrations about God creating Adam with His own hand: "He wrote the Tawrah with His hand and planted the tree of Tuba with His hand" [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat Ahl al-Jannah and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah, and al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat: 2/47, "Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, created three things with His hand: He created Adam with His hand, He wrote the Tawrah with His hand, and He planted the Paradise (al-Firdaws) with His hand," and said: This is mursal.]].

Al-Hasan said: The Tablets were of wood. Al-Kalbi [137/b] said: They were of green emerald (zabarjad). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They were of red ruby (yaqut). Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The Tablets were of crystal (bard). Ibn Jurayj said: They were of emerald (zumurrud). God commanded Jibril until he brought them from 'Adn, and they were written with the Pen with which the Reminder (al-Dhikr) was written, and the ink was drawn from the River of Light. Wahb said: God commanded him to cut the Tablets from a solid rock, which God softened for him, so he cut them with his hand and then split them with his finger. Musa heard the scratching of the Pen with the Ten Words. That was on the first day of Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the Tablets were ten cubits long, according to the height of Musa. Muqatil and Wahb said: ﴿And We wrote for him on the Tablets﴾ like the engraving of a seal-ring. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The Tawrah was sent down, and it was seventy camel-loads, of which a portion was read in a year, and only four men read it: Musa, Yusha' (Joshua), 'Uzayr (Ezra), and 'Isa (Jesus).

Al-Hasan said: This verse in the Tawrah is a thousand verses, meaning ﴿And We wrote for him on the Tablets﴾ ﴿of everything﴾ of what they were commanded and forbidden, ﴿an admonition﴾, a prohibition of ignorance. The real meaning of admonition (mawi'zah) is reminder and warning with what one fears its consequence, ﴿and a detailed explanation of everything﴾, that is, a clarification of everything of the command and prohibition, the lawful and the unlawful, the prescribed punishments (hudud) and the rulings (ahkam).

﴿So take it with strength﴾, that is, with earnestness and diligence. It was said: with the strength of the heart and soundness of resolve, because if one takes it with weakness of intention, it leads to slackness. ﴿And command your people, they should take the best of it﴾. 'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They should make lawful its lawful things, forbid its unlawful things, reflect upon its parables, act upon its clear (muhkam) verses, and stop at its ambiguous (mutashabih) verses. Musa, peace be upon him, was more devoted in worship than his people, so he was commanded with what they were not commanded.

Qutrub said: "the best of it" means "its goodness," and all of it is good. It was also said: the best of it is the obligatory duties (fara'id) and the supererogatory acts (nawafil), which are what merit reward, and what is below them is the permissible (mubah), because no reward is merited for it. It was also said: "the best of it" means the better of two matters in every case, such as pardon being better than retaliation (qisas), and patience being better than retaliating.

﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾. Mujahid said: Its destination in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: It means Hell (Jahannam), warning you not to be like them. Qatadah and others said: "I will bring you to al-Sham and show you the dwellings of the past generations who opposed God's command, so that you may take heed from them." 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He meant the abode of Pharaoh and his people, which is Egypt, as evidenced by the reading of Qassamah ibn Zuhayr: "sa-uwarikum dara al-fasiqin" (I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient). As-Suddi said: The abode of the defiantly disobedient is the place where the disbelievers were overthrown. Al-Kalbi said: It is what they passed by when they traveled, of the dwellings of 'Ad and Thamud and the generations who were destroyed.

I will translate the passage faithfully.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means those who tyrannize over My servants and wage war against My friends, so that they do not believe in Me. Meaning: I will turn them away from accepting My signs and affirming them. They are punished by being deprived of guidance, because of their obstinacy toward the truth, like His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: I will prevent them from understanding the Qur'an. Ibn Jurayj said: It means regarding the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, i.e., I will turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking lessons from them. It was also said: The ruling of this verse applies specifically to the people of Egypt, and by "the signs" he meant the nine signs which Allah the Exalted gave to Musa (peace be upon him). But most scholars hold that the verse is general: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of guidance﴾ [i.e., these arrogant ones] ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "al-Rashad" (الرَّشَدِ) with a fatha on the ra' and the shin, while the others read it with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the shin. Both are dialectal variants, like al-suqm and al-saqam, al-bukhl and al-bakhal, and al-huzn and al-hazan.

Abu 'Amr used to distinguish between them, saying: al-rushd (with a damma) means righteousness in affairs, and al-rashad (with a fatha) means uprightness in religion. The meaning of the verse: if they see the path of guidance and rectitude, they will not take it ﴿as a way﴾ for themselves; ﴿and if they see the way of error﴾, i.e., the path of misguidance, ﴿they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾, heedless of reflecting upon them and being admonished by them, heedless and inattentive.

﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾, i.e., the meeting of the Last Abode, which is the appointed place of reward and punishment, ﴿their deeds have become void﴾, nullified and become as though they had never been. ﴿Are they recompensed﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿except for what they used to do﴾, i.e., except for the recompense of what they ﴿used to do﴾ in this world.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 148–149:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And the people of Moses took, after him﴾, i.e., after his departure to the mountain, ﴿from their ornaments﴾ which they had borrowed from the people of Pharaoh. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿min ḥilyihim﴾ with a kasrah on the ḥa'. [Ya'qub recited it with a fatha on the ḥa' and a sukun on the lam.] [[Omitted from "A" and restored from "B".]] ﴿And the Samiri made from them a calf﴾, and he cast into its mouth some dust from the hoofprint of Jibril, peace be upon him, so it turned into a calf, ﴿a body﴾, living, with flesh and blood, ﴿which lowed﴾. The lowing (khuwar) is the sound of cattle. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and a group of the people of tafsir.

It was said: it was a fashioned body of gold with no spirit in it, from which a sound would be heard.

It was said: what was heard was the sound of the wind's rustling entering its hollow and leaving it. The first view is the most sound.

It was said: it lowed only once. It was also said: it lowed frequently, and whenever it lowed they prostrated to it, and when it fell silent they raised their heads. Wahb said: the lowing was heard from it while it did not move.

Al-Suddi said: it would low and walk. ﴿Did they not see﴾, meaning those who worshipped the calf, ﴿that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way?﴾ Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They took it, and they were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., they took it as a god, and they were disbelievers.

﴿And when they were overcome with remorse (suqita fi aydihim)﴾, i.e., they regretted worshipping the calf. The Arabs say of everyone who regrets a matter: "suqita fi yadayhi" (he has been struck in his hands, i.e., has fallen into regret). ﴿And when they saw that they had gone astray, they said: "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us﴾, i.e., does not turn to us in repentance, ﴿and forgive us﴾, i.e., does not overlook our sin, ﴿we will surely be among the losers."﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "tarhamna wa-taghfir lana" with a ta' in both, and "Rabbana" with the ba' in the accusative. This remorse and seeking of forgiveness on their part occurred after Moses returned to them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 150–151:

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿When Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾. Abu al-Darda' said: "al-Asif is one of intense anger." Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: "Asifan means grieved." Al-asaf (grief) is the most intense sorrow. ﴿He said, "Evil is what you have done in my absence after me."﴾ That is: how wrong is what you did after my departure. It is said: "He left him (khalafahu) with good or evil" when he left him in charge of his family after departing from them, with good or evil. ﴿Did you hasten﴾ meaning, did you get ahead of ﴿the command of your Lord?﴾ al-Hasan said: "The promise of your Lord, which He made to you, of the forty nights." al-Kalbi said: "Did you hasten into worshipping the calf before the command of your Lord came to you?"

﴿And he threw down the Tablets﴾, in which was the Torah, and he had been carrying them, so he threw them to the ground out of intense anger.

The narrators said: The Torah was in seven sevenths. When he threw the Tablets, they broke, so six-sevenths of it were lifted up and one-seventh remained. Thus what was among the reports of the unseen was lifted, and what remained was the admonition, the rulings, and the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head﴾, by his locks of hair and his beard, ﴿dragging him toward himself.﴾ Harun was three years older than Musa and was more beloved to the Children of Israel than Musa, because he was gentle in anger.

﴿He said﴾, Harun at that point, ﴿"Son of my mother"﴾. The people of Kufa and Syria read it here and in Ta-Ha with a kasra on the mim, meaning "O son of my mother," dropping the possessive yā' while the kasra remains to indicate the possessive, as in His saying "O My servants" (yā 'ibādi). The people of the Hijaz, Basra, and Hafs read it with a fatha on the mim, meaning "O son of my mother" (yā ibna ummāh).

It is also said: he made it one word and built it on fatha, like their saying Hadramawt and Khamsata 'ashar (fifteen), and similar. He said "son of my mother," though Harun was his full brother, in order to soften him and win his sympathy.

It is also said: he was his brother only through the mother, not the father. ﴿Indeed, the people overpowered me﴾, meaning the calf-worshippers, ﴿and they nearly killed me﴾, meaning they intended it and came close to killing me. ﴿So do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me﴾ in your reckoning against me ﴿among the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning the calf-worshippers.

﴿He said﴾, Musa, when the excuse of his brother became clear to him: ﴿"My Lord, forgive me"﴾ for what I did to my brother, ﴿and my brother"﴾, if there was any shortcoming on his part in denouncing the calf-worshippers, ﴿"and admit us both"﴾ together ﴿"into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 152–154:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾, i.e., they took it as a god, ﴿will certainly receive anger from their Lord﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and humiliation in the worldly life﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: It is what they were commanded regarding the killing of themselves. And 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: "Indeed, those who took the calf" refers to the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; He reproached them for the deeds of their fathers and attributed it to them: ﴿will certainly receive anger from their Lord and humiliation in the worldly life﴾. He meant what befell the Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir of killing and expulsion.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: It is the jizyah (poll tax). ﴿And thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾, the liars. Abu Qilabah said: By Allah, it is the recompense of every fabricator until the Day of Resurrection, that Allah humiliates him. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: This applies to every innovator until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And when the anger subsided﴾, i.e., calmed, ﴿from Musa, he took up the tablets﴾ which he had thrown down, and six-sevenths of them had gone; ﴿and in their inscription﴾ they differed concerning it. It was said: He meant by it the tablets, because they were copied (nusikhat) from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

It was also said: When Musa threw the tablets, they broke, so he copied another copy from them, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and in their inscription﴾.

It was also said: He meant: "and in what was copied from them." 'Ata' said: "in what remained of them." Ibn 'Abbas and 'Amr ibn Dinar said: When Musa threw the tablets and they broke, he fasted for forty days, and they were returned to him in two tablets, and in them was ﴿guidance and mercy﴾, i.e., guidance from misguidance and mercy from punishment, ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾, i.e., for those who are fearful of their Lord. Al-Kisa'i said: Since it preceded the verb, it is good, like His saying: (lil-ru'ya ta'burun) [Yusuf: 43]. Qutrub said: He meant "from their Lord they fear." It was said: He meant "fearing" (rahibun). It was said: He meant "fearing for their Lord" (rahibun li-rabbihim).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 155:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time﴾. That is, from among his people, so it is in the accusative by removing the preposition (harf al-sifah). ﴿Seventy men for Our appointed time﴾. In this there is evidence that not all of them worshipped the calf. Al-Suddi said: Allah, Exalted is He, commanded Musa to come to Him with some men of the Children of Israel who would apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, so Musa chose from his people seventy men. ﴿So when﴾ they came to that place, they said: "We will never believe you until we see Allah openly," so the thunderbolt (al-sa'iqah) seized them and they died.

Ibn Ishaq said: He chose them so that they would repent to Him for what their people had done, and ask for repentance on behalf of those whom they had left behind among their people. This indicates that all of them had worshipped the calf.

Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿The quake (al-rajfah) seized them﴾ because they had not separated themselves from their people when they worshipped the calf, and they had not enjoined upon them what is right nor forbidden them what is wrong.

Ibn Abbas said: The seventy who said, "We will never believe you until we see Allah openly, and the thunderbolt seized them" (Al-Baqarah 2:55), were before the seventy who were seized by the quake. Allah, Exalted is He, commanded Musa, peace be upon him, to choose seventy men from his people, so he chose them and went out with them to supplicate their Lord. Among what they supplicated was that they said: "O Allah, give us what You have not given anyone before us, and do not give it to anyone after us." Allah disliked this supplication of theirs, so the quake seized them.

Wahb said: The quake was not a sound, but when the people saw that awesome majesty, trembling and agitation seized them, and they shook until their joints nearly came apart. When Musa saw that, he had mercy on them and feared death for them, and the loss of them weighed heavily upon him, for they had been his helpers in good, listening and obedient. At that, he supplicated, wept, and implored his Lord, so Allah removed that quake from them, they became calm, and they heard the speech of their Lord. This is His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿He said﴾, meaning Musa: ﴿"My Lord, had You willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me"﴾, meaning because of the worship of the calf, ﴿"and me"﴾ because of the killing of the Copt.

﴿"Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?"﴾

Meaning the worshippers of the calf. Musa thought that they were being punished for taking the calf, and he said this by way of asking: "Will You destroy us for the deed of the foolish?"

Al-Mubarrad said: His saying, "Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?" is a question of entreaty (istif'at isti'tf), meaning: do not destroy us. Musa, peace be upon him, knew that Allah, Exalted is He, is too just to take one person to account for the crime of another.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"It is none but Your trial"﴾, that is, the one into which the foolish fell. It was only Your test and Your affliction. You led astray with it some people, so they were tempted, and You guided some people, so You preserved them until they remained steadfast in Your religion. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿"You lead astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector (waliyyuna), our Helper and Guardian, so forgive us, have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers."﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 156–157:**

﴿And ordain for us﴾, i.e., make obligatory for us, ﴿in this world a good﴾, namely blessing and well-being, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., and in the Hereafter, ﴿a good﴾, i.e., forgiveness and Paradise. ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, i.e., we have repented to You. ﴿He said﴾, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will﴾ of My creation, ﴿but My mercy encompasses all things﴾, i.e., it has covered all things. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: His mercy encompassed the righteous and the wicked in this world, but on the Day of Resurrection it will be for the God-fearing alone.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said: It encompasses all things, but it is not made obligatory except for those who fear God. That is because the disbeliever is provided for, and harm is averted from him on account of the believers, due to the vastness of God's mercy toward the believers. So he lives within it. When he reaches the Hereafter, it becomes obligatory for the believers alone, like one who benefits from the light of another's fire when the owner of the lamp takes his lamp away.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: When the verse "and My mercy encompasses all things" was revealed, Iblis said: "I am part of that thing." Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿So I will ordain it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our signs﴾. The Jews and Christians wished for it and said: "We fear God, we believe, and we give zakah." So Allah made it for this community, and He said:

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾, to the end of the verse.

Nawf al-Bakali al-Himyari said: When Musa (peace be upon him) chose seventy men from his people, Allah the Exalted said to Musa: "I will make the earth for you a place of prostration and a means of purification. You may pray wherever prayer reaches you, except at a latrine, a bathhouse, or a grave. I will place tranquility in your hearts, and I will make you recite the Torah from memory. Man and woman, free and slave, young and old will recite it." Musa said this to his people, but they said: "We do not want to pray except in churches, we cannot bear tranquility in our hearts, we cannot recite the Torah from memory, and we do not want to read it except by looking at it." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So I will ordain it for those who fear Me and give zakah﴾, up to His saying: "Those are the successful" [7:157]. So Allah made it for this community. Then Musa (peace be upon him) said: "My Lord, make me their prophet." He said: "Their prophet is from among them." He said: "My Lord, make me one of them." He said: "You will not reach them." Musa (peace be upon him) said: "My Lord, I brought to You the delegation of the Children of Israel, yet You have made our delegation for others." So Allah the Exalted revealed: (And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly) [7:159], and Musa was pleased. [[The narration of Nawf al-Bakali is among the Isra'iliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin). Nawf was a narrator of stories, and he was the stepson of Ka'b al-Ahbar. He has an entry in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib. See below the commentary on the occasion of revelation of this verse in the surah, p. (291).]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾, and he is Muhammad ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: He is your Prophet. He was unlettered, neither writing, nor reading, nor calculating. The Prophet ﷺ said: "We are an unlettered nation; we do not write and we do not calculate." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fasting, chapter on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not write and we do not calculate," 4/126, and Muslim in Fasting, chapter on the obligation of fasting Ramadan upon sighting the crescent..., no. (1080), 2/761. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/228 from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).]] The word "ummi" is attributed to "umm" (mother), meaning he is as his mother bore him. It was also said that it is attributed to his "umma" (community), its original form being "ummati," and the "ta'" was dropped in the relative form, as it was dropped in "Makki" and "Madani." It was also said: it is attributed to Umm al-Qura, which is Makkah.

﴿Whom they find written﴾, i.e., they find his description, his attributes and his prophethood, ﴿with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us that Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] told us: Muhammad ibn Sinan told us: Fulayh told us: Hilal told us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: I met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and I said: "Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Torah." He said: "Indeed, by Allah, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur'an: 'O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner, and a guardian for the unlettered. You are My servant and My Messenger. I have named you al-Mutawakkil (the one who relies upon Allah). He is not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repel evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. Allah will not take him until He sets right through him the crooked community, so that they say: There is no god but Allah, and through him He will open blind eyes, deaf ears, and veiled hearts.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Sales, chapter on disliking clamor in the markets: 4/342-343, and in the commentary of Surah al-Fath, chapter on "Indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bearer of good news and a warner" 8/585.]]

Another narration: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah followed him, from Hilal, from 'Ata', from Ibn Salam. Al-Imam al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysafuni informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Bistam informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sayyar al-Qurashi informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman told us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from 'Abd Allah ibn Damrah, from Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I find in the Torah written: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; he is not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and overlooks. His community are the praisers who praise Allah in every situation and magnify Him at every elevation. They gird their waists upon their midsections and wash their extremities. Their rows in prayer and their rows in battle are equal. Their caller calls out in the atmosphere of the sky. In the depth of the night they have a hum like the hum of bees. His birth is in Makkah, his emigration is to Taba, and his kingdom is in Syria." [[Narrated by al-Darimi in the Introduction, chapter on the description of the Prophet ﷺ in the books before his mission: 1/5; Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat: 1/360; al-Baghawi in al-Masabih: 4/36; and see Mishkat al-Masabih: 3/1607.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He enjoins upon them what is right﴾, i.e., faith, ﴿and forbids them from what is wrong﴾, i.e., from polytheism. It was also said: "what is right" means the Shari'ah (divine law) and the Sunnah (prophetic practice), and "what is wrong" means what is not recognized in Shari'ah or Sunnah. 'Ata' said: He enjoins them to what is right: to renounce rivals (to God), noble character, and maintaining ties of kinship; and He forbids them from what is wrong: from worshipping idols and severing ties of kinship.

﴿And makes lawful for them the good things﴾, meaning what they used to prohibit in the time of ignorance, such as the bahirah, the saibah, the wasilah, and the ham. ﴿And prohibits for them the evil things﴾, meaning carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, fornication, and other prohibited things.

﴿And lifts from them their burden﴾. Ibn 'Amir read "aşarahum" in the plural. The "isr" is everything that weighs heavily upon a person, whether a saying or an action.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: It means the heavy covenant that was taken from the Children of Israel to act upon what is in the Torah.

Qatadah said: It means the strictness that was upon them in religion. ﴿And the shackles﴾, meaning the burdens ﴿that were upon them﴾, such as: killing oneself as repentance, cutting off the sinning limbs, cutting off impurity from a garment with scissors, specifying retaliation for killing while prohibiting accepting blood money, abstaining from work on the Sabbath, that their prayer is valid only in churches, and other hardships. They were likened to shackles that bind the hand to the neck.

﴿So those who believed in him﴾, i.e., in Muhammad ﷺ,

﴿and honored him﴾, i.e., revered him, ﴿and supported him﴾ against the enemies, ﴿and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿those are the successful﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: It means the heavy covenant that was taken from the Children of Israel to act upon what is in the Torah.

Qatadah said: It means the strictness that was upon them in religion. ﴿And the shackles﴾, meaning the burdens ﴿that were upon them﴾, such as: killing oneself as repentance, cutting off the sinning limbs, cutting off impurity from a garment with scissors, specifying retaliation for killing while prohibiting accepting blood money, abstaining from work on the Sabbath, that their prayer is valid only in churches, and other hardships. They were likened to shackles that bind the hand to the neck.

﴿So those who believed in him﴾, i.e., in Muhammad ﷺ,

﴿and honored him﴾, i.e., revered him, ﴿and supported him﴾ against the enemies, ﴿and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿those are the successful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 158–159:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from] He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet who believes in Allah and His words﴾ — i.e., His signs, and these are the Qur'an. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: it means Jesus, son of Mary, and it is read "kalimatihi" (His word, singular): ﴿and follow him that you may be guided﴾.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And among the people of Moses﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel — ﴿is a community﴾, i.e., a group, ﴿who guide by truth﴾, i.e., they give guidance and call to the truth. It was also said: the meaning is that they are guided and remain upright upon it, ﴿and by it they do justice﴾, i.e., they judge by the truth and stand up for justice. Al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi' said: they are a people beyond China, at the farthest east, on a river [flowing with sand] [[In some copies: (the course of the sand).]] called the River of Awdaf. None of them has property apart from his companion; they are rained upon at night and see the sun by day; they sow crops, and none of us can reach them; and they are upon the truth [[See: al-Tabari: 13/173-174; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 4/406.]].

It is mentioned that Gabriel, peace be upon him, took the Prophet ﷺ on the night of his Night Journey, and he spoke to them [Gabriel said to them: "Do you know whom you are speaking to?" They said: "No." He said: "This is Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, so believe in him."] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "B".]] They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Moses, peace be upon him, instructed us that whoever among you reaches Ahmad should convey to him our greetings." The Prophet ﷺ returned the greeting to Moses and to them, then he recited to them ten surahs of the Qur'an that were revealed in Makkah, and commanded them to pray and to give zakat, and commanded them to remain in their places. They used to observe the Sabbath, so he commanded them to gather (for worship) and to abandon the Sabbath [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/586; Ruh al-Ma'ani of al-Alusi: 9/84.]].

It was also said: they are those among the Jews who embraced Islam in the time of the Prophet ﷺ [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 4/406.]]. The first view is more sound [[The reports that the author - may Allah have mercy on him - cited in the interpretation of this verse are among the Isra'iliyyat, which, even if their chains are authentic up to those who narrated them, are not to be relied upon in these unseen matters for which there is no text in the Book or the Sunnah. Ibn 'Atiyyah considered them improbable in his tafsir "al-Muharrar al-Wajiz": 6/109. And al-Alusi said in Ruh al-Ma'ani: 9/85, "Ibn al-Khazin weakened this narration, and I do not regard it as anything, nor do I think you will find for it a chain on which one can rely, even if you sought a tunnel in the earth or a ladder to the sky." For this reason we record here the summary of what Ibn Kathir - may Allah have mercy on him - said in the interpretation of this noble verse: "Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the Children of Israel that among them is a group who follow the truth and act justly by it, as He, exalted is He, said: 'Among the People of the Scripture is a short-legged community...' [Qur'an 3:113] and He, exalted is He, said: 'And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah; they do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account' [Qur'an 3:199]..." Then he indicated the narration of Ibn Jarir and said: "Ibn Jarir has mentioned in its interpretation a wondrous report." Likewise Ibn 'Atiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, gave his opinion on the interpretation of the verse, saying: It may be that he means the description of the righteous believers among the Children of Israel in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, and the period following him... And it may be that he means the group among the Children of Israel who believed in Muhammad ﷺ, by way of drawing in the faith of all of them." See: al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 6/108-109; al-Isra'iliyyat wa'l-Mawdu'at by Abu Shuhbah, pp. 291-292.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 160–162:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And We divided them﴾, meaning: We separated them, namely the Children of Israel, ﴿into twelve tribes, as nations﴾.

Al-Farra' said: He said "twelve" (ithnatay 'ashrata), while the word sibt (tribe) is masculine, because He said "umaman" (nations), so the feminine was referred back to the nations. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "And We divided them into twelve nations," and He said "asbatan umaman" (tribes, nations) with the plural, and what is above ten is not explained by the plural. Thus one does not say "atani ithna 'ashara rijalan" (twelve men came to me with the plural). In reality, "asbat" is an adjective (na't) of the omitted specifier, which is "firqa" (group), meaning: "And We divided them into twelve groups, nations."

It was also said: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its estimate being: "And We divided them into tribes, nations, twelve." The asbat (tribes) are the clans, and the singular of it is sibt.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water﴾ in the wilderness (al-tih), ﴿"Strike the rock with your staff," so there gushed forth﴾ inbajasat, meaning burst forth (infajarat). Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: it became moist with sweat, and that is al-inbijas, then it burst forth. ﴿From it twelve springs﴾, one spring for each tribe, ﴿Each group knew its drinking place﴾, each tribe, ﴿and each tribe were the sons of one father.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And We shaded them with the clouds﴾ in the wilderness, protecting them from the heat of the sun, ﴿and We sent down upon them manna and quails. "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you." And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾

﴿And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, 'Hittah (relief),' and enter the gate prostrating, We will forgive you your sins."﴾ The people of Madina, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "naghfir" with a ta' and a damma and a fath on the fa'. The others read it with a nun, a fath, and a kasra on the fa'. ﴿Your sins (khati'atikum)﴾: Ibn 'Amir read "khati'atakum" in the singular with a raised ta'; Abu 'Amr read "khataya-kum"; the people of Madina and Ya'qub read "khati'atikum" in the plural with a raised ta'. [What is between the brackets is omitted from "b".] The others read in the plural with a kasra on the ta'. ﴿We will surely increase the doers of good﴾.

﴿So those who did wrong among them changed the word from what had been said to them, and We sent upon them a punishment (rijz) from the sky because they were wronging.﴾ Rijz means punishment (adhab).
