The Qur'anic verse and the question of the town's location

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. It was said: it is Madyan. [That is: O Muhammad, ask these Jews, who are your neighbours, a question of rebuke and reproach, about the town that was by the sea] [[Addition from "B".]] That is, near it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is a town called Ayla (Ilah), between Madyan and al-Tur, on the shore of the sea. Al-Zuhri said: it is Tiberias of Syria (Tabariyyat al-Sham).

﴿When they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, that is, they wronged in it and exceeded God's command by hunting fish. ﴿When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day openly on the water, in great numbers﴾: shurraʿan (شُرَّعًا) is the plural of shari (شَارِع), meaning visible and surfacing on the water. Al-Dahhak said: it means successive.

In the story: they would come to them on the Sabbath day like fat white rams.

﴿But on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, as they had come on the Sabbath day. Al-Hasan recited "lā yusbitūn" (لَا يُسْبِتُونَ) with a damma on the yāʾ, meaning they do not enter upon the Sabbath. The well-known reading has a fatha on the yāʾ (لَا يَسْبِتُونَ), and its meaning is: they do not hold the Sabbath in honour. ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, We tried them, ﴿for their defiance﴾.

Then Satan whispered to them and said: God has not forbidden you from hunting, He has only forbidden you from eating, so hunt. Or it was said: he whispered to them that you have only been forbidden from taking, so they made a ḥayḍ (حَيْضًا), an enclosure, on the shore of the sea, driving the fish into it on the Sabbath, and then taking them on Sunday. They did this for a time, then grew bold toward the Sabbath and said: we see that the Sabbath has only been made lawful for us, so they took, ate and sold. The people of the town then became three groups, and they numbered about seventy thousand. One third forbade it; one third did not forbid it and stayed silent, saying: why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy? And one third were the people of the sin. When they would not desist, those who forbade said: we will not live with you in one town. So they divided the town by a wall: for the Muslims a gate, and for the transgressors a gate. Dawud, peace be upon him, cursed them. Then one morning the forbidders found that not one of the transgressors had come out. They said: something has happened to them; perhaps wine has overcome them. So they climbed over the wall, and behold, they were monkeys. The monkeys recognised their own kin among the humans, but the humans did not recognise their kin among the monkeys. The monkeys began to come to their relatives among the humans, sniffing their clothes and weeping. He would say: did we not forbid you? And it would nod its head and say: yes. None were saved except those who forbade, and the rest of them perished.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 164–165:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?"﴾ They differed about those who said this. It was said: They were from the doomed group. That is because when they were told, "Desist from this evil deed, before the punishment descends upon you, for we know that Allah will send down His might upon you if you do not desist," they responded and said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?" [Or] "whom You know Allah will punish with a severe punishment." They said, ﴿"An excuse before your Lord."﴾ That is, those who forbade said, "Our admonition is an excuse" (ma'dhira, i.e., ma'dhiratun). Hafs read *ma'dhiratan* with a fatha, meaning: "We do this as an excuse before your Lord." The more correct view is that it is the saying of the group that remained silent. They said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?" and they said, "An excuse before your Lord." The meaning is that enjoining good is obligatory upon us, so admonishing these people is upon us as an excuse before Allah. ﴿"And perhaps they will fear Allah."﴾ That is, they will fear Allah and abandon disobedience. Had the address been to the transgressors, it would have said, "perhaps you will fear."

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ That is, they abandoned what they had been admonished with, ﴿We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who had wronged with a severe punishment﴾ meaning the disobedient group, ﴿with a severe punishment﴾ That is, harsh and painful, from *ba's* (ba's), which is severity.

The reciters differed regarding it. The people of Medina and Ibn Amir read *bi-ya'sin* with a kasra on the ba', on the pattern *fi'il*, except that Ibn Amir pronounces it with a hamza, while Abu Ja'far and Nafi' do not pronounce the hamza. Asim, in the transmission of Abu Bakr, read it with a fatha on the ba', a sukun on the ya', and a fatha on the hamza, on the pattern *fay'al*, like *sayqal*. The others read it on the pattern *fa'il*, like *ba'ir* and *saghir*.

﴿Because they used to defy (yafsuqun)﴾ Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "I hear Allah say, 'We saved those who forbade evil and We seized those who had wronged with a severe punishment,' but I do not know what happened to the silent group." Ikrimah said: I said to him, "May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they denounced and disliked what those people were doing, and said, 'Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?' And if Allah had not said, 'We saved them,' He would not have said, 'We destroyed them.'" So Ibn Abbas was pleased with my words, approved, and ordered that two cloaks be given to me, and he clothed me with them.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: The two groups were saved: those who said, "Why do you admonish a people?" and those who said, "An excuse before your Lord." Allah destroyed those who took the fish. This is the view of al-Hasan.

Ibn Zayd said: The one who forbade was saved, and both of the other groups were destroyed. This is the most severe verse concerning abandoning the forbidding of what is evil.

And if Allah had not said, 'We saved them,' He would not have said, 'We destroyed them.'" So Ibn Abbas was pleased with my words, approved, and ordered that two cloaks be given to me, and he clothed me with them.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: The two groups were saved: those who said, "Why do you admonish a people?" and those who said, "An excuse before your Lord." Allah destroyed those who took the fish. This is the view of al-Hasan.

Ibn Zayd said: The one who forbade was saved, and both of the other groups were destroyed. This is the most severe verse concerning abandoning the forbidding of what is evil.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 166–167:

Allah's statement: ﴿So when they defied what they had been forbidden﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they refused to turn back from disobedience. ﴿We said to them: "Be apes, despised and driven away."﴾

[They were] banished. They remained for three days while people looked at them, and then they perished.

﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾, i.e., your Lord announced and made known. It is said: ta'adhdhana and adhdhana, like: tawa'ada and awada (both meaning to warn/threaten). Ibn 'Abbas said: "Your Lord proclaimed" means "your Lord said." Mujahid said: "Your Lord commanded." 'Ata' said: "Your Lord decreed."

﴿He will surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who will afflict them with a terrible torment﴾, i.e., against the Jews. Allah sent against them Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, who fight them until they embrace Islam or pay the jizya (poll tax). ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 168–169:**

﴿And We divided them﴾ and scattered them ﴿throughout the earth as communities﴾, groups. God divided them, so their affair was dispersed and no unified word ever came together for them. ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: this refers to those who lived to see the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and believed in him. ﴿And among them are others below that﴾, meaning those who remained upon disbelief.

Al-Kalbi said: "Among them are the righteous" are those who are beyond the river Awdaf, from beyond China [[See the previous note at the end of the tafsir (exegesis) of verse (159) of this surah. p. (291).]]. ﴿And among them are others below that﴾ means: those here among the Jews. ﴿And We tested them with good things﴾, with fertility and well-being, ﴿and bad things﴾, with drought and hardship, ﴿so that they might return﴾, so that they would return to obedience to their Lord and repent.

His statement, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Then there succeeded them﴾, meaning there came after these people whom We have described ﴿a successor﴾ (khalf). The khalf is the generation that comes after a generation. Abu Hatim said: khalf, with the lam unvocalized (sukun), means offspring; the singular and plural are the same in it. Khalf, with the lam vocalized with fatha, means a substitute, whether a child or a stranger.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: khalf with fatha means a righteous successor, and with sukun it means a wicked one.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: khalaf, with the lam vocalized or unvocalized, in the sense of a bad generation is one and the same; but in the sense of a righteous generation it is only with the lam vocalized (khalaf), and never otherwise.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: most of what occurs in praise is with the lam vocalized with fatha (khalaf), and in blame with the lam unvocalized (khalf), though it may be vocalized in blame and unvocalized in praise.

﴿They inherited the Book﴾, meaning the Book passed down to them from their fathers, which is the Torah, ﴿they take the goods of this lower world﴾. The 'arad is the goods of this world. The 'arad, with the ra' unvocalized, is any wealth other than dirhams and dinars. By "the lower" (al-adna) he means the world, that is, this transient abode; it is the feminine form of "the world" (al-dunya). These Jews inherited the Torah, read it, but neglected acting upon what is in it, opposed its ruling, and accepted bribes in matters of God's judgment and altered His words. ﴿And they say: "It will be forgiven us"﴾, our sins, desiring vain things from God.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawba related to us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith related to us; Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i related to us; 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud related to us; Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal related to us; 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam al-Ghassani, from Damra ibn Habib, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The shrewd one is he who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his soul's desires and wishes vainly upon God" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Sifat al-Qiyama, chapter "The shrewd one is he who holds himself to account": 7/156, and he said: this is a hasan (good) hadith. Also Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "Mention of death and preparing for it": 2/1423, no. (4260). Al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim): 1/57, and al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: I say, no, by God; Abu Bakr [ibn Maryam] is weak (wahin). It was also narrated elsewhere: 4/251. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 4/124, and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/309, saying: this is a hasan hadith; and he authenticated it in Masabih al-Sunna: 3/444. In the chain is Abu Bakr ibn Maryam al-Ghassani, who is weak; Ibn Tahir said: the hadith depends upon him, and he is very weak. See: Fayd al-Qadir by al-Manawi: 5/68.]].

﴿And if there comes to them goods like it, they will take it﴾. This is a report of their greed for this world and their persistence in sins. It means: whenever some worldly good presents itself to them, they take it, whether lawful or unlawful, and they desire forgiveness from God; and if they find the like of it the next day, they take it. Al-Suddi said: the Children of Israel would not appoint a judge except that he would accept bribes in the ruling. It was said to him: "Why do you accept bribes?" He would say: "I will be forgiven." The others would then criticize him, but when he died, or was removed and replaced by a man from among those who had been criticizing him, he too would accept bribes. He says: and if the others come to goods like it, they will take it.

﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about God except the truth?﴾, meaning: a covenant was taken from them in the Torah that they would not say about God other than the truth, and that is what they did in desiring forgiveness while persisting in sin. There is nothing in the Torah promising forgiveness for persistence in sin. ﴿And they studied what is in it﴾, meaning they read what is in it, and so they are cognizant of it. Had they understood it, they would have acted for the Hereafter. The study of the Book (dars al-kitab) is reading it and reflecting upon it again and again. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. Do you not understand?﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 170–172:**

﴿Those who hold fast to the Book﴾. Abu Bakr, transmitting from ʿAsim, read "yumsikūna" with a light (takhfif) pronunciation, while the common reading is with emphasis (tashdid). The reason is that one says "masaktu bi-l-shay'" (I held onto the thing), and one does not say "amsaktu bi-l-shay'"; one says only "amsaktuhu" (I held it). Ubayy ibn Ka'b read "wa-lladhīna tamassakū bi-l-kitāb" in the past tense, and this is good because of His saying, ﴿and establish prayer﴾, since a past verb is rarely joined to a future verb except in meaning. The intended meaning is those who act by what is in the Book. Mujahid said: they are the believers among the People of the Book, ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and his companions, who held fast to the Book that Moses brought. They did not distort it, did not conceal it, and did not take it as a means of gain. ʿAtaʾ said: they are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿and establish prayer. Indeed, We do not waste the reward of the righteous﴾.

His saying, ﴿And [recall] when We raised the mountain above them﴾: that is, We uprooted the mountain, and it was said: We lifted it. ﴿as though it were a canopy﴾. ʿAtaʾ said: a roof. The ẓullah is anything that shades you. ﴿And they thought﴾, that is, knew, ﴿that it would fall upon them﴾. ﴿[We said], "Take what We have given you with determination﴾, that is, with effort and diligence. ﴿and remember what is in it﴾, that is, act upon it. ﴿that you may become righteous﴾. This was when they refused to accept the rulings of the Torah, so God raised a mountain over their heads. Al-Hasan said: when they looked at the mountain, each man of them fell prostrate on his left eyebrow, looking at the mountain with his right eye out of fear that it would fall on him. For this reason you will not find a Jew who does not prostrate on his left eyebrow.

His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Zayd ibn al-Khattab, who told him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about this verse: ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and the rest of the verse. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, then He passed His right hand over his back and brought forth from it descendants. He said: I created these for Paradise, and they will act by the deeds of the people of Paradise. Then He passed His hand over his back and brought forth from it descendants, and He said: I created these for the Fire, and they will act by the deeds of the people of the Fire." A man said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise because of it. And when a servant is created for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire because of it." [Abu Dawud related it in the Sunnah, chapter on Qadar; al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surat al-A'raf, and said: this is a hasan hadith, and Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from ʿUmar. Malik related it in the Muwatta', beginning of the Book of Qadar. Al-Hakim authenticated it. Ahmad related it in the Musnad. Al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, and al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah. Al-Mundhiri said in Tahdhib al-Sunan: the meaning of this hadith has been authenticated from the Prophet (ﷺ) through eight chains, too long to mention. See also Ibn Kathir, and what Shaykh Shakir wrote as a comment in al-Tabari's tafsir, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's al-Tamhid.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith. Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from ʿUmar, and some have mentioned a man between Muslim ibn Yasar and ʿUmar in this chain.

Muqatil and others among the exegetes said: Allah passed His hand over the right side of Adam's back and brought forth from it white descendants resembling tiny ants, moving. Then He passed His hand over the left side of his back and brought forth from it black descendants resembling tiny ants. He said: "O Adam, these are your descendants." Then He said to them: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." He said to the white ones: "These are in Paradise by My mercy, and I do not mind, and they are the companions of the right hand." He said to the black ones: "These are in the Fire, and I do not mind, and they are the companions of the left hand." Then He returned them all into his loins. So the dead are held back until all the people of the covenant come forth from the loins of men and the wombs of women. Allah said concerning those who broke the first covenant: ﴿And We did not find most of them to be keepers of covenant﴾ [al-Aʿraf 102].

Some exegetes said: the people of happiness acknowledged willingly and said "Yes," while the people of wretchedness said it out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) and unwillingly. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Al ʿImran 83].

They differed concerning the place of the covenant. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: at Batn Nuʿman, a valley beside ʿArafah. It is also narrated from him that it was at Dahna' in the land of India, which is the place where Adam (peace be upon him) descended. Al-Kalbi said: between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Al-Suddi said: Allah brought Adam out of Paradise and he did not descend from heaven, then He passed His hand over his back and brought forth his descendants.

It is narrated that Allah brought them all forth, fashioned them, gave them intellects by which they understand and tongues by which they speak, then He spoke to them face to face (qubulan), meaning directly, and said: "Am I not your Lord?" Al-Zajjaj said: it is possible that Allah gave to creatures like ants a comprehension by which they understand, as He said: ﴿A female ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings"﴾ [al-Naml 18].

It is narrated that Allah the Exalted said to all of them: "Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord; there is no lord for you other than Me. So do not associate anything with Me, for I will surely take vengeance upon those who associate others with Me and do not believe in Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you books." They all spoke and said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; there is no lord for us other than You." Thus He took their covenants. Then He wrote down their terms of life, their provisions, and their afflictions. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I love to be thanked." When He had established them in His oneness and had them testify against one another, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not come until every person whose covenant was taken is born. This is His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾, that is, from the loins of the children of Adam, their descendants. [Al-Tabari, 3/238–239; al-Musnad 5/125; al-Mustadrak 2/323; Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7/25.]

The people of Medina, Abu ʿAmr and Ibn ʿAmir read "dhurriyyatihim" in the plural with a kasra on the taʾ, while the others read "dhurriyyatahum" in the singular with a fatha on the taʾ.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾, when He only brought them out from Adam's back? It is answered: Allah brought forth the descendants of Adam, some of them from the backs of others, in the manner in which sons are born from fathers in succession. So mention of Adam's back was dispensed with, since it is known that they are all his children and were brought forth from his back. [The hadith scholar Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, may Allah have mercy on him, said after citing the reports of the taking of the descendants and the testimony: "People have greatly multiplied the transmission of reports on this topic, and the theologians have spoken at length about it. The People of the Sunnah agree on believing these reports, affirming them, and abandoning dispute about them. And with Allah is protection and success." (al-Tamhid 16/12).

Ibn Kathir cited the reports in his tafsir (2/262–265), then said: "... These hadiths indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. As for the testimony taken from them there that He is their Lord, it appears only in the report of Kulthum ibn Jubayr from Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas, and in the report of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr. We have explained that both are mawquf (halting at the companion), not marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet). ... For this reason, those among the early and later scholars said: the intended meaning of this testimony is only their being created upon monotheism (fitrah), as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and ʿIyad ibn Himar al-Mujashiʿi, and in the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from al-Aswad ibn Sariʿ. Al-Hasan al-Basri explained the verse in this way..."]

And see: Tafsir al-Fakhr al-Razi 15/50–56; al-Silsilah al-Sahihah by al-Albani 4/158–163; Dar' Ta'arud al-ʿAql wa-l-Naql by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah 8/359 and following; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/313 and following.

His saying, ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ That is, some of them testified against others. ﴿[This], lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware"﴾. Abu ʿAmr read "an yaqūlū" and "yaqūlū" with the yāʾ in both places, while the others read them with the tāʾ in both places.

They differed concerning His saying, "shahidna" (we testify). Al-Suddi said: it is a report from Allah about Himself and His angels, that they testified to the acknowledgment of the children of Adam. Some said: it is a report of the words of the children of Adam when Allah made some of them testify against others, and they said "Yes, we testify." Al-Kalbi said: it is from the words of the angels, and there is an ellipsis in it, its sense being: when the offspring said "Yes," Allah said to the angels: "Bear witness." They said: "We bear witness." His saying, "an yaqūlū," means: and He made them testify against themselves that they should say, that is, lest they say, or out of dislike that they should say. Whoever reads with the tāʾ, the sense of the speech is: "I address you: Am I not your Lord?" lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed we were unaware of this," that is, unaware of this covenant and this acknowledgment. If it is asked: how can the proof be binding on someone who does not remember the covenant? It is answered: Allah has made clear the signs of His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers in what they reported. Whoever denies this is obstinate, a breaker of the covenant, and the proof binds him. Their forgetting and their lack of retention do not nullify the argument, after the report of the truthful informant who possesses the miracle.

The ẓullah is anything that shades you. ﴿And they thought﴾, that is, knew, ﴿that it would fall upon them﴾. ﴿[We said], "Take what We have given you with determination﴾, that is, with effort and diligence. ﴿and remember what is in it﴾, that is, act upon it. ﴿that you may become righteous﴾. This was when they refused to accept the rulings of the Torah, so God raised a mountain over their heads. Al-Hasan said: when they looked at the mountain, each man of them fell prostrate on his left eyebrow, looking at the mountain with his right eye out of fear that it would fall on him. For this reason you will not find a Jew who does not prostrate on his left eyebrow.

His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and the rest of the verse.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Zayd ibn al-Khattab, who told him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about this verse: ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, and the rest of the verse. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, then He passed His right hand over his back and brought forth from it descendants. He said: I created these for Paradise, and they will act by the deeds of the people of Paradise. Then He passed His hand over his back and brought forth from it descendants, and He said: I created these for the Fire, and they will act by the deeds of the people of the Fire." A man said: "Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise because of it. And when a servant is created for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire because of it." [Abu Dawud related it in the Sunnah, chapter on Qadar; al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surat al-A'raf, and said: this is a hasan hadith, and Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from ʿUmar. Malik related it in the Muwatta', beginning of the Book of Qadar. Al-Hakim authenticated it. Ahmad related it in the Musnad. Al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah, and al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah. Al-Mundhiri said in Tahdhib al-Sunan: the meaning of this hadith has been authenticated from the Prophet (ﷺ) through eight chains, too long to mention. See also Ibn Kathir, and what Shaykh Shakir wrote as a comment in al-Tabari's tafsir, and Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's al-Tamhid.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith. Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from ʿUmar, and some have mentioned a man between Muslim ibn Yasar and ʿUmar in this chain.

Muqatil and others among the exegetes said: Allah passed His hand over the right side of Adam's back and brought forth from it white descendants resembling tiny ants, moving. Then He passed His hand over the left side of his back and brought forth from it black descendants resembling tiny ants. He said: "O Adam, these are your descendants." Then He said to them: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." He said to the white ones: "These are in Paradise by My mercy, and I do not mind, and they are the companions of the right hand." He said to the black ones: "These are in the Fire, and I do not mind, and they are the companions of the left hand." Then He returned them all into his loins. So the dead are held back until all the people of the covenant come forth from the loins of men and the wombs of women. Allah said concerning those who broke the first covenant: ﴿And We did not find most of them to be keepers of covenant﴾ [al-Aʿraf 102].

Some exegetes said: the people of happiness acknowledged willingly and said "Yes," while the people of wretchedness said it out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) and unwillingly. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Al ʿImran 83].

They differed concerning the place of the covenant. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: at Batn Nuʿman, a valley beside ʿArafah. It is also narrated from him that it was at Dahna' in the land of India, which is the place where Adam (peace be upon him) descended. Al-Kalbi said: between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Al-Suddi said: Allah brought Adam out of Paradise and he did not descend from heaven, then He passed His hand over his back and brought forth his descendants.

It is narrated that Allah brought them all forth, fashioned them, gave them intellects by which they understand and tongues by which they speak, then He spoke to them face to face (qubulan), meaning directly, and said: "Am I not your Lord?" Al-Zajjaj said: it is possible that Allah gave to creatures like ants a comprehension by which they understand, as He said: ﴿A female ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings"﴾ [al-Naml 18].

It is narrated that Allah the Exalted said to all of them: "Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord; there is no lord for you other than Me. So do not associate anything with Me, for I will surely take vengeance upon those who associate others with Me and do not believe in Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pact, and I will send down to you books." They all spoke and said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; there is no lord for us other than You." Thus He took their covenants. Then He wrote down their terms of life, their provisions, and their afflictions. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I love to be thanked." When He had established them in His oneness and had them testify against one another, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not come until every person whose covenant was taken is born. This is His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾, that is, from the loins of the children of Adam, their descendants. [Al-Tabari, 3/238–239; al-Musnad 5/125; al-Mustadrak 2/323; Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7/25.]

The people of Medina, Abu ʿAmr and Ibn ʿAmir read "dhurriyyatihim" in the plural with a kasra on the taʾ, while the others read "dhurriyyatahum" in the singular with a fatha on the taʾ.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins﴾, when He only brought them out from Adam's back? It is answered: Allah brought forth the descendants of Adam, some of them from the backs of others, in the manner in which sons are born from fathers in succession. So mention of Adam's back was dispensed with, since it is known that they are all his children and were brought forth from his back. [The hadith scholar Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, may Allah have mercy on him, said after citing the reports of the taking of the descendants and the testimony: "People have greatly multiplied the transmission of reports on this topic, and the theologians have spoken at length about it. The People of the Sunnah agree on believing these reports, affirming them, and abandoning dispute about them. And with Allah is protection and success." (al-Tamhid 16/12).

Ibn Kathir cited the reports in his tafsir (2/262–265), then said: "... These hadiths indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. As for the testimony taken from them there that He is their Lord, it appears only in the report of Kulthum ibn Jubayr from Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas, and in the report of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr. We have explained that both are mawquf (halting at the companion), not marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet). ... For this reason, those among the early and later scholars said: the intended meaning of this testimony is only their being created upon monotheism (fitrah), as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and ʿIyad ibn Himar al-Mujashiʿi, and in the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from al-Aswad ibn Sariʿ. Al-Hasan al-Basri explained the verse in this way..."]

And see: Tafsir al-Fakhr al-Razi 15/50–56; al-Silsilah al-Sahihah by al-Albani 4/158–163; Dar' Ta'arud al-ʿAql wa-l-Naql by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah 8/359 and following; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 7/313 and following.

His saying, ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ That is, some of them testified against others. ﴿[This], lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware"﴾. Abu ʿAmr read "an yaqūlū" and "yaqūlū" with the yāʾ in both places, while the others read them with the tāʾ in both places.

They differed concerning His saying, "shahidna" (we testify). Al-Suddi said: it is a report from Allah about Himself and His angels, that they testified to the acknowledgment of the children of Adam. Some said: it is a report of the words of the children of Adam when Allah made some of them testify against others, and they said "Yes, we testify." Al-Kalbi said: it is from the words of the angels, and there is an ellipsis in it, its sense being: when the offspring said "Yes," Allah said to the angels: "Bear witness." They said: "We bear witness." His saying, "an yaqūlū," means: and He made them testify against themselves that they should say, that is, lest they say, or out of dislike that they should say. Whoever reads with the tāʾ, the sense of the speech is: "I address you: Am I not your Lord?" lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed we were unaware of this," that is, unaware of this covenant and this acknowledgment. If it is asked: how can the proof be binding on someone who does not remember the covenant? It is answered: Allah has made clear the signs of His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers in what they reported. Whoever denies this is obstinate, a breaker of the covenant, and the proof binds him. Their forgetting and their lack of retention do not nullify the argument, after the report of the truthful informant who possesses the miracle.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 170–172:**

﴿Or you might say: "It was only that our forefathers associated partners with God before us, and we were their offspring after them."﴾ He says: He took the covenant from you only so that you would not say, O polytheists, "It was only that our forefathers associated partners with God before us, and broke the covenant, and we were their offspring after them," meaning: we were their followers, and we imitated them. Then you would make this an excuse for yourselves and say: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the wrongdoers did?﴾ Will You punish us for the sin of our wrongdoing forefathers? They could not then argue with such words after God had reminded them of the taking of the covenant concerning monotheism (tawhid, the affirmation of God's oneness).

﴿And thus We detail the signs﴾, meaning: We make the signs clear so that the servants may reflect upon them, ﴿so that perhaps they will return﴾ from disbelief to monotheism.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, the verse. The commentators differed concerning him. Ibn Abbas [[See: al-Tabari: 13/254; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 261; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/608-609.]] said: he is Balam ibn Ba'ura (Bal'am ibn Ba'ura). Mujahid (1) said: Bal'am ibn Ba'ir. Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas (1): he was from the Children of Israel. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was from the Canaanites, from the city of the giants [[al-Tabari: 13/254-255.]]. Muqatil said: he was from the city of Balqa.

His story, as related by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi and others [[See: al-Tabari: 13/264-267; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/267-268; al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 1/322, where he said: "This which Ibn Ishaq mentioned in the story of Bal'am is authentic; it has been mentioned by more than one of the early scholars."]], is that when Moses intended to fight the giants and camped in the land of the Banu Canaan in the land of Syria, the people of Bal'am came to Bal'am—and he had the Greatest Name of Allah—and said: "Moses is a fierce man, and with him is a great army, and he has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us, and to settle the Children of Israel in them. You are a man whose supplication is answered, so go out and pray to Allah to turn them away from us." He said: "Woe to you! He is the Prophet of Allah, and with him are the angels and the believers. How can I pray against them, when I know of Allah what I know? If I did this, my worldly life and my hereafter would be lost." They pressed him and insisted upon him, so he said: "Until I consult my Lord." He would not supplicate until he saw what he was commanded in a dream. He consulted (his Lord) about praying against them, and it was said to him in a dream: "Do not pray against them." He said to his people: "I have consulted my Lord, and I have been forbidden." They then presented him with a gift, and he accepted it. Then they returned to him, and he said: "Until I consult." He consulted, but nothing was revealed to him. He said: "I have consulted, but nothing has come to me." They said: "If your Lord disliked your praying against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time." They continued to beseech him until they tempted him, and he was tempted. He mounted his she-donkey heading towards a mountain overlooking the army of the Children of Israel, called Husban. When he had ridden her not far, she knelt beneath him. He dismounted and beat her until he had worn her out, and she rose, so he mounted her again. She did not go far with him before she knelt, so he did the same to her and she rose, so he mounted her, and she did not go far with him before she knelt, so he beat her until he had worn her out. Allah permitted her to speak, and she spoke to him as a proof against him, saying: "Woe to you, O Bal'am! Where are you taking me? Do you not see the angels before me turning me back from this direction? Are you taking me to the Prophet of Allah and the believers, to pray against them?" He did not desist, so Allah released her, and she went on until, when she brought him up over the mountain of Husban, he began to pray against them, but whenever he prayed against them, Allah turned his tongue towards his own people, and whenever he prayed for his people with good, Allah turned his tongue towards the Children of Israel. His people said to him: "O Bal'am, do you know what you are doing? You are only praying for them against us!" He said: "This is something I do not control; this is a matter in which Allah has prevailed." His tongue then hung out and fell upon his chest. He said to them: "Now this world and the hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but cunning and guile. I will devise a plan for you and scheme. Beautify the women, adorn them, give them goods, then send them to the army to sell them there, and order them that no woman shall refuse herself to a man who desires her, for if even one of them commits fornication, you will be rid of them." They did so. When the women entered the army, a woman of the Canaanites, named Kasti daughter of Sur, passed by a man of the notables of the Children of Israel called Zimri ibn Shalum, chief of the tribe of Simeon ibn Ya'qub. He went to her, took her hand when her beauty pleased him, then brought her and stood with her before Moses. He said: "I think you will say this is forbidden to you?" He said: "Indeed, she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, I will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and lay with her. He had been absent when Zimri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was ravaging the Children of Israel, and was informed of the news. He took his spear, which was entirely of iron, then entered the tent upon the two of them while they were lying together, and he pierced them both with his spear. Then he went out with them, raising them to the sky, the spear taken in his arm, his elbow leaning on his side, and he rested the spear against his beard. He was the eldest son of al-'Izar, and he kept saying: "O Allah, this is how we deal with those who disobey You." The plague was lifted. When he saw their army, the she-donkey stood still and halted with him, so he struck her. She said: "Why are you striking me? I am under command, and this is a fire before me that has prevented me from walking." He returned and informed the king, who said: "You must pray against him, or I will crucify you." He asked about them and was told: "Muhammad killed them." He said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have killed his kinsmen." When Umayya died, his sister Fari'a came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her about her brother's death. She said: "While he was sleeping, two visitors came to him, opened the roof of the house, descended, and one of them sat at his feet while the other sat at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: 'Does he understand?' The other said: 'He refuses.' She said: I asked him about that, and he said: 'Good was intended for me,' then he turned away from me and fainted. When he came to, he said: 'Every life, however long it lasts for a time, must one day pass away.'

'Would that I had been, before what has now appeared to me,
on the peaks of the mountains, grazing the wild goats.'

'Indeed the Day of Reckoning is a great day,
on which the young grow grey, a heavy day.'"

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Recite to me some of your brother's poetry." She recited some of his poems to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "His poetry believed, and his heart disbelieved," and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, the verse [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/255-257; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 261; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/609.]].

It is related from Ibn Abbas in another narration that it was revealed concerning al-Basus, a man from the Children of Israel. He had been given three answered supplications. He had a wife, and she had a son from him. She said: "Make one supplication for me." He said: "You have one of them; what do you want?" She said: "Pray to Allah that He make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel." He prayed for her, and she became the most beautiful of the women among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one among them like her, she became averse to him. The husband became angry and prayed against her, and she became a barking bitch. Two of the supplications were used up. Her sons came and said: "We cannot bear this. Our mother has become a barking bitch, and the people reproach us with her. Pray to Allah that He return her to the state she was in." He prayed to Allah and she returned as she had been, and all the supplications were used up [[Asbab al-Nuzul (261-262); al-Durr al-Manthur 3/608; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 4/422.]]. The first two opinions are more apparent [[Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit (4/423): "The proper approach in such matters, when reports come from the commentators, is to understand their sayings as illustrations, not as restriction to a specific individual, for that leads to confusion and contradiction." And the leader of the commentators, al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The correct statement on this matter is to say that Allah, may He be remembered, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to recite to his people the account of a man who was righteous, to whom Allah gave His proofs and evidences, which are the 'signs'... It is possible that the one to whom Allah gave this was Bal'am, and it is possible that it was Umayya, and there is no report which establishes which of the two men is meant, nor any indication from reason as to which of them is meant. So the correct approach is to say what Allah said, and to affirm the outward meaning of the revelation as it came from Allah" (al-Tafsir 13/259-260).]].

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites among the People of the Book, who used to recognise the Prophet (ﷺ) as they recognise their own sons.

Qatadah said: This is a parable which Allah, mighty and majestic, struck for one to whom guidance was presented and who refused to accept it, and that is His saying: "And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs." Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: It is the Greatest Name of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: He would not ask Allah for anything without being given it. Ibn Abbas said in another narration: He was given a book from the books of Allah, but he detached himself from it, meaning he came out of it as a snake sheds its skin, i.e., he came out of it as the snake comes out of its skin.

﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he overtook him and caught up with him, ﴿and he became of the misguided﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 176:

﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾: that is, We would have raised his rank and station through those signs. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "We would have raised him through his knowledge of them." Mujahid and 'Ata' said: "We would have lifted disbelief from him and protected him through the signs."

﴿But he inclined toward the earth﴾: that is, he settled into the worldly life and leaned toward it. Al-Zajjaj said: "Khalada and akhlada are one and the same." Its root is from al-khulud (permanence and remaining), and it is said: "Fulan akhlada bi-l-makan" when he stayed in a place. Here "the earth" is an expression for the worldly life, because all the deserts and properties in it are earth, and the rest of its goods are extracted from the earth.

﴿And he followed his desire﴾: he submitted to what desire called him to. Ibn Zayd said: "His desire was with the people." 'Ata' said: "He meant the worldly life, and obeyed his devil." This is the most severe verse for the scholars, because Allah informed that He had given him [a sign] [[In "b": (His signs).]] from His Greatest Name, the answered supplications, knowledge and wisdom. So by inclining to the earth and following desire he deserved the change of the blessing upon him and its stripping away from him. And who is safe from these two traits except the one whom Allah protects?

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawba informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith related to us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud related to us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Zakariya ibn Abi Za'ida, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn Zurara, from Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two hungry wolves released among a flock of sheep do not cause as much corruption to it as a person's greed for wealth and status does to his religion."

[Takhrij note from the original text: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter 30: 7/46, who said: "This is a sound hadith," and Ibn Hibban authenticated it (p. 612 of Mawarid al-Zam'an). Also narrated by al-Darimi in al-Riqaq: 2/304, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/257-258. Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali also attributed it to al-Nasa'i, and said: it is narrated through another route from the Prophet (ﷺ) from the hadiths of Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayra, Usama ibn Zayd, Abu Sa'id, and 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with them). Also narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/456, 460. See: "Sharh Hadith Ma Dhi'bani Ja'i'an" by Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali in Majmu'at al-Rasa'il al-Munira: 3/1 onward.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾. It is said: "lahatha al-kalbu yalhathu lahthan" when the dog extends its tongue. Mujahid said: "He is like the one who reads the Book and does not act upon it."

The meaning: this disbeliever, if you rebuke him, he will not be deterred, and if you leave him, he will not be guided. So both states are equal to him, like the two states of the dog: if it is driven away and pursued, it pants, and if it is left and lies down, it still pants. Al-Qutaybi said: "Every creature pants only from exhaustion or thirst, except the dog, which pants in a state of weariness, in a state of rest, and in a state of thirst." So Allah struck this as a parable for one who denies His signs: if you admonish him, he is astray, and if you leave him, he is astray, like the dog which pants whether you chase it or leave it in its condition. Its parallel is His saying: (And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent) [Al-A'raf: 193]. Then with this parable He generalized to all who deny the signs of Allah, saying: ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs; so relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾. It was also said: this is a parable for the disbelievers of Makkah, because they used to wish for a guide who would direct them and call them to the obedience of Allah. When there came to them a Prophet whose truthfulness they did not doubt, they denied him, and so they were not guided, whether they were left or called.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 177–178:

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾, that is: evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs. Its underlying structure is: "Evil as an example is the example of the people," so the word "example" (mathal) was omitted and "the people" (al-qawm) was put in its place and therefore given the nominative case (marfu'). ﴿And they were wronging themselves﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 177–178:

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾, that is: evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs. Its underlying structure is: "Evil as an example is the example of the people," so the word "example" (mathal) was omitted and "the people" (al-qawm) was put in its place and therefore given the nominative case (marfu'). ﴿And they were wronging themselves﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 179–180:

﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, informs us that He created many of the jinn and mankind for the Fire. They are those upon whom the eternal Word has been realized with wretchedness, and whoever Allah has created for Hell has no means of escaping from it.

Abu Bakr Ya'qub ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi informed us; Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhaldi informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah al-Balkhi informed us; Musa ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hakam al-Shatawi narrated to us; Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from A'ishah bint Talhah, from A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said: The Prophet ﷺ came upon the funeral of a child from among the children of the Ansar. A'ishah said: "Tuba (blessed) to him, a little bird from the little birds of Paradise!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And how do you know? Allah created Paradise and created for it its people while they were in their fathers' loins, and He created the Fire and created for it its people while they were in their fathers' loins."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Qadar, chapter on the meaning of "every child is born upon the fitrah...", no. (2662): 4/2050; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/141.]]

It has been said that the lam in His words "for Hell" is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), meaning: We created them, and the consequence of their affair is Hell, as in His words: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ (al-Qasas 8). Then He described them, saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, meaning they do not know, through them, good and guidance.

﴿And they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ the path of truth and the way of right guidance, ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ the admonitions of the Qur'an, so that they might reflect upon them and take lessons from them. Then He set forth for them an example regarding their ignorance and their confining themselves to eating and drinking, saying: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray.﴾ That is: they are like livestock in that their aim is eating, drinking and enjoying desires. "Rather, they are further astray" because livestock distinguish between harms and benefits, so they do not advance toward harms, whereas these people advance toward the Fire out of obstinacy while knowing its destruction. ﴿Those are the heedless.﴾

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them﴾. Muqatil said: This was because a man invoked Allah in his prayer and invoked "the Merciful" (al-Rahman). Some of the polytheists of Makkah said: "Muhammad and his companions claim that they worship one Lord, so why does this one invoke two?" Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them." Al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan (the most beautiful), like al-kubra and al-sughra (the greatest and the smallest).

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bishran informed us; Abu Ali Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Muradi informed us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise. Indeed He is Witr (Single) and loves the Witr."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Da'awat, chapter "Allah has a hundred names, other than one"; 11/214, and in al-Shurut and al-Tawhid; and Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on the names of Allah and the merit of whoever enumerates them, no. (2677): 4/2062; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/30.]]

﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. Hamzah recited "yalhadun" (with a fatha on the ya' and the ha' wherever it occurs), and al-Kisa'i agreed with him in al-Nahl; the rest recited it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the ha'. The meaning of al-ilhad (deviation) is inclining away from the intended course. It is said: alhada yulhidu ilhadan, and lahada yalhadu luhudan, meaning he inclined. Ya'qub ibn al-Sikkit said: al-ilhad is deviating from the truth and introducing into it what does not belong to it. It is said: alhada fi al-din and lahada, and Hamzah recited with it.

﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾: they are the polytheists who turned Allah's names away from what they are, so they named their idols with them, adding and subtracting. They derived "al-Lat" from "Allah," "al-Uzza" from "al-'Aziz," and "Manat" from "al-Mannan." This is the view of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.

It has also been said: it is their naming the idols "gods." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas: "they deviate concerning His names" means they lie. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: deviation concerning the names of Allah is naming Him with what He has not been named with, and what the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have not spoken of.

The summary of this: the names of Allah, exalted is He, are by tawqif (scriptural determination; they are fixed only by revelation). He is called Jawad (Generous) but is not called Sakhi (Lavish), though it has the same meaning as Jawad. He is called Rahim (Merciful) but is not called Rafiq (Gentle). He is called 'Alim (Knowing) but is not called 'Aqil (Intelligent). Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿They deceive Allah, but He is the one who deceives them﴾ (al-Nisa' 142), and the Mighty One, the Speaker, says: "They plotted, and Allah plotted" (Al 'Imran: 54). Yet it is not said in supplication: "O Deceiver! O Plotter!" Rather He is invoked by His names that have been revealed by tawqif, in the manner of exaltation, so one says: "O Allah! O Merciful (al-Rahman)! O Compassionate (al-Rahim)! O Mighty (al-'Aziz)! O Generous (al-Karim)!" and the like.

﴿They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, informs us that He created many of the jinn and mankind for the Fire. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 181–184:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among those We have created is a community﴾ meaning a group (ʿiṣābah), ﴿who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbas: he means the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), namely the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and those who follow them in goodness. Qatadah said: It has reached us that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he recited this verse, would say: "This is for you, and the people before you were given something like it: and from the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/286.]

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to me, Ibn Jabir narrated to me, and he is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, ʿUmayr ibn Hani narrated to me that he heard Muʿawiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A community from among my ummah will not cease to stand firm by the command of Allah; those who forsake them will not harm them, nor will those who oppose them, until the command of Allah comes while they remain upon that." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Manaqib, chapter 28: 6/632; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on his saying (ﷺ): "A group from among my ummah will not cease to be victorious upon the truth..." no. 1037: 3/1524; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/212.] Al-Kalbi said: they are from all of creation.

﴿And those who denied Our signs, We will draw them gradually from where they do not know﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: We will plan against them from where they do not know. It was also said: We will come to them from their place of safety, as He said: "So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect" [al-Hashr: 2]. Al-Kalbi said: He makes their deeds appear fair to them and destroys them. Al-Dahhak said: Whenever they renew a disobedience, We renew a blessing for them. Sufyan al-Thawri said: We lavish blessings upon them and make them forget gratitude. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: al-istidraj (gradual drawing-on) is to advance toward something secretly, little by little, so that it is neither sudden nor open. From this comes "daraja al-sabiyy" when a child draws his steps close together while walking, and from it "darraja al-kitab" when one folds a book bit by bit.

﴿And I give them respite﴾ meaning: I grant them time and lengthen the span of their lives, so that they persist in sins. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾ meaning: indeed My seizing is strong and severe. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Indeed My scheme is severe. It was said: it was revealed concerning the mockers, and Allah destroyed them in a single night.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion﴾. Qatadah said: It was related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) stood on al-Safa at night and began calling the clans of Quraysh, clan by clan: "O Banu so-and-so, O Banu so-and-so," warning them of Allah's punishment and His calamities. One of them said: Indeed this companion of yours is a madman; he has been crying out until morning. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion﴾ [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 13/289 with a sound chain to Qatadah. See al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 66.] of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Madness (jinnah)﴾ means insanity. ﴿He is not﴾ meaning he is not ﴿but a clear warner﴾. Then He urged them to the reflection that leads to knowledge, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 181–184:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And among those We have created is a community﴾ meaning a group (ʿiṣābah), ﴿who guide by the truth and by it do justice﴾. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbas: he means the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), namely the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and those who follow them in goodness. Then He urged them to the reflection that leads to knowledge, saying:

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 185–187:**

﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and at what Allah has created﴾ [of] anything [in them]? That is: and that they might look at what Allah has created of anything, so that they might take it as evidence of His oneness.

﴿And [have they not considered] that perhaps their term has drawn near?﴾ That is: perhaps their term has drawn near, so that they die before they believe and go to the punishment. ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ That is: after the Qur'an, will they believe? He says: in what book other than that which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought will they believe? There is no prophet after him and no book after it.

Then He mentioned the cause of their turning away from belief, saying:

﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him. And He leaves them﴾ The people of Basra and 'Asim recited it with a *ya'* (يَذَرُهُمْ) and a raised *ra'* (رفع الراء), while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it with a *ya'* and a jussive *ra'* (جزم الراء), because the mention of Allah had preceded it; the jussive *ra'* is connected to "yudlil" (يُضْلِلِ). The others recited it with a *nun* (نَذَرُهُمْ) and a raised *ra'*, taking it as a new, independent statement.

﴿In their transgression, they wander blindly.﴾ That is: they hesitate, bewildered.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to rest?﴾ Qatadah said: The Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Indeed there is kinship between us and you, so reveal to us when the Hour will be." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 13/292, 298.]] meaning: the Resurrection. ﴿When will it come to rest?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: its end. Qatadah said: its establishing. Its root meaning is firmness, that is: when will it be established? ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the knowledge of it is only with my Lord.﴾ He has kept its occurrence to Himself, and none knows it but Him. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him.﴾

That is, none will disclose it or make it manifest. Mujahid said: none will bring it. ﴿Heavy it is in the heavens and the earth﴾ meaning: the weight of its knowledge and the hiddenness of its matter for the people of the heavens and the earth, and everything hidden is heavy. Al-Hasan said: it means that when it comes, it will be heavy and great upon the people of the heavens and the earth. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾ — unexpectedly, while you are heedless.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: We were told by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: We were told by Abu al-Yaman, who said: We were told by Shu'ayb, who said: We were told by Abu al-Zinad, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will certainly come while two men have spread their garment between them, and they will neither sell it nor fold it. The Hour will certainly come while a man has left with the milk of his she-camel and will not drink it. The Hour will certainly come while a man is plastering his cistern and will not water with it. The Hour will certainly come while a man has raised his morsel to his mouth and will not eat it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter "Haddathana Abu al-Yaman": 11/352, and by Muslim in al-Fitan, chapter "Qurb al-Sa'ah" (2954): 4/2270. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/26–27.]]

﴿They ask you as though you were eager to know it﴾ — that is, knowledgeable of it, from their saying "ahfaytu fi al-mas'alah," meaning I pressed the question insistently. The meaning is: as though you had pressed the question about it until you came to know it. ﴿Say: its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know﴾ that its knowledge is with Allah, even though they asked Muhammad (ﷺ) about it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verse 188:

﴿Say: I have no power over benefit or harm for myself, except what Allah wills.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The people of Makkah said: "O Muhammad, would your Lord not inform you of cheap goods before their price rises, so that you could buy them and profit from them when prices are high? And of a land that is about to become barren, so that you could move away from it to one that has become fertile?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: I have no power over benefit for myself﴾ [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 263.]] meaning: I am not able to bring about benefit for myself, namely to acquire gain by making a profit, ﴿nor harm﴾, meaning to repel harm by moving away from a land that is about to become barren, ﴿except what Allah wills that I possess.﴾

﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ Meaning: had I known the fertility and the barrenness, I would have acquired much of good, that is, of wealth, in preparation for the year of famine. ﴿And no harm would have touched me﴾, meaning: no adversity, poverty or hunger.

Ibn Juraij said: "Say: I have no power over benefit or harm for myself" means: guidance and misguidance. "(And had I known the unseen)", that is, when I will die, "I would have acquired much of good", meaning: of righteous deeds, "and no harm would have touched me."

Ibn Zayd said: "And I would have avoided what is evil and guarded against it."

It has also been said: its meaning is, "And had I known the unseen," that is, when the Hour will come, "I would have informed you so that you might believe, and no harm would have touched me through your denial." It has also been said: "no harm would have touched me" means: "no madness," because they used to attribute madness to him.

﴿I am only a warner﴾ to those who do not believe in what I have brought, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ of Paradise, ﴿to a people who believe﴾, who affirm it.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 189–190:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam. ﴿And made from it its mate﴾, meaning Eve (Hawwa'). ﴿So that he might find tranquillity in her﴾, that he might be at ease with her and find refuge in her. ١٤٢/أ ﴿When he covered her﴾, meaning he had intercourse with her and lay with her, ﴿she bore a light burden﴾, and this is the first stage of a woman's pregnancy from the drop of semen, which is light upon her. ﴿And she carried it about﴾, meaning she continued with it, stood and sat with it, and it did not weigh her down. ﴿Then, when she became heavy﴾, meaning the child grew large in her womb, she became burdened with her pregnancy, and her delivery drew near. ﴿They both called upon Allah, their Lord﴾, meaning Adam and Eve: ﴿"If You give us a righteous one﴾, O our Lord, ﴿a righteous one﴾, meaning a complete human being like us, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

The exegetes said: When Eve conceived, Iblis came to her in the form of a man and said to her: "What is in your belly?" She said: "I do not know." He said: "I fear it may be an animal, or a dog, or a pig. And how do you know from where it will come out? From your back passage, and it will kill you, or from your [front passage] [[In "B": (fika) (your mouth).]], and your belly will be split open." He said: (﴿Then you took the calf﴾), and (﴿And when you killed a soul﴾). He addressed the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and that action had been done by their fathers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ He means: Iblis and the idols. ﴿While they themselves are created﴾, i.e., they are created beings.

Then He addressed the believers, saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance﴾

The others read it with a kasra on the ط (ṭā') (وَقَرَأَ الْآخَرُونَ بِكَسْرِ الطَّاءِ). ﴿Or do they have eyes with which they see, or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ He means that the power of created beings lies in these limbs and instruments, and the idols do not have these instruments. You are thus superior to them, with feet that walk, hands that grasp, eyes that see and ears that hear. So how can you worship those who are inferior to you in power? ﴿Say: Call upon your partners﴾, O assembly of polytheists, ﴿then plot against me﴾, you and they, ﴿and give me no respite﴾, meaning: do not delay me, and hasten in your plotting against me.

His statement: ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who revealed the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an; that is, He will support and help me, just as He strengthened me by sending down the Book. ﴿And He takes care of the righteous﴾. Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiya Allāhu 'anhumā) said: He means those who do not associate anything with Allah, so Allah takes care of them by His help, and the enmity of those who oppose them does not harm them.

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear﴾, meaning the idols. ﴿And you see them looking at you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿meaning the idols﴾, ﴿yet they do not see﴾. The intended sense of "looking" is not literal looking; rather, it means facing or being opposite, as the Arabs say: "My house looks at your house," meaning it faces it. It was also said: "And you see them looking at you" means: as if they were looking at you, like His saying: ﴿And you see people as drunken﴾ (al-Ḥajj 2), meaning: as if they were drunk. This is the view of most of the commentators (mufassirūn). Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿And if you call them to guidance﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿they do not hear﴾ and do not understand that with their hearts; ﴿and you see them looking at you﴾ with their eyes, ﴿yet they do not see﴾ with their hearts.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Take what is easy (al-'afw)﴾. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: Allah commanded His Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace, to take the 'afw (easy part) of people's character. Mujahid said: ﴿Take what is easy﴾ means the 'afw of people's characters and deeds without spying, such as accepting apologies, pardoning, being lenient, and leaving off probing into matters and the like.

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Jibril: "What is this?" He said: "I do not know until I ask Him." Then he returned and said: "Your Lord commands you to join relations with those who cut you off, to give to those who deprive you, and to pardon those who wrong you."

Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiya Allāhu 'anhumā), al-Suddi, al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Kalbi said: it means take what is left over for you of wealth, which is the surplus beyond one's dependents. This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: the 'afw﴾ (al-Baqarah 219). Then this was abrogated (nusikhat) by the obligatory charities (al-ṣadaqāt al-mafrūḍāt). His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And enjoin what is customary (al-'urf)﴾, meaning what is good (al-ma'rūf), which is everything the Sharia recognizes. 'Aṭā' said: ﴿And enjoin al-'urf﴾ means: "There is no god but Allah."

﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, meaning Abu Jahl and his companions. It was abrogated by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf). It was also said: when the ignorant person behaves foolishly toward you, do not respond to him with foolishness. This is like His statement: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say: "Peace"﴾ (al-Furqan 63), which is the peace of disengagement. Ja'far al-Ṣādiq said: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) with the noble qualities of character, and there is no verse in the Qur'an that comprises the noble qualities of character more than this verse.

Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Ṣamad [al-Jurjani] [In A: "al-Jawzajani"] informed us: Abu al-Qasim 'Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i narrated to us: al-Haytham ibn Kulayb narrated to us: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jadali, from 'A'ishah (raḍiya Allāhu 'anhā) that she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was neither obscene nor foul-mouthed, nor did he shout in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and overlooked."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 200–201:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should cause you to waver﴾, meaning: it strikes you, befalls you, and presents itself to you from Satan as a nazgh (a prick, a stirring). The nazgh from Satan is whispering (al-waswasah). Al-Zajjaj said: the nazgh is the slightest movement that comes from a human being, and from Satan it is the slightest whispering. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: when this verse was revealed, "Take what comes easily" (khudh al-afw), the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How, O Lord, with anger?" Then it was revealed: "And if an evil suggestion from Satan should cause you to waver, then seek refuge in Allah." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/333.]] That is: seek protection (istajir) in Allah. ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have taramount piety (alladhina ittaqaw)﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿when an evil thought from Satan touches them﴾. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and al-Kisa'i read "tayf" (ṭayf), while the others read "ta'if" (ṭā’if) with a long vowel and a hamzah. Both are dialectal forms, like al-mayyit and al-ma'it, and their meaning is: a thing that visits you. Some people distinguished between them: Abu Amr said: the ta'if is that which circles around a thing, and the tayf is the passing thought and whispering. It was also said: the ta'if is that which circles around a person from the whispering of Satan, and the tayf is the lamam (passing impulse) and the touch (almass).

﴿They remember﴾ means they come to know (ʿarafu), Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the man who becomes angry with a flash of anger, so he remembers Allah the Exalted and so he restrains his rage. Mujahid said: it is the man who is about to commit a sin, so he remembers Allah and so he abandons it.

﴿Then they are seeing clearly (mubsirun)﴾, meaning they perceive the places of their wrongdoing through remembrance and reflection. Al-Suddi said: when they slip, they repent. Muqatil said: when the pious person is touched by a nazgh from Satan, he remembers and recognizes that it is disobedience, so he sees clearly and is turned back from disobeying Allah.
