**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 202–204:**

His saying: ﴿And their brothers extend them⦆ means the brothers of the devils from among the polytheists extend them, that is, the devil extends them. Al-Kalbi said: "For every disbeliever there is a brother among the devils."

﴿in error﴾ means they seek to lead them astray until they persist in it. It was also said: they increase them in misguidance. The people of Medina read "yumiddūnahum" (with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *kasra* on the *mīm*), from *al-imdād* (extending/supplying). The others read it with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ* and a *ḍamma* on the *mīm*. Both are dialectal variants (*lughatān*) with the same meaning.

﴿Then they do not desist﴾ means they do not restrain themselves. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Neither do humans refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils withhold from them. Accordingly, His saying 'then they do not desist' refers to the actions of both the polytheists and the devils together." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: "It means the polytheists do not refrain from error, nor do they see it (as error), unlike what He said about the believers: '…they remember, and then they are seeing clearly.'"

﴿And when you do not bring them a sign﴾ means: when you do not bring the polytheists a sign, ﴿they say, "Why do you not invent it?"⦆ That is: "Why do you not fabricate it and originate it from your own self and choice?" The Arabs say: *ijtabaytu al-kalām* (I invented the speech) when I fabricated it. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Mecca would ask the Prophet ﷺ for signs out of obstinacy. When they were delayed, they accused him and said, "Why do you not invent it?" That is: "Why do you not originate them and produce them from yourself?"

﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿"I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."⦆ Then He said: ﴿"These are insights"⦆ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿proofs, guidance and mercy⦆ — arguments, clarification and demonstration ﴿from your Lord⦆. Its singular is *baṣīrah*, and its root meaning is the manifestness of a thing and its firm establishment, such that a person sees it and is guided by it. He says: these are indications that lead you to the truth.

﴿And a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy⦆. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. A group held that it concerns recitation during the prayer. It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that they used to speak during the prayer about their needs, so they were commanded to be silent and to listen to the recitation of the Qur'an.[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 13/345, 349 (in which is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak); Sunan al-Bayhaqi 2/155; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 264. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr (3/636) attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Shaybah.]]

Others said: it was revealed concerning refraining from reciting audibly behind the imam.[[Numerous reports on this are found in: al-Durr al-Manthur 3/635; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 264.]]

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning raising the voices while they were behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer."[[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan 1/326, who said: in its chain is Abd Allah ibn Amir, who is weak. See also: Nasb al-Raya by al-Zayla'i 2/14; Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaqu bi'l-qira'ah khalf al-imam by Abu al-Hasanat al-Lucknawi p. 77, printed in India.]]

Al-Kalbi said: "They would raise their voices in the prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell."[[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir from al-Kalbi.]]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard some people reciting along with the imam. When he finished, he said: "Has the time not come for you to understand? ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, as Allah has commanded you.⦆"[[Narrated by al-Tabari 13/346. Al-Suyuti attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh from Ibn Mas'ud; see al-Durr al-Manthur 13/635.]] This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and al-Nakha'i: that the verse concerns recitation during the prayer.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ʿAta' and Mujahid said: the verse concerns the sermon. They were commanded to be silent for the imam's sermon on Friday.[[See: al-Tabari 13/352; al-Durr al-Manthur 3/637; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 264. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said in al-Muharrar al-Wajiz 6/196: "As for the view of those who say it was revealed concerning the sermon, it is weak, because the verse is Meccan, and the sermon was not established until after the Prophet's ﷺ migration from Mecca. Likewise what al-Zahrawi (?) mentioned, that it was revealed on account of a young man from the Ansar who was reciting in the prayer while the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in the prayer." See also: al-Qira'ah khalf al-imam by al-Bayhaqi.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: "This applies to silence on the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of Fitr, the Friday, and in what the imam recites audibly."[[Narrated by Abu al-Shaykh, as in al-Durr al-Manthur; see Imam al-Kalam by al-Lucknawi p. 81.]]

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Aziz said: "[It is obligatory] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]] to be silent for the words of every preacher."

The first view is the most preferable, namely that it concerns recitation in the prayer, because the verse is Meccan, and Friday prayer was made obligatory in Medina.[[This is the view preferred by the leader of the exegetes, al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, where he said in the Tafsir 13/352–353: "The most correct of these views is the view of the one who says: they were commanded to listen to the Qur'an in the prayer when the imam recites, and the one behind him who follows him hears it; and in the sermon. We say this is more correct because of the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'And when he recites, be silent,' and because of the consensus of all that whoever hears the Friday sermon and is obligated to attend the Friday prayer must listen to it and be silent for it, together with the continuous reports of the command to do so from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. There is no time at which anyone is obligated to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for its reciter except in these two situations, with disagreement regarding one of them: being behind an imam whom one follows. It is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we mentioned, his saying: 'When the imam recites, be silent.' So silence behind him during his recitation is obligatory for the one who follows him and hears his recitation, by the general apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." See also an excellent study on this by Abu al-Hasanat al-Lucknawi in his book "Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaqu bi'l-qira'ah khalf al-imam" pp. 75 ff., in our edition.]] They agreed that one is commanded to be silent while the imam is delivering the sermon.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' narrated to us: al-Shafi'i narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you say to your companion, 'Be silent,' while the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday, then you have engaged in idle talk (laghw)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Friday, chapter "Silence while the imam is delivering the sermon," 2/414; and Muslim in the same book and chapter, no. 851, 2/583; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 4/583.]]

The scholars differed concerning recitation behind the imam in the prayer. A group held that it is obligatory, whether the imam recites audibly or silently. This is reported from ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas and Muʿadh, and it is the view of al-Awza'i and al-Shafi'i.

Another group held that one recites in those parts in which the imam recites silently, and does not recite when he recites audibly. This is reported from Ibn ʿUmar, and it is the view of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad. Al-Zuhri, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq also held this view.

Another group held that one does not recite at all, whether the imam recites silently or audibly. This is reported from Jabir, and al-Thawri and the companions of opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y) held this view.[[See these views with their evidences in: al-Tamhid by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr 11/22–56; al-Istidhkar 2/166–193; Imam al-Kalam by al-Lucknawi, in which he gathered the views with their evidences and discussed them impartially, preferring what the evidence supports.]] Whoever does not hold recitation behind the imam relies on the apparent meaning of this verse. Whoever makes it obligatory says: the verse refers to other than the Fatihah, and when he recites the Fatihah he follows the imam's pauses and does not contend with the imam in recitation.

The evidence for this is what Abu ʿUthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Mahbubi narrated to us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us: Hannad narrated to us: ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Makhul, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi', from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the Dawn prayer, and the recitation became burdensome for him. When he finished, he said: "I see you reciting behind your imam?" We said: "Yes, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do not do so, except with Umm al-Qur'an (the Fatihah), for there is no prayer for one who does not recite it."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter "One who omits recitation in his prayer," 1/390; al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Prayer, chapter "What has been related concerning recitation behind the imam," 2/226–227, and he said: the hadith of ʿUbadah is hasan (good); al-Daraqutni 1/318, and he said: its chain is hasan. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 7, verses 202–204:**

The people of Medina read "yumiddūnahum" (with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *kasra* on the *mīm*), from *al-imdād* (extending/supplying). The others read it with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ* and a *ḍamma* on the *mīm*. Both are dialectal variants (*lughatān*) with the same meaning.

﴿Then they do not desist﴾ means they do not restrain themselves. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Neither do humans refrain from the evil deeds they commit, nor do the devils withhold from them. Accordingly, His saying 'then they do not desist' refers to the actions of both the polytheists and the devils together." Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: "It means the polytheists do not refrain from error, nor do they see it (as error), unlike what He said about the believers: '…they remember, and then they are seeing clearly.'"

﴿And when you do not bring them a sign﴾ means: when you do not bring the polytheists a sign, ﴿they say, "Why do you not invent it?"⦆ That is: "Why do you not fabricate it and originate it from your own self and choice?" The Arabs say: *ijtabaytu al-kalām* (I invented the speech) when I fabricated it. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Mecca would ask the Prophet ﷺ for signs out of obstinacy. When they were delayed, they accused him and said, "Why do you not invent it?" That is: "Why do you not originate them and produce them from yourself?"

﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿"I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."⦆ Then He said: ﴿"These are insights"⦆ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿proofs, guidance and mercy⦆ — arguments, clarification and demonstration ﴿from your Lord⦆. Its singular is *baṣīrah*, and its root meaning is the manifestness of a thing and its firm establishment, such that a person sees it and is guided by it. He says: these are indications that lead you to the truth.

﴿And a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy⦆. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. A group held that it concerns recitation during the prayer. It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that they used to speak during the prayer about their needs, so they were commanded to be silent and to listen to the recitation of the Qur'an.[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 13/345, 349 (in which is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak); Sunan al-Bayhaqi 2/155; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 264. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr (3/636) attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Shaybah.]]

Others said: it was revealed concerning refraining from reciting audibly behind the imam.[[Numerous reports on this are found in: al-Durr al-Manthur 3/635; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 264.]]

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning raising the voices while they were behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the prayer."[[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan 1/326, who said: in its chain is Abd Allah ibn Amir, who is weak. See also: Nasb al-Raya by al-Zayla'i 2/14; Imam al-Kalam fima yata'allaqu bi'l-qira'ah khalf al-imam by Abu al-Hasanat al-Lucknawi p. 77, printed in India.]]

Al-Kalbi said: "They would raise their voices in the prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell."[[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir from al-Kalbi.]]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard some people reciting along with the imam. When he finished, he said: "Has the time not come for you to understand? ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, as Allah has commanded you.⦆"[[Narrated by al-Tabari 13/346. Al-Suyuti attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh from Ibn Mas'ud; see al-Durr al-Manthur 13/635.]] This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and al-Nakha'i: that the verse concerns recitation during the prayer.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ʿAta' and Mujahid said: the verse concerns the sermon. They were commanded to be silent for the imam's sermon on Friday.[[See: al-Tabari 13/352; al-Durr al-Manthur 3/637; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 264. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said in al-Muharrar al-Wajiz 6/196: "As for the view of those who say it was revealed concerning the sermon, it is weak, because the verse is Meccan, and the sermon was not established until after the Prophet's ﷺ migration from Mecca. Likewise what al-Zahrawi (?) mentioned, that it was revealed on account of a young man from the Ansar who was reciting in the prayer while the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in the prayer." See also: al-Qira'ah khalf al-imam by al-Bayhaqi.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: "This applies to silence on the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of Fitr, the Friday, and in what the imam recites audibly."[[Narrated by Abu al-Shaykh, as in al-Durr al-Manthur; see Imam al-Kalam by al-Lucknawi p. 81.]]

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Aziz said: "[It is obligatory] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]] to be silent for the words of every preacher."

The first view is the most preferable, namely that it concerns recitation in the prayer, because the verse is Meccan, and Friday prayer was made obligatory in Medina.[[This is the view preferred by the leader of the exegetes, al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, where he said in the Tafsir 13/352–353: "The most correct of these views is the view of the one who says: they were commanded to listen to the Qur'an in the prayer when the imam recites, and the one behind him who follows him hears it; and in the sermon. There is no time at which anyone is obligated to listen to the Qur'an and be silent for its reciter except in these two situations, with disagreement regarding one of them: being behind an imam whom one follows. It is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what we mentioned, his saying: 'When the imam recites, be silent.' So silence behind him during his recitation is obligatory for the one who follows him and hears his recitation, by the general apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' narrated to us: al-Shafi'i narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you say to your companion, 'Be silent,' while the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday, then you have engaged in idle talk (laghw)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Friday, chapter "Silence while the imam is delivering the sermon," 2/414; and Muslim in the same book and chapter, no. 851, 2/583; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 4/583.]]

The scholars differed concerning recitation behind the imam in the prayer. A group held that it is obligatory, whether the imam recites audibly or silently. This is reported from ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas and Muʿadh, and it is the view of al-Awza'i and al-Shafi'i.

Another group held that one recites in those parts in which the imam recites silently, and does not recite when he recites audibly. This is reported from Ibn ʿUmar, and it is the view of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad. Al-Zuhri, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq also held this view.

This is reported from Jabir, and al-Thawri and the companions of opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y) held this view.[[See these views with their evidences in: al-Tamhid by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr 11/22–56; al-Istidhkar 2/166–193; Imam al-Kalam by al-Lucknawi, in which he gathered the views with their evidences and discussed them impartially, preferring what the evidence supports.]] Whoever does not hold recitation behind the imam relies on the apparent meaning of this verse. When he finished, he said: "I see you reciting behind your imam?" We said: "Yes, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do not do so, except with Umm al-Qur'an (the Fatihah), for there is no prayer for one who does not recite it."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter "One who omits recitation in his prayer," 1/390; al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Prayer, chapter "What has been related concerning recitation behind the imam," 2/226–227, and he said: the hadith of ʿUbadah is hasan (good); al-Daraqutni 1/318, and he said: its chain is hasan. Al-Hakim authenticated it, 1/318, and Ibn Hibban, p. 127 of Mawarid al-Zam'an; al-Bukhari narrated it in his Juz' al-Qira'ah khalf al-imam, and al-Bayhaqi also in al-Qira'ah; the author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah 3/82.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 7, verses 205–206:**

That is, you should be humble before Me and fear Me, in the silent prayer. As for His saying, ﴿and without loudness in speech﴾, He meant in the audible prayer: do not recite with excessive loudness, but in a lowered and quiet voice, such that whoever is behind you can hear. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: He commanded them to remember Him in their hearts, through humbling themselves before Him in supplication and submission, without raising the voice or shouting in supplication. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾, meaning at dawn and in the evenings. The singular of ﴿aṣāl﴾ (evenings) is ﴿aṣīl﴾, like ﴿yamīn﴾ (right) and ﴿aymān﴾ (rights). It refers to the period between the 'Asr and the Maghrib (sunset prayers).

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord﴾, meaning the angels brought near in excellence and honour, ﴿do not disdain﴾, meaning do not become arrogant, ﴿from His worship, and they glorify Him﴾, meaning they exalt Him and remember Him, saying: "Glory be to Allah."

The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so for him is Paradise; I was commanded to prostrate and I disobeyed, so for me is the Fire.'"

(488), with the wording: "Keep to frequent prostration to Allah, for you do not prostrate to Allah a single prostration except that He raises you..."]

As for His saying, ﴿and without loudness in speech﴾, He meant in the audible prayer: do not recite with excessive loudness, but in a lowered and quiet voice, such that whoever is behind you can hear. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: He commanded them to remember Him in their hearts, through humbling themselves before Him in supplication and submission, without raising the voice or shouting in supplication. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾, meaning at dawn and in the evenings. The singular of ﴿aṣāl﴾ (evenings) is ﴿aṣīl﴾, like ﴿yamīn﴾ (right) and ﴿aymān﴾ (rights). It refers to the period between the 'Asr and the Maghrib (sunset prayers).

﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord﴾, meaning the angels brought near in excellence and honour, ﴿do not disdain﴾, meaning do not become arrogant, ﴿from His worship, and they glorify Him﴾, meaning they exalt Him and remember Him, saying: "Glory be to Allah."

﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muneeb narrated to us: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam recites the prostration verse (sajdah) and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping and says: 'Woe is me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so for him is Paradise; I was commanded to prostrate and I disobeyed, so for me is the Fire.'"

[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, chapter on applying the name of disbelief to one who abandons the prayer (salah) (81): 1/87. Also by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/147.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an narrated to us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani narrated to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: al-Awza'i narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Hisham, from Ma'dan, who said: I asked Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I said: "Narrate to me a hadith by which Allah may benefit me." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No servant prostrates to Allah a single prostration except that Allah raises him by it one degree and removes from him by it one sin."

[Narrated by Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Iqamah, chapter on what has come concerning frequent prostration, no. (1423): 1/457; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/276, 280. Also narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Salah, chapter on the excellence of prostration and encouragement to it, no. (488), with the wording: "Keep to frequent prostration to Allah, for you do not prostrate to Allah a single prostration except that He raises you..."]
